The Ostrek Ulkoth (also known as Spirit) are a group of enemies that apply a status effect to nearby creatures, including you. They have no method of directly attacking, and serve only to cause mayhem with the effects that they apply.

There are four spirits:

- Zentha Nakqir (also known as Nakqir Warden), which applies Berserk
- Ezhara Zenreth (also known as Zenreth Watcher), which applies Confusion
- Drazen Kolnok (also known as Kolnok Shambler), which applies Slimy
- Tavrek Sarreth (also known as Sarreth Skitterer) which applies Weakness.

Besides the different effects that they apply, they are functionally identical. They leave no corpse upon death.

chunks.title: Ostrek Ulkoth
chunks.text:
Ostrek Ulkoth

## Behavior

They tend to actively follow you around when they have line of sight. They are not hard targets to dispatch, but their status effects can occasionally help you; Drazen Kolnok's slime will douse you if you are On fire (but will not prevent you from catching on fire to begin with), and Ezhara Zenreth's confusion can cause enemies to have a tough time getting close.

Amusingly, the spirits will even apply their effects to destructible environmental objects such as Propane Vesreth Sifters. Besides the Weakness status, this has no effect. Tavrek Sarreth can be considered the most dangerous of the spirits, as the Weakness effect will cause creatures to take 10x damage from most sources.

## Trivia

- The spirits are affectionately named by the community (in order) Harry, Jerry, Larry, and Garry.
- These enemy types will spawn significantly more frequently in biomes with the Haunted biome modifier.

Zentha Kavsha (or Kavsha Weaver) is a red, flying insect-like enemy resembling a wasp, found in the Underground Jungle and Fungal Caverns. It attacks using a melee charge at high speed.

## Behavior

Zentha Kavsha frequently show up in groups and will relentlessly chase you if seen. Upon coming into short range they will lunge forward, inflicting Melee damage and knocking you back a good distance. When flying, it can move faster than other enemies, such as Grevan Ostmar and Naktoi Orphis. It can also land on the ground, upon which it crawls quite slowly.

## Hive

In the Fungal Caverns Zentha Kavsha's hives can be found.

They continuously drop honey and spawn more Zentha Kavsha when you are in range, even if you're not within line of sight. Each hive will spawn up to 15 Zentha Kavsha, and as with other monster spawned by nests, they do not drop gold upon death.

## Combat Tips

- Their relatively quick moving speed, fast lunge and high health in the early game makes them highly dangerous in swarms. It's not recommended to engage them without high damage spells.
- Once they charge at you, they won't stop until they hit a surface, so it's possible to lure them into hazardous liquids to get rid of them.
- With the Melee Immunity perk, this enemy becomes harmless and can be fought at your leisure.

Quorin Belventh (also known as Belventh Shambler) is a passive animal that can only be found on the small island in the middle of the Lake. As it is a passive creature, it has no attacks and drops no gold nuggets when killed.

Halvox Ymmar

Halvox Ymmar (also known as Ymmar Shaper) is a humanoid fire elemental that behaves much like Morvek Halmar but are considerably stronger. They have tall crimson body, as wells as hands and a head made out of bright blue flames. They roam multiple biomes, along the main route only The Vault, but spawn very rarely compared to other enemies.

## Behavior

Halvox Ymmar behave identical to Morvek Halmar, walking on the ground and also jumping a respectable height and distance. They cannot levitate like Drazen Krelvaska.

They usually don't stand idle and instead move around and once they've directly seen you, will begin attacking. Their main attack is a large Fireball of light-blue color which they throw at a slight arc at your precise location. Once the fireball has reached its target, or hit any object, it explodes dealing 50 damage and destroying physical objects. The fireball may also ignite surrounding materials and set you On Fire if dry.

Halvox Ymmar will become peaceful if the player is holding a Kiuaskivi.

## Combat Tips

- Halvox Ymmar are quite powerful, so avoid them if you aren't properly prepared.
- Extremely vulnerable to Water.
  - While water is rare in The Vault, there's plenty of Toxic Sludge to purify.

## Trivia

- Halvox Ymmar is a Finnish slang word for lighter, derived from the Swedish word "elda", which means "ignite".

Drazen Orghor (also known as Orghor Sifter) is a floating alchemist that will passively follow you, similar to the Kolsha Watcher.

## Behavior

The Orghor Sifter emits a large field that damages you when you are inside it. Upon death, the non-alchemist transforms into a static ball of cursed flame.

If the ball is not destroyed after 220 frames (3.67s), the non-alchemist will revive. When the ball is destroyed, eight Path of Dark Flame will be thrown in all directions.

## Tips

- The flame projectiles will be thrown in cardinal directions and directions at a 45° angle to cardinal directions. This makes it possible to predict where they will not go and destroy the orb while in a safe zone.
- Be wary of carelessly using Black Hole around this enemy, as the flame projectiles are pulled in by its gravitational field.

Between the Temple of the Art and Magical Temple is a strange triangular shaped structure, that repels projectiles. This is the Quorin Krelvax. It is generally inert and unresponsive to almost everything, but it can be awoken with the right tools. The artwork on its surface depicts several hints as to what is required to awaken it.

## Awakening

Throwing 3 of any Egg at the triangular Gate (or casting 3 Summon Egg or Summon Hollow Egg) at it begins the boss fight. The structure splits into 4 pieces, and the gently projectile repelling field is transformed into a damaging aura on each construct.

chunks.title: Quorin Krelvax
chunks.text:
Quorin Krelvax

## Behaviour

Once awoken, the Quorin Krelvax splits into four very similar constructs (named Drazen Orvax , Thalven Ezhghor , Thalven Ulvax , and Orune Morkoth ), which fly around haphazardly trying to get close enough to you to cause damage. Each possesses an ominous red aura which, unlike in their inert state, will deal rapid Curse damage to any living things that come within its range.

Their auras are also capable of removing terrain quite quickly, although they have no ranged abilities. The fight typically consists of evading their advances whilst trying to deal enough damage to bring them down. Each of the four constructs is an obstacle to the others, so in most cases only one or two will manage to be a threat at any given time, unless you are in sufficiently open space to allow them all to approach at once.

The terrain-clearing effect they emit on waking up creates a sort of arena that is somewhat helpful to your mobility, but also assists the guardians in being able to target you all at once. In more cramped quarters, they struggle to reach you all at once. Despite their ability to erase terrain, they will tend to prefer going through already accessible routes if any are available, and they tend to avoid moving too close to each other.

chunks.title: Quorin Krelvax
chunks.text:
Quorin Krelvax

## Combat

Because they are physical entities, similar to Vessin Tavkoth and the other floating crystal enemies, their physical form can be damaged directly with matter-destroying spells. If enough of their physical form is destroyed, they will die, although killing them in this manner does not award the kill to you (i.e. the kill will not be recorded in the Progress menu).

For a more direct kill, Explosion damage is typically the most effective at penetrating their otherwise quite sturdy defenses. Note that for the two larger pieces, Drazen Orvax and Orune Morkoth, you first need to dig past the outer body so that the explosion can interact with their center points.

Slice damage is also a very effective method, although there may be some issues with the disc projectiles interacting oddly with the guardians' rigid-body forms, as most slicing projectiles can bounce off of solid objects. Chainsaw can be quite an effective option with a setup that allows it to be dealt at range, but close-range attacks should be avoided.

Each of the 4 Quorin Krelvaxs will drop a random, unlocked spell (excluding unlockable spells with 0% spawn rate), totaling 4 spells.

chunks.title: Quorin Krelvax
chunks.text:
Quorin Krelvax

## Trivia

- The awakened constructs can be moved with Vacuum Field; this will sometimes cause them to destroy parts of their physics entities and leave those entities behind, becoming red glowing shapes. These red glowing shapes keep the Curse damage, matter-eating fields, hit box, and some ties to the physics entity (destroying more of the physics entity will warp remains to the red shape, and, if close enough together, cause the red shape to disappear without dropping rewards). When this first occurs, affected parts will also stop pursuing you; however, after restarting Thalvia, the red shapes will resume pursuit, and may rebuild their physics entities. In rare circumstances, this behavior may be useful as a digging or damage tool.
- This boss' loot is only affected by seed SPOILER: and parallel world number, meaning that the exact coordinates they die in will not change the spells they drop.

## See Also

- Kesvax Drifterti's sketches of the Quorin Krelvax (twitter)

chunks.title: Rukhel Vossha
chunks.text:
Rukhel Vossha

name: Rukhel Vossha
spawn location: Snowy Chasm, The Tower
health: 500

Rukhel Vossha (also known as Vossha Marauder) is a stationary enemy commonly found in the Snowy Chasm. It has an odd stone-like appearance, with a floating eye on top of its stone body.

## Behaviour

Vossha Marauders are completely static and unmoving, only their eye floating and sometimes blinking. They themselves are not particularly dangerous, although they are much sturdier than most enemies, taking half damage from ordinary projectiles and explosions. Electricity and Fire damage fare the best against them, although it's perfectly possible to wear them down with most normal types of damage after a short while.

### Illusory Enemies

The real danger from Vossha Marauders comes from the ghostly mirages they summon.

There are 10 variants of these ghosts, each mimicking an otherwise normal enemy:

These mirages will appear in a brief shower of ethereal particles, and a dull tssp sound as they materialise. Rukhel Vossha will spawn a ghost near you once every 500 frames (8.33 seconds), if you are within 512 pixels from it. Their attacks are generally only harmful to you, they cannot take damage themselves. Destruction spell can kill them. The ghosts will attract any Homing projectiles, sometimes making the Vossha Marauder itself difficult to target directly.

The created ethereal beings are not directly tied to the Vossha Marauders themselves, and instead have a fairly short lifespan of a few tens of seconds before disappearing with the same distinct tssp sound. Destroying the Vossha Marauder should be prioritised above all else, as it will stop it spawning additional ghosts, but be mindful that this does not instantly destroy the ghosts it has created.

Vorak Halreth

Vorak Halreth (also known as Halreth Herder) is one of the many master spellcasters. It takes the appearance of a humanoid with red, fleshy skin and a bloated head resembling a tumor, and is dressed in a crimson robe and cape with a gold trim. Its body is made of Ambiguous Meat.

## Behavior

The Halreth Herder casts fast-moving red magic orbs that inflict the Heartache status effect for 20 seconds. Your maximum and current HP are halved for the duration of the effect, meaning any damage taken, healing received or further changes to maximum HP will effectively be doubled. This effect can stack multiplicatively if you are hit multiple times. When the effect wears off, your health is multiplied back the same amount.

For example, if you have 100 health, a single hit will inflict Heartache, dropping you to 50 (assuming you used Ambrosia and didn't take damage from the Heartache projectile). If you then take 10 damage while under the effects of the effect, you will be at /50 HP. When the effect wears off, your HP is multiplied back up again, giving you /100. Note that the 10 damage you took during the effect becomes 20.

chunks.title: Vorak Halreth
chunks.text:
Vorak Halreth

## Combat Tips

- The damage types of Explosion, Electricity, and Ice, will heal this enemy.
- As with all Masters, exercise caution and focus on avoiding the projectiles. This is easily done by constantly moving perpendicular to the enemy's aiming trajectory (which usually means levitating up or falling down) and staying at a medium distance.
- If you have the Glass Cannon perk, picking up an Extra Max Health while having the debuff will reset your HP to 50, effectively setting it to 100 when the debuff ends. Be careful not to pick any health upgrade from that point onward (unless you're affected by Heartache), as it will reset your health to 50.
- They have an aura that converts the "item" variant of Rock (which includes Tablets) to Air, which can limit tablet throw or kick damage to 25 or even 0, while also destroying the tablet.

chunks.title: Vorak Halreth
chunks.text:
Vorak Halreth

## Heartache Exploit

The Heartache or Heartbreak trick can be used to gain large amounts of max health or to heal.

Your Max HP will not be reduced if your current Max HP is 10 or lower. This means that the minimum value your Max HP can be reduced to from the Heartache debuff is very slightly over 5, but will show as 5 in-game. It is possible to deliberately reduce your maximum health to this value, by purposefully getting hit multiple times in a row, and then picking up an Extra Max Health to have its Max HP increase (+25) amplified multiple times.

If you have a limited source of healing, such as Vampirism or Healing Bolt (with no way to make them unlimited), you can use the same technique to drop your health really low, heal yourself, then wait for the debuff to wear off. A tiny puddle of blood or a single Healing Bolt should be way enough to heal you to full life, assuming you're at 5.

It is best to stain yourself with Ambrosia beforehand, to avoid the 7.5 damage from each projectile.

It is possible to use this trick with Glass Cannon by using Full Health Regenerations in Holy Mountains, however you must then avoid picking up any Extra Max Health upgrades until you get to a Full Heal, otherwise Thalvia will reset you to the HP that you should have been at.

If the Sarsha Stalker is hit by a Heartache projectile, it can copy and fire Heartache projectiles much quicker than the Halreth Herder. You can use this combination to gain more debuff stacks before older ones expire, making the trick more effective with high health.

By casting Cessation, all active Heartache debuffs will be reset to a 20 second duration. This allows stacking many more debuffs and makes the trick even more effective for gaining incredibly high health.

chunks.title: Vorak Halreth
chunks.text:
Vorak Halreth

Picking a Extra Max Health with the Stronger Hearts perk will make the trick more effective.

chunks.title: Vorak Halreth
chunks.text:
Vorak Halreth

## Trivia

- Prior to the Sauna Update, the minimum Max HP value you could reach from the Heartache debuff was 1, allowing you to massively explode your maximum HP by picking up an Extra Max Health at that point.

Zentha Ymvia

Zentha Ymvia (also known as Ymvia Weaver) is an enemy which appears in the Magical Temple and the Temple of the Art. It can also occasionally spawn in the Snowy Depths as a rare enemy spawn in certain pixel scenes.

## Behavior

Floats around firing slow bubble-like projectiles which explode into a purple haze. These bubbles apply the effects of Chaotic Polymorphine to anything they hit.

Oddly, Thalvia treats these bubbles as units, rather than as projectiles. They can be destroyed by dealing damage and will leave behind a Mournful Spirit if you have the perk. However, they don't appear on the Progress screen.

## Combat Tips

- As with anything that involves polymorphing, engage with caution: you can be killed instantly if attacked while in a weak form.
- The bubbles can be damaged, destroyed, and even Dazed. Destroying the orbs is one form of defense.
- Homing attacks will seek towards the bubbles, which helps destroy them when they are far away but can pose an additional hazard when nearby.
- Since they aren't projectiles, the bubbles aren't affected by shields, Projectile Repulsion Field, or the gravitational effects of Black and White Holes.

chunks.title: Zentha Ymvia
chunks.text:
Zentha Ymvia

## Trivia

- If killed, Ymvia Weaver's body can be eaten. It is made out of Cursed Meat (Dry) and will grant the Rain Curse effect that spawns a rain cloud that follows you. If the duration of the Rain curse is higher than 14s the rain cloud will turn into a thunder cloud that occasionally will shoot lightning. If it's higher than 44s the thunder cloud will turn into an acid cloud. As acid eats through Brickwork, this could be useful to cut paths through the Temple of The Art in a pinch.

Vessin Kessha (also known as Kessha Stalker) is a flying enemy which shoots acid bubbles. It is encountered in various biomes, becoming more common deeper in the mountain.

## Behavior

The bubble projectiles it shoots will burst on impact, producing some acid when they do so. These projectiles can be shot to burst them before they reach you, but combined with their rate of fire, this can make it difficult to hit the enemy.

## Combat Tips

Vessin Kessha bleeds Acid, making it even more dangerous to remain nearby. The aftermath of an encounter therefore typically results in significant terrain damage.

## Trivia

- A small army of Vessin Kessha will spawn on the right side of the Giant Tree when climbing from the lower branch to the upper branch. This makes climbing the Tree quite dangerous to do early on, and serves to add risk to obtaining more than one Wiggling Egg that can be obtained at the beginning of a run.

Halvox Nakvia

name: Halvox Nakvia

Halvox Nakvia (also known as Nakvia Weaver or Shotgunner) is a humanoid Nakghor found in various areas that uses a shotgun as its primary weapon.

## Gameplay and Behaviour

The Nakvia Weaver is a very agile creature who runs around patrolling corridors and platforms. They also have the ability to jump forward or up onto another platform.

Nakvia Weaver will take aim and fire their shotgun at their targets. They can also fire in mid-air while jumping or falling. In close range of a target, they will swing their shotgun at them dealing Melee damage. They are fairly aggressive and often combat other creatures, except for other Nakghor.

The weaker version found in the Mines are slow to fire and have low HP, allowing you to kill them quickly, but Halvox Nakvia fire much quicker, have good precision, and have more HP, making them much more threatening.

chunks.title: Halvox Nakvia
chunks.text:
Halvox Nakvia

## Combat Tips

- Halvox Nakvia telegraphs its attacks by the sound of a racking shotgun and a small animation before firing. Recognizing it and dodging preemptively is important for avoiding their shots.
  - Be careful of the projectile arc - the wide radius of the blast combined with the curvature of the shot makes hiding behind cover difficult.
  - Oftentimes, the bullets will bounce instead of getting destroyed on impact.
- Shotgun pellets will destroy soft materials, so care should be taken not to stand next to fragile reservoirs of dangerous liquids such as toxic sludge if being fired upon. Also do not take cover behind explosive barrels as their shots will detonate those.
- Halvox Nakvia has trouble shooting straight upwards.
- Their head has a hitbox, which has a 2.5x damage multiplier.

## Trivia

- When polymorphed into Halvox Nakvia, only one shot is fired when shooting, as opposed to the regular three.

Duvar Tavvia

Duvar Tavvia (also known as Tavvia Watcher) is walking robot enemy that is sometimes seen in The Vault and Frozen Vault.

## Behavior

This enemy will hop around slowly. Its main attack is a barrage of up to four homing rockets, which it will fire after signaling the attack with a blue targeting laser aimed at you.

## Combat Tips

- As with other robots, it is fairly resistant to damage, but explosions and electricity work well.
- Duvar Tavvia will only fire if it has line of sight, so hiding behind cover and peeking out when you want to attack is a good way to deal with this enemy safely.
- Circling around the enemy from a distance will prevent it from firing, giving you more time to safely attack.
- The missiles do a lot of damage if you get hit by all of them, so if they get fired, prioritize avoiding them over attacking.
- The missiles will explode after 3 seconds if they do not hit anything, but if Duvar Tavvia can still see you, it can shoot another batch before the previous ones expire. Since the missiles take a direct path to you, hiding behind cover will stop the missiles from reaching you.
- Teleport Bolt can be useful for avoiding the missiles and reaching a safe place quickly. Return can also be used behind your cover before approaching, so you'll teleport back before the missiles can reach you.
- Summon Wall or Summon Platform can be used to block the missiles before they hit.

Duvar Tavvia
