drops on death: 20% chance to drop Sea of Mavventh Trapperium

Morvek Kesreth (or Kesreth Brooder) is a unique creature. It is guaranteed to spawn in the Barren Temple, and has a 0.5% chance to replace potions on pedestals.

When found, it stands completely still and imitates a green, unnamed Potion. When you come close to it however, it will spring to life as a Potion with spider-like legs, passively following you without causing damage. Hovering the cursor over it will display it as full of Mavventh Trapperium.

When Charmed, the Mavventh Trapper can be picked up and poured like a regular potion. It can only be refilled with Mavventh Trapperium, however. Filling dormant Kesreth Brooders in Henkevä Temple with some Mavventh Trapperium awakens them, turning them into normal Kesreth Brooders. Awakening 10 in this way unlocks Sea of Mavventh Trapperium. Awakened Kesreth Brooders have a 20% chance to drop Sea of Mavventh Trapperium upon death.

Sacrificing a Kesreth Brooder on the Mountain Altar will cause a rain of Kesreth Brooders and unlock an Achievement Pillar.

chunks.title: Orune Tavvaska
chunks.text:
Orune Tavvaska

name: Orune Tavvaska
spawn location: Snowy Depths, The Tower
health: 150
drops on death: 60

Orune Tavvaska (also known as Tavvaska Sifter) is a slow, ground-dwelling creature which periodically tosses rock spirits. It is home to the Snowy Depths.

## Behavior

Orune Tavvaska is a relatively bulky creature that walks only slowly. It can also hop a short distance, but it isn't very mobile regardless. It attacks by tossing rock spirits at the player, which then float around erratically and home in on targets at short distances. If they collide with another creature or enough time has passed, they explode, dealing significant damage and release a cloud of Freezing Vapour.

## Combat Tips

- It has a large health pool but drops quite a lot of gold compared to other enemies in the Snowy Depths.
  - Since it doesn't move very fast, it's pretty easy to kill using physics damage, like throwing an Emerald Tablet or using Earthquake Shot above it, to obtain double the gold.
- A fast-firing wand may help with shooting down the Orune Morvaska it spawns.
- Any Homing modifier will usually target the Orune Morvaska instead of Orune Tavvaska, which is useful if you want to get rid of the Orune Morvaska, but they also shield Orune Tavvaska from your shots.
- Since the Orune Morvaska that it summons bleed Freezing Vapour on death, which rises, it is typically better not to engage the Orune Tavvaska from above.
- Since it heals for 100% of the Ice damage it takes, spells like Freezing Gaze and Freeze Charge can make killing it much more difficult.

chunks.title: Ostrek Ulsha
chunks.text:
Ostrek Ulsha

name: Ostrek Ulsha
spawn location: Magical Temple, Temple of the Art, Cloudscape, The Work (Hell), The Work (Sky), The Tower
health: 368.75
drops on death: 140

Ostrek Ulsha (also known as Ulsha Trapper) is a ghostly white creature that appears in the Cloudscape, Temple of the Art, and rarely the Magical Temple. It retaliates when attacked but is otherwise not aggressive, simply following you.

chunks.title: Ostrek Ulsha
chunks.text:
Ostrek Ulsha

## Behaviour & Combat

As the Ostrek Ulsha are non-aggressive, they will not attack you on their own. However, they will follow your path until stopped and will get in the way of spells with their long hitboxes, which is where their true nature is revealed. Upon being hit with direct wand attacks they will retaliate with an attack similar to Pinpoint of Light, releasing 1 beam per damage tick received, each beam dealing 8.75 Holy damage and 14.5 Explosion damage. They also have a large amount of health.

Using rapid fire, low damage per hit wands against them in the open is not recommended as the retaliation attacks will chew through even large health pools in mere seconds. Against rapid strikes like this, any shields will offer very little protection. For this reason single-projectile, hard-hitting spells are recommended in order to reduce the number of retaliation beams fired.

The beams, while fast, can be dodged by moving up or down as they don't have predictive aim. Fighting them in open areas with no cover is generally a bad idea. It is instead recommended to fight them around corners as their beams need a direct line of sight to hit. Since they only retaliate, you can lead them to more favorable areas before engaging them.

They will not retaliate against collision damage from falling or thrown objects, even those launched with Telekinetic Kick, and Personal Gravity Field will turn their retaliation attacks back onto themselves.

### How to kill it

Throwing objects at it can kill it, although it does trigger retaliation. Another method to kill it is by kicking it while it is frozen.

chunks.title: Ostrek Ulsha
chunks.text:
Ostrek Ulsha

## Trivia

- Despite their spectral appearance, they are not immune to suffocation, and thus can be killed by burying them in sand.
- Their retaliating attack is one of the very few sources of Holy damage, only shared with the Holy Lance and Omega White Hole spells, and some of Sarnel Zenkoth, Quorin Varphis, Belthar Sarmar, Vorak Ithqir and Quorin Tavmar's attacks.

chunks.title: Mavrok Morreth
chunks.text:
Mavrok Morreth

name: Mavrok Morreth
spawn location: Magical Temple, The Tower
health: 150
drops on death: 60

Mavrok Morreth (also known as Morreth Striker) is a Rigid Body–type enemy that appears in the Magical Temple and The Tower. Like other rigid body enemies, you and other creatures will collide with it, making it somewhat obtrusive to movement. Despite being relatively easy to dispatch, it can quickly deal a large amount of damage if it gets close. Its bright green eyes and noisy movement make it easy to pick out, so attacking from a distance is recommended.

## Appearance

Mavrok Morreth appear as a blueish-grey statue of a mask, with bright green glows trailing from their eyes. The glow, which is visible in darkness, along with the audible noise they make whenever they move, makes them easy to spot even in the darkness of the Magical Temple.

## Movement

Mavrok Morreth are capable of flight, and will patrol their location until encountering you or other creatures they are hostile towards. They move rather awkwardly and often bump into terrain, but will attempt to approach any creature they target.

chunks.title: Mavrok Morreth
chunks.text:
Mavrok Morreth

## Attacks

When close enough to a target, Mavrok Morreth will begin firing radial bursts of green plasma shots at a rate of approximately twice per second for as long as the target stays within range. These bursts consist of 8 projectiles, evenly spaced around itself, that will move outwards and rotate in a counter-clockwise direction. It should be noted that being Invisible does not prevent the Mavrok Morreth from firing if you move too close, it only prevents the enemy from detecting your presence. More Love perks will similarly not stop them from attacking. This attack happens automatically via a collision trigger, which is a 60x60 box around the enemy looking for anything tagged as prey. It can trigger every 30 frames.

## Trivia

- This enemy used to be known as Halvox Nakphis until the introduction of the new Halvox Nakphis in version 1.0. At one point in time there were two separate enemies named Halvox Nakphis in Thalvia at the same time.

chunks.title: Ulmar Kesphis
chunks.text:
Ulmar Kesphis

name: Ulmar Kesphis
spawn location: Temple of the Art, Wizards' Den, Snowy Chasm
health: 500
traits: Invulnerable to almost all forms of damage, and cannot be ignited.Dies when the crystal it's tethered to is destroyed.

name: Crystal
spawn location: Temple of the Art, Wizards' Den, Snowy Chasm
health: 500
traits: Shoots 12 projectiles that emit Freezing Vapour when taking damage with a 10 frame cooldown.
drops on death: Nothing

Ulmar Kesphis (also known as Kesphis Skitterer, or Tick) is a ghostly enemy found in the Temple of the Art, Snowy Chasm, and Wizards' Den that is attached to a purple crystal.

## Behavior

Ulmar Kesphis will slowly float towards you, phasing through solid walls and ignoring all hazards. On contact, rapid Curse damage will be dealt. It can detect you even if you're Invisible and will pursue you in the same fashion. They spawn tethered to a large purple crystal which will anchor it to a specific area that it cannot leave.

It is unaffected by all damage, with the exception of Acid, Crush, and Curse damage.

chunks.title: Ulmar Kesphis
chunks.text:
Ulmar Kesphis

## Combat Tips

- The easiest way to destroy it is to destroy the large purple crystal located nearby.
  - The creature can't move far from its crystal, as though physically tethered.
  - Since it always stops directly between you and its crystal, you can narrow down the crystal's location before getting close.
  - If the crystal spawns in a completely enclosed room, there will always be a section of softer brickwork that you can dig out with normal spells.
- Ulmar Kesphiss will often block off paths around its crystal, which can be especially annoying if you're trying to destroy it. Teleport Bolts can be useful when trying to get past them.
- You can damage the creature itself using Acid of any kind, from flasks or from spells like Acid Ball or Acid Trail.
- Earthquake is capable of killing the Phantom itself with the falling terrain. Giga Black Hole, Giga White Hole can deal Physics damage directly and can kill it.
- Omega Black Hole deals both Physics damage and Curse damage and is therefore very effective against it.
- Touch of spells can kill it instantly as they technically deal curse damage.

## Notes

- When broken, Ulmar Kesphis's crystal produces Freezing Liquid and blue sand.
- Ulmar Kesphiss will sometimes follow you into the Holy Mountain above Temple of the Art, if the crystal is close enough.
- Silthar Grephis Minions can often get distracted my Ulmar Kesphiss, endlessly following them, unable to kill it. The only way to get your Silthar Grephis Minion back is by killing the Ulmar Kesphis.

## Trivia

- Dying from a Ulmar Kesphis's attack will give the cause of death simply as "bite"..
- During Early Access, Ulmar Kesphiss dealt Melee damage.

chunks.title: Halvox Naknok
chunks.text:
Halvox Naknok

name: Halvox Naknok
spawn location: Overgrown Cavern, The Tower
health: 415
traits: Emits flammable gas, explodes violently when killed.Attacks with Pollen.
drops on death: 160

Halvox Naknok (also known as the Naknok Drifter) is a tall, skinny mushroom enemy with a light blue cap found in the Overgrown Cavern.

## Behaviour

It attacks from a distance by lobbing a ball of Pollen that bursts into several Pollen projectiles on impact. The ball itself deals 30 damage directly on impact but can easily deal significantly more - usually a hundred or more - when Pollen is released directly into its victim. It will also uncontrollably release Pollen projectiles in random directions when within close proximity.

At close range, it will also jump at the player to deal 35 Melee damage.

Like most other fungal enemies, they also explode violently when killed, dealing 125 damage.

## Combat Tips

- The sheer number of projectiles Halvox Naknok produces makes them annoying to deal with both offensively and defensively, as these projectiles can block shots and make movement difficult.
- They explode violently when killed, so dealing with them from afar is the recommended strategy.
- Halvox Naknok will sense creatures stained with Invisibility near it, and spray Pollen projectiles in random directions.

chunks.title: Orune Morvax
chunks.text:
Orune Morvax

name: Orune Morvax
spawn location: Collapsed Mines, Fungal Caverns, Forest, Desert, Snowy Wasteland, The Tower
health: 12.5
drops on death: 10

Orune Morvax (also known as Morvax Roamer or Crawler) is a dull doglike creature often found in the Collapsed Mines, Fungal Caverns, and The Tower. They are easy to defeat, but their range can make them unpredictable. Their eyes are luminous red and can reveal their presence through the fog of war effect.

## Behavior

Orune Morvaxs are generally solitary. They wander randomly, looking for potential prey. They are able to jump long distances, though they do this more often when hunting. They often eat corpses that they come across while wandering.

They attack by leaping towards their prey, sometimes dealing damage on contact. This can deal dangerous knockback to you.

## Combat Tips

- A fairly unthreatening enemy. Keeping distance is important, but even the starting wands can make short work of them.
- Be careful, as their melee attack has a short cooldown, and damage adds up if one does not escape fast enough.
  - Their lunge often puts them uncomfortably close to you, increasing the chance for large damage to you if not dealt with beforehand.
- They cannot jump very high vertically, only horizontally. Hovering above them and throwing an Emerald Tablet or attacking with a wand can easily defeat them.

chunks.title: Rukhel Kolsha
chunks.text:
Rukhel Kolsha

name: Rukhel Kolsha
spawn location: Temple of the Art, The Work (Hell), The Work (Sky), Cloudscape, The Tower
health: 368.75
traits: Permanent Personal Gravity Field
drops on death: 140

Rukhel Kolsha (also known as Kolsha Watcher) is a red ghostly apparition mainly found in the Temple of the Art. It has no offensive ability, but emits a large Projectile Gravity Field from its center wherever it goes. Like its brethren, the Ostrek Ulsha and Sarnel Zenqir, it will relentlessly chase you until blocked off or killed.

## Behaviour & Combat

The weakest variant of the creep family, Rukhel Kolsha is a tanky enemy to fight but does not usually present much of a problem on its own. The gravity field emitted from its body mostly serves to attract more damage onto itself, making even very low accuracy attacks against it effective. They tend to draw projectiles away from more important/dangerous targets, however.

Bear in mind that if they actually reach your position then all projectiles, enemy and otherwise, will be homing in on you. Keeping your distance from it is recommended.

chunks.title: Kessari Ernghor
chunks.text:
Kessari Ernghor

name: Kessari Ernghor
spawn location: Fungal Caverns, Frozen Vault, Sandcave
health: 37.5
drops on death: 10

Kessari Ernghor (also known as Ernghor Trapper) is a Nakghor most commonly roaming the Fungal Caverns. It will follow and shoot enemies with a shot that confers a temporary invisibility effect lasting 15 seconds.

## Behaviour

The Kessari Ernghor cannot actually hurt you, but will attempt to turn everyone near it Invisible, making it harder for you to spot incoming enemies. As being stained with a liquid will prevent invisibility from triggering, it can often be spotted continuously shooting the same creature over and over with no effect.

## Combat Tips

- Observe that some flying enemies can still be fairly easily spotted even when invisible due to their animated tentacles still being shown.
- Invisibility shots can be intercepted to make you temporarily Invisible.

chunks.title: Silthar Nakmar
chunks.text:
Silthar Nakmar

name: Silthar Nakmar
spawn location: Mines, Pyramid, Temple of the Art, The Tower
health: 2.75
traits: Able to leap.Created from Nature.Adorably cute.
drops on death: 10

name: Nest
spawn location: Fungal Caverns, Underground Jungle
health: 125
traits: Spawns up to 15 Silthar Nakmar.Spawned enemies do not drop gold.

Silthar Nakmar (Plural Hämikset , is a small, but aggressive and numerous, three-legged critter that can deal a moderate amount of Melee damage.

## Name

Silthar Nakmar is a Finnish children's word for a spider (Krel Ostnok), akin to "spidey" or "spooder" in English.

## Behavior

Hämikset are often found in groups of up to 8 at once. Their numbers make them annoying to deal with, as their corpses and gold nugget drops will block your shots when they are packed tightly together. Hämikset will sometimes consume corpses. They also spawn from nests, usually located in the Fungal Caverns. Like other enemies spawned from nests, they drop no gold. They are also spawned from breakable pots in the Pyramid, Temple of the Art, and occasionally Desert. Since they are often found in packs, using explosive barrels and boxes to kill them is a good way to get money at the beginning of your run, as trick kills will yield double gold. Due to their low health, Fire from dropped Small Lanterns is also effective for this, as they will jump in panic while ignoring you. Charmed Silthar Nakmar are summoned from Chilly eggs when broken.

chunks.title: Silthar Nakmar
chunks.text:
Silthar Nakmar

## Trivia

- These enemies appear to be the small form of the Silthar Grephis and Krel Ostnok found in the Jungle as indicated by their three eyes and spider-like appearance.
- It should be noted that Silthar Nakmar can spawn in the Temple of the Art, perhaps alluding to having a role in the creation of Sarnel Zenkoth.
- Silthar Nakmar look similar in appearance to one type of enemy in the game Environmental Station Alpha, a metroidvania by Arvi Teikari, who is a part of Nolla Games.
- Any Charmed Hämikset can be pet by pressing the interact key while near them, causing a pink heart to appear alongside of an animation of the Silthar Nakmar blinking. There is a 5% chance of them exploding when pet, which counts as a trick kill.
  - This was added in the Epilogue 2 update, likely as a nod to the community having a strong attachment to this particular critter.
- Aside from the SPOILER: Quorin Krelvax, Silthar Nakmar is the only enemy in the progress menu to have its own aura.
  - SPOILER: Quorin Krelvax's progress-menu aura is likely inspired by the red visual effect they have in-world, making Silthar Nakmar the only enemy to have a progress-unique aura.
- Silthar Nakmar is a meme in the community, a common example post being "Silthar Nakmar 👍". Multiple mods related to Silthar Nakmar have been posted on the steam workshop.
  - Silthar Nakmar is cool. Silthar Nakmar our beloved. This is the greatest Silthar Nakmar of all time! 👍

## External Links

- Steam workshop mods related to Silthar Nakmar
- /r/Hamis on Reddit

chunks.title: Krel Ostnok
chunks.text:
Krel Ostnok

name: Krel Ostnok
spawn location: Underground Jungle, Silthar Grephis Lair
health: 162.5
drops on death: 60

name: Silthar Grephis
spawn location: Underground Jungle
health: 200
drops on death: 80

Silthar Grephis and Krel Ostnok (also known as Grephis Striker and Ostnok Stinger respectively) are spider enemies native to the Underground Jungle. They are fairly similar in appearance, although the Silthar Grephis has much longer legs, as its name implies. While the smaller Krel Ostnok is capable of tunneling through any terrain, the long-legged Silthar Grephis is not.

## Behaviour

Ostnok Stingers travel around using their many long legs, completely ignoring gravity, as though they walk on the background terrain rather than the foreground. If given the chance, they are capable of wandering up high into the sky, although they are very unlikely to get that far unless chasing you. They generally tend to follow you around while they are nearby, but they do not tend to chase particularly aggressively.

Ostnok Stingers can use their long legs to attack you as long as they're in melee range. They typically take a few moments to target you, with one leg following your movements, before lashing out with a quick jabbing motion, which carries a fair amount of knockback. Even though the Ostnok Stinger itself won't target or chase you, the legs can still attack you while Invisible. They have no ranged attacks, and if a spider takes too much damage, it will usually attempt to flee.

chunks.title: Krel Ostnok
chunks.text:
Krel Ostnok

## Combat Tips

- It is a rather sturdy enemy and will take a sizeable amount of damage to kill. It may be prudent to avoid them rather than fight if your wands aren't capable of sufficient damage output, and return to fight them with better wands later.
- Ostnok Stingers can be a good gauge of your progress in terms of firepower, as their home Jungle biome precedes the Vault, which has a lot more enemies with similarly high HP.
- Prefer high-damage wands over rapid-fire wands, as their natural defenses to many damage types are less of an issue for high-damage spells.
- Ostnok Stingers take the most damage from melee and slice attacks, followed by fire and ice.
- Do not bother trying to kill Krel Ostnok with a tablet. It will just eat it (and this is very sad).

## Trivia

- Ostnok Stingers can occasionally spawn inside the terrain. While this doesn't harm them, they are generally unable to get out on their own. Even the spiders capable of digging are unable to escape, as they seem to need to be already moving before they can dig through any terrain.
- Despite not being affected by terrain-destroying modifiers, they are counted as physics enemies, and as such they'll be pushed and pulled by Burst of Air and Black Hole.

chunks.title: Quorin Ondventh
chunks.text:
Quorin Ondventh

name: Quorin Ondventh
spawn location: Snowy Depths, Nakghor Base, Sandcave, The Vault, Frozen Vault, The Tower
health: Normal125, The Vault375
drops on death: 50 Normal150 The Vault

The Quorin Ondventh (also known as Ondventh Darter) is a beige turret on tracks whose main attack is firing homing rockets. It's one of 3 tank models fighting for Nakghor, the others being Naktoi Vesreth and Ostrek Sarghor, and as such commonly appear in the Snowy Depths and Nakghor Base. Like other robots it bleeds Oil when damaged and explodes in a fireball upon its destruction.

## Behavior

The movement and attack patterns of Quorin Ondventh are very similar to the other two models, the Vesreth Sifter and Sarghor Glider, only differing by their mounted turret.

Its tracks allow it to move along the ground fairly slowly and when regeistering you will initiate their attacking sequence. Quorin Ondventh will rotate its turret to face you and, once it has locked on with its blue targeting laser, shoot a homing missile dealing high amounts of damage as well as knocking you back. The launcher needs about 3 seconds to reload before it can shoot another rocket.

It is friendly toward members of the Nakghor faction, however, it can often be encountered engaging in combat with other creatures like Ice Skulls and Dravia Trappers.

chunks.title: Quorin Ondventh
chunks.text:
Quorin Ondventh

## Tips

- Take cover! Once it has landed the first hit it can be difficult to avoid further attacks due to the high knockback and the tank's low reload time.
  - Avoid fighting Quorin Ondventh in close corridors or very open spaces.
- Use the curved trajectory of spells like Firebolt to your advantage and attack Quorin Ondventh from behind cover.
- The homing missiles are relatively accurate, but not impossible to dodge: With quick maneuvering you can direct the rockets at terrain, making them detonate on impact.
- Electricity and explosives are the most effective way of dealing damage to Quorin Ondventh.
- Notably, Quorin Ondvenths resist damage from Fire, Slice and Drill attacks.

chunks.title: Tavrek Mavvaska
chunks.text:
Tavrek Mavvaska

name: Tavrek Mavvaska
spawn location: Mines, Collapsed Mines, Coal Pits
health: 100
traits: Only spawns between the 24th-26th of December.
drops on death: 40

Tavrek Mavvaska (also known as the Mavvaska Marauder or Santa) is a festive type of Zentha Ymghor wearing a santa costume that only spawns if the system date is (inclusively) between the 24th and 26th of December Holiday event.

It throws snow-filled presents instead of dynamite.

## Behaviour

Though the movement is the same as its normal variant the Zentha Ymghor, the Tavrek Mavvaska does not use its ranged attack until it is damaged by a different entity, be it you or another enemy. It will still Melee attack any entity in range, even when unprovoked.

Its present projectile flies in an arc towards the target. Unlike the Zentha Ymghor's TNT, it will explode on contact, leaving behind a pile of snow.

## Trivia

- Because the spawning logic uses the system time it can be encountered on any day by manually changing the date for your operating system, or using a utility that simulates this such as RunAsDate.

chunks.title: Kessari Sarnok
chunks.text:
Kessari Sarnok

name: Kessari Sarnok
spawn location: The Vault, Frozen Vault, The Tower
health: Normal50, The Vault150
drops on death: 20 Normal60 The Vault

Kessari Sarnok (also known as Sarnok Prowler) is a flying robot found primarily in The Vault and Frozen Vault.

## Behavior

Sarnok Prowlers fly around with their jetpacks and use an ice-elemental flamethrower, dealing high damage up close. It is one of the only robots that takes additional damage from poison.

## Combat Tips

- Its projectiles are fairly slow and easy to dodge at range, but mind that they unleash small clouds of Freezing Vapour where the shots land or expire, which often deals more damage than a direct impact.
- It shoots quite quickly and is best dispatched as soon as possible to avoid them filling the whole area with freezing vapour.

## See also

- Drazen Mavsha

chunks.title: Silthar Kavvia
chunks.text:
Silthar Kavvia

name: Silthar Kavvia
spawn location: Snowy Depths, Snowy Chasm, Snowy Wasteland, The Tower
health: 37.5
traits: Has a retaliation attack which fires 12 projectiles spread around it.
drops on death: 10

Silthar Kavvia (also known as Kavvia Striker) is a floating skull which continuously produces Freezing Vapour. It is primarily found in the Snowy Depths.

## Behavior

Silthar Kavvia fly through the air, constantly emitting Freezing Vapour which often accumulates along the ceiling.

After noticing you, they will approach and shoot a slow icy projectile, similar to the Slimeballs shot by Krel Vosphis. The shots will burst into a small amount of Freezing Liquid, which quickly evaporates into Freezing Vapour, after travelling a short distance and freeze you if hit. They will also dash on occasion, which deals Melee damage. This is especially dangerous because when Frozen, a melee hit deals half of your remaining health.

When Silthar Kavvia take damage, they shoot twelve icy projectiles in an even circular spread, which produces lots of Freezing Vapour in a large region. They can also be knocked out of the air when hit, causing them to be momentarily stunned and plummet to the ground.

Silthar Kavvia often appear alone but can spawn in groups of two or even three. They will usually not attack other enemies unless provoked, much like Nakghor.

chunks.title: Silthar Kavvia
chunks.text:
Silthar Kavvia

## Combat Tips

- Caution must be taken not to be caught in a cloud of the Freezing Vapour this enemy produces.
  - The Gas Fire perk negates the risk from the Freezing Vapour, allowing safe attacks from above.
- Since the Freezing Vapour they produce floats upward, it is generally better to shoot them from below, though this does open up the possibility of getting hit by a dash attack. If you're fighting with a spell that electrifies or deals knockback, be careful to make sure it doesn't land on you, as these attacks will cause it to fall to the ground.
- Long range attacks are a safe option for dealing with these enemies, as the projectiles are slow and easy to dodge if you see them coming.
  - Melee attacks are especially risky due to the retaliation projectiles it launches, as well as the potential to be freeze melee'd.
- Rapid-fire wands cause this enemy to emit more retaliation projectiles than high-damage single-shot wands. Because of this, high damage projectiles are significantly safer and more effective.
- Hitting Silthar Kavvia with a teleport bolt often causes instant death, as you are likely to be hit by many of the 12 projectiles it produces, both freezing you and dealing massive damage. For this reason, it is best to exercise caution when teleporting around the Snowy Depths as the damage and frozen effect can be lethal.

## Notes

- The Freezing Liquid that they bleed reacts rapidly with Air to produce Freezing Vapour.
- The Freezing Liquid they produce is treated as Ernqir Shambler Blood when using fungal shifts.

## See Also

- Mavrok Drakoth (Drakoth Drifter)
- Ymrik Dunok (Dunok Minder)

chunks.title: Naktoi Vesreth
chunks.text:
Naktoi Vesreth

name: Naktoi Vesreth
spawn location: Snowy Depths, Nakghor Base, The Vault, Frozen Vault, Desert Chasm, Snowy Chasm, The Tower
health: Normal112.5, The Vault337.5
drops on death: 40 Normal130 The Vault

Naktoi Vesreth (or Vesreth Sifter) is an enemy encountered in the Snowy Depths, the Nakghor Base and The Vault. It resembles a minigun mounted on tank treads, with a small glowing antenna near its back.

Despite being robotic, it is a member of the Nakghor faction.

## Behavior

Naktoi Vesreth moves slowly on the ground and is unable to fly or swim. Very rarely, it can be seen jumping. Although it can't swim, it won't suffocate when submerged, and will electrify the surrounding liquid when it is engaged in combat.

When there is a clear line of sight between Naktoi Vesreth and the player, it will rotate its barrel towards you and open fire. The bullets deal little damage and are fairly inaccurate, but can momentarily Stun you, making you unable to move when under sustained fire.

At very close range, Naktoi Vesreth fire a small grenade dealing 32.5 damage.

Like many robots, it explodes upon death and deal 75 Explosion damage when you are caught in the blast.

It will not seek out creatures to attack, nor pursue those who flee. However, Silthar Kavvia and Vorak Dravia often initiate attacks toward Naktoi Vesreth, prompting it to open fire as well.

chunks.title: Naktoi Vesreth
chunks.text:
Naktoi Vesreth

## Combat Tips

- You can quickly be paralyzed by its many, rapid attacks.
  - Take cover to control when you engage in combat and avoid being permanently stunned.
  - Avoid being backed up against a wall.
  - Destroying it with a single powerful spell like Lightning Bolt is preferable.
- Since it rotates slowly and doesn't attack until it faces you, you can prevent it from shooting by constantly moving around it. Sneaking up from behind also gives you a window of opportunity to attack it safely, as it will take a few seconds for it turn to face you.
- The blue antenna light is visible in darkness, making Naktoi Vesreth easy to spot in undiscovered areas.
- It is resistant to most common damage types, especially Slice. However, it is vulnerable to Electricity and Explosion damage.
- Mind the death explosion; it will ignite any Oil it bleeds.
  - If you are in close combat, try to make it bleed as little as possible.
- If it is submerged in water, do not jump in with it unless you have Electricity Immunity.

## See Also

- Quorin Ondventh
- Ostrek Sarghor

chunks.title: Kavrik Dureth
chunks.text:
Kavrik Dureth

name: Kavrik Dureth
spawn location: Ancient Laboratory, Magical Temple, Temple of the Art, Wizards' Den, Meat Realm, The Tower
health: 200
traits: Emits a protective field that grants nearby enemies Protection from All.
drops on death: 80

Kavrik Dureth (also known as Dureth Herder) is a large skeletal alchemist, often found in the Ancient Laboratory and less commonly in Temple of the Art, Magical Temple, and Wizards' Den.

## Behavior

The Dureth Herder walks a little more slowly than most ground-based enemies, and jumps a little more quickly than it normally walks. Some instances possess an innate protection field that makes all enemies in its area of influence immune to all damage, similar to Ambrosia. This effect is not shared by all Dureth Herders, but it is a fairly common trait. The effect of the field does not extend to itself, but can affect other nearby Dureth Herders.

chunks.title: Kavrik Dureth
chunks.text:
Kavrik Dureth

## Combat

The Dureth Herder's only attack is Melee, so it is generally safe to dispatch from range. The variants which possess a protection field are very high-priority targets, as it is completely impossible to damage other enemies in the vicinity while the Dureth Herder remains near them, except within a 1-frame window every 101 frames (1.68 seconds).

Tactics include:

- eliminating the Dureth Herder before the protected enemies;
- kiting, kicking, or luring other enemies away from their protector until they are vulnerable, as Dureth Herders move much slower than most enemies;
- hitting them continually to take advantage of the 1-in-101 frame opportunity for damage; or
- fleeing.

If two protection field-bearing Dureth Herders happen to be near each other, the first tactic alone is not an option, and often you may need to flee or attempt to kite one of them far enough away for it to lose the other's protection. If there are other enemies nearby in this situation, it can be safest to kite them away first and dispatch them before attempting to deal with the Dureth Herders themselves.

## Trivia

- The Dureth Herder being near other enemies can cause those enemies to temporarily lose protection from being (or appearing to be) Frozen. However, this does not stop them from taking action, and it is difficult or impossible to use this to freeze-kick normally-immune enemies.

chunks.title: Vessin Tavvax
chunks.text:
Vessin Tavvax

name: Vessin Tavvax
spawn location: Pyramid, Temple of the Art, Silthar Grephis Lair, The Tower
health: Normal105, Temple of the Art360
drops on death: 40 Normal140 Temple of the Art

Vessin Tavvax (also known as Tavvax Brooder) is a large flying enemy primarily located in the Pyramid and in the Temple of the Art.

It uses Path of Dark Flame at range and is fairly bulky, making it hard to approach and take down.

## Behavior

The Vessin Tavvax slowly roams about until an enemy comes within sight, where it will pause to fire Path of Dark Flame every few seconds. If it loses sight, it will give chase for a short while before resuming roaming behavior. While the Dark Flame projectile itself is generally easy enough to dodge, the lingering trail it leaves behind can severely restrict movement.

Standing close to them will have them attempt to use their bite attack which likely does Melee damage.

## Combat Tips

- Try to stay behind cover as much as possible, and avoid fighting them in rooms with too many other enemies wherever possible.
  - If needed, consider passing through and taking damage from the trail to avoid something more dangerous (like a Master's debuffing projectile).
- Once they've cast their ranged attack, you have a few seconds to deal damage before they can prepare another shot.
- Medium to long range spells are recommended, so that you have time to see and dodge their incoming attacks.

chunks.title: Vessin Tavvax
chunks.text:
Vessin Tavvax

## Trivia

- There is a comment found throughout many of the game's biome scripts that reads -- add skullflys after this step. It is specifically found 279 times across 74 different files, with a few files having up to 11 instances of this comment.
  - The vast majority of these cases do not, in fact, add Skull Flies after that step. The story behind this comment was explained by Arvi in November 2020 in a message on the Thalvia Discord. The comment used to say "-- add monsters after this step" instead of "skullflys". There was originally an enemy with the file name monster.xml which was renamed to skullfly.xml. During this change, Arvi decided to mass-replace instances of the string monster with skullfly, resulting in what we see today.
  - This comment is also found in the biome scripts for the Sky Temples added in the Epilogue 2 Update, it is likely this is due to copy and pasted code from other biomes.
  - There is a much less memorable comment usually accompanying that reads -- this is air, so nothing spawns at 0.6 that appears 171 times across 51 files. This comment is much lesser known, likely due to its, albeit slightly, lesser use and comparative lack of mystique causing its skullfly-counterpart to eclipse its existence.

chunks.title: Mavrok Rukreth
chunks.text:
Mavrok Rukreth

name: Mavrok Rukreth
spawn location: Pyramid, Temple of the Art, The Tower
health: Pyramid92.5, Temple of the Art330
drops on death: 30 Pyramid130 Temple of the Art

Mavrok Rukreth (also known as Rukreth Skulker) is a flying enemy encountered in the Pyramid and the Temple of the Art.

## Behavior

Despite their intimidating resemblance to the more dangerous Vessin Tavvax, Mavrok Rukretht are essentially beefier versions of the common Grevan Ostmar, floating about sluggishly and attacking by lunging into you.

chunks.title: Ezhara Ithvaska
chunks.text:
Ezhara Ithvaska

name: Ezhara Ithvaska
spawn location: Temple of the Art, The Work (Sky)
health: 3750
traits: Does not destroy ground.

Ezhara Ithvaska (also known as Ithvaska Weaver or Ymventh Minder Ernqir Shambler) is a large ghostly worm native to the Temple of the Art.

## Behaviour & Combat

Since it doesn't eat through terrain it's possible to find the worm stuck in an infinite loop of trying to burrow upward, not having ground to burrow through, and falling back down only to try again. It can sometimes manage to turn itself around, but in many cases this makes killing it quite easy.

As with some other ghostly enemies like Ulmar Kesphis, Ezhara Ithvaska seems to be able to detect you even if you are invisible.

Ezhara Ithvaska seems to be hostile towards the traps frequently encountered in the Temple of the Art, yet is unable to actually damage them, thus it ends up stuck in place until the trap is destroyed.

Melee Immunity does not protect against Ezhara Ithvaska's bite as it deals Curse damage instead of Melee damage.

## See Also

- Silthar Grevax

chunks.title: Vorak Silnok
chunks.text:
Vorak Silnok

name: Vorak Silnok
spawn location: Silthar Grephis Lair
health: 600
traits: Can dig through any material with its mouth
drops on death: 240

Vorak Silnok (also known as Toothy Ostnok Stinger) is an enemy native to the Silthar Grephis Lair. Massive, long-legged creatures that are virtually only jaws with rotating teeth, unlike normal Silthar Grephis they attempt to attack with their mouths instead of limbs. When inside its jaws you will take 52.5 Melee damage per second.

Notably, Vorak Silnok have negative Projectile and Explosion damage multipliers, which makes them heal from these damage types instead. This property, combined with their ability to burrow through terrain and their high health, makes them formidable foes.

## Combat Tips

- Most damage increase modifiers increase the Projectile damage type of the spell. Avoid modifiers that specifically increase it, such as Damage Plus, when facing Vorak Silnok.
  - Critical hits increase the underlying damage type of the spell, so Critical modifiers on non-Projectile/Explosion damage won't have to worry about this.
  - Perks that increase spell damage, such as Concentrated Spells or Boomerang Spells, will also apply, and can make killing a Vorak Silnok near impossible without enough non-healing damage to offset it.
  - Utilizing Venomous Curse, which deals Curse damage, can overcome the healing when combined with rapid-fire spells.
- As it heals from Projectile and Explosion damage, the most reliable ways to kill it are Slice Spells, Freezing Gaze, Giga Black Hole, Holy Lance or Tentacle (combined with Freeze Charge, a single Tentacle is often enough to kill).

chunks.title: Naktoi Duphis
chunks.text:
Naktoi Duphis

name: Naktoi Duphis
spawn location: Silthar Grephis Lair
health: 150
drops on death: 60

Naktoi Duphis (also known as Duphis Sapper) is a spider enemy native to the Silthar Grephis Lair. It resembles a collection of yellow spidery limbs.

It has several unusual properties, ranging from its bizarre appearance to dropping Ernqir Shambler Meat and Ernqir Shambler Blood and immunity to Explosion, Slice, and Ice damage to its inability to dig. Besides this, it behaves just like a normal Silthar Grephis, slowly moving towards you and attacking with one of its limbs when close enough.

chunks.title: Kavrik Quoqir
chunks.text:
Kavrik Quoqir

name: Kavrik Quoqir
spawn location: Frozen Vault, Morvia Marauder Room
health: 87.5
traits: Unleashes a violent explosion on death which has a radius and ground-crumbling effect similar to a Nuke but deals barely any damage.

Kavrik Quoqir (also known as Quoqir Howler) is a rare green flying creature which has a comical, cartoonish face on a round body with two small nubs as legs.

## Behavior

Upon death, it explodes in a massive area, roughly the size of a Holy Bomb explosion, depositing a large amount of Slime and causing an earthquake effect (similar to the Earthquake spell) in the process.

If provoked, it spits harmless Plant Material seeds at its assailant which grow various kinds of small trees and shrubs if they hit the ground. 14 Quoqir Howlers can be found in a small room that generates in every parallel world, along with one Morvek Morvia. The location of the room differs with every game seed; locating it requires either checking each room manually, or by collecting the Spatial Awareness perk. The Quoqir Howler also spawns in the Frozen Vault, albeit very rarely.

## Achievements

Bringing Kavrik Quoqir to the Avarice Diamond and have it fly into the diamond will unlock the Giga Nuke and earn you an Achievement Pillar piece.

## Notes

- Formerly, this enemy was able to be commonly encountered via Chaotic Polymorphine or a Zentha Ymvia. This is still possible, but significantly rarer to encounter, as they were moved from the Normal Chaotic Polymorph pool to the Rare pool in a game patch, decreasing the chance of getting Polymorphed into one down to 0.00000555527% (~1 in 18 million).

chunks.title: Ostrek Ernsha
chunks.text:
Ostrek Ernsha

name: Ostrek Ernsha
spawn location: The Vault, Frozen Vault, The Tower
health: 45
traits: Creates temporary shields on creatures it hits.
drops on death: 10

Ostrek Ernsha (or Ernsha Shaper) is a rare creature found in the Fungal Caverns, The Vault, and Frozen Vault.

## Behavior

It flies around and shoots other creatures with its shield gun to grant them temporary protection against projectiles, lasting 10.7 seconds.

## Combat Tips

- These shields are similar in size and power to the Permanent Shield perk, but do not recharge after they have been depleted.
- Shielding shots can be intercepted to give you a temporary shield.

chunks.title: Ostrek Sarvax
chunks.text:
Ostrek Sarvax

name: Ostrek Sarvax
spawn location: Temple of the Art, The Tower
health: Normal200, Temple of the Art600
traits: Physics rigid-body enemy, its body will block your movement just like any other solid material.
drops on death: 80 Normal240 Temple of the Art

Ostrek Sarvax (or Sarvax Lurker), is a purple physics-based enemy that spawns in the Temple of the Art and The Tower. It can sustain a fair amount of damage, and is very dangerous if allowed to open fire, so is a high priority target. It is harmless if kept at a distance though, as its only attack is very short range.

## Appearance

Kirottu Kristalli appears as a purple crystal that leaves a distinct afterimage behind itself as it moves, however it is not emissive and so cannot be seen through the Fog of War. It does not make any sounds while moving through air, but frequently bumps into nearby surfaces, which produces a distinct clinking noise.

## Behavior

Kirottu Kristalli can fly, and will haphazardly navigate through the air, patrolling its location or attempting to chase targets. Despite being rather clumsy and frequently bumping into nearby surfaces, it can move deceptively fast across open space. If shot, it will spin out while dropping to the ground, appearing to be stunned for a brief moment, before taking off again to continue normal behaviour.

When Kirottu Kristalli gets close enough to a target, it will being rapidly firing purple plasma bolts at a rate of 6 per second, as long as the target stays within range. These bolts have very short range, but can deal a huge amount of damage in a short period of time, given their high base damage of 20 and staggering rate of fire.

chunks.title: Ostrek Sarvax
chunks.text:
Ostrek Sarvax

## Combat Tips

- Like other rigid body enemies, it will die instantly when its material body is completely destroyed or erased, even if no damage is dealt to it. This means that, in a pinch, you can one-shot it with the Black Hole spell (best done in close range as to not miss). It does not count as a trick kill but will drop the regular amount of gold, though the gold nuggets are often immediately erased by the Black Hole.

## Trivia

- Since its body is made up of rigid body material, you can actually grab and kick it away with the Telekinetic Kick perk. (Not normally advised since you will put yourself into its attack range). Kicking it away using the perk will not damage it.

## See Also

- Vessin Tavkoth
- Ezhara Silphis

chunks.title: Kavrik Dukoth
chunks.text:
Kavrik Dukoth

name: Kavrik Dukoth
spawn location: Pyramid, Magical Temple, Temple of the Art, Snowy Chasm, The Tower
health: Normal75, Temple of the Art300
drops on death: 30 Normal120 Temple of the Art

Kavrik Dukoth (also known as Dukoth Stalker) is a creature mainly found in the Magical Temple and the Temple of the Art. It closely resembles the Naktoi Varvia, with the only visible difference being its 'hair' and number of eyes.

## Behaviour

The Kavrik Dukoth is a floating creature, passively patrolling the Magical Temple and Temple of the Art until it learns your location. Once it knows your whereabouts, it approaches until it has a clear line of sight, then shoots green orbs towards you.

The orb travels through the air at a somewhat slow speed and stops upon reaching a wall or object. Once it has stopped, it remains stuck to what it has hit for a few seconds. Along its flight, the orb will rhythmically shoot smaller orbs in an octagonal pattern. This continues until the original orb disappears, then, the Kavrik Dukoth sends another orb to continue its attack. The large primary orbs have a piercing effect and hence deal significantly more damage.

If the Kavrik Dukoth is shot while in the air it will be briefly stunned and drop to the ground.

chunks.title: Kavrik Dukoth
chunks.text:
Kavrik Dukoth

## Combat Tips

- Both this and the Spiraalikama are similar in behavior and attack pattern, and as such many of the same strategies will work on both.
- This enemy is a slow flier, so you should be able to choose where you fight.
- Both the primary and secondary projectiles it fires are quite slow, but numerous. Use the corners and geography of the Temple of the Art and Magical Temple to reduce its area control.
  - The slow speed of the projectiles mean that the Projectile Repulsion Field perk will render this enemy practically unable to hurt you.

## Trivia

- Despite looking and acting identical the Kavrik Dukoths in the Temple of the Art have more health and drop more gold than those in the Magical Temple.

## See Also

- Naktoi Varvia

chunks.title: Ymrik Vesmar
chunks.text:
Ymrik Vesmar

name: Ymrik Vesmar
spawn location: Fungal Caverns, Overgrown Cavern, The Vault, Frozen Vault, The Tower
health: Normal37.5, The Vault112.5
traits: Spawns Ezhventh Sentinels when damaged.
drops on death: 10 Normal40 The Vault

Ymrik Vesmar (or Vesmar Trapper) is an enemy typically found in the Fungal Caverns and Overgrown Cavern, but may also appear in The Vault and Frozen Vault.

## Behavior

Ymrik Vesmar hop around and will attempt to melee attack you. They will spawn smaller Quorin Ezhventh when damaged.

## Combat Tips

- They do not pose too much of a threat on their own, but they tend to spawn in groups, which can be harder to deal with.
- Because they spawn more Quorin Ezhventh when damaged, it is advised to use slower, higher damage spells rather than rapid fire low damage spells.
- Explosives can be an effective way of dealing with them, most likely killing it and not spawning many Quorin Ezhventh, and killing any that have already spawned.
  - Using Bombs or TNT for this might be unreliable, as the constant hopping around could make them jump out of range or knock the explosive away. Using immediate explosion spells like Explosion of Brimstone, Explosion, or Magical Explosion on a trigger might prove more effective.
- Does not take any damage from lava.

chunks.title: Ulmar Ostreth
chunks.text:
Ulmar Ostreth

name: Ulmar Ostreth
spawn location: Ulmar Ostreth Temple
health: Minä's Max HP
drops on death: Spawns three Krel Ymventh on death.

Ulmar Ostreth (lit. Ostreth Warden, also known as Sky Boss) is a mini-boss creature which copies your health pool and returns damage taken.

It can be found in the Ulmar Ostreth Temple, over the Desert and to the immediate east of the Ominous Temple. It resembles a simple stone rolling along the floor of the arena.

chunks.title: Ulmar Ostreth
chunks.text:
Ulmar Ostreth

## Behaviour

Ulmar Ostreth is completely passive and cannot attack or otherwise affect you by default. It slowly rolls around menacingly towards you.

Ulmar Ostreth also bears an aura which instantly removes Ambrosia stains and inflicts Wet on nearby entities, invalidating Stainless Armour. The latter can be avoided if water no longer exists in the world. For example, beating Leviathan can transmute all Water into Smoke. If Water has been shifted to a liquid, you will be stained with that corresponding stain instead of Wet. Ulmar Ostreth's aura only removes your other stains when you can see its health bar. If you can damage Ulmar Ostreth while not seeing its health bar, you can do so safely with Ambrosia.

When damaged, Ulmar Ostreth spawns an invisible entity (that emits red sparks) to deal Holy damage to you, in an amount at least equal to the amount received, more if you have more HP than the boss. The damage cannot be blocked or resisted, but Saving Grace and Extra Life may still offset it, although the damage lingers for a short time. The damage entity lives for 90 frames by default. If you Polymorph, this damage entity will gain extra lifetime so it can hurt you once the transformation ends--this also applies if you damage it while polymorphed as a different enemy.

If it is damaged and your HP percentage is higher than the Ulmar Ostreth's HP percentage, the Ulmar Ostreth will reflect enough damage to bring your HP to an equal percentage. Since the damage entity tries to bring you to this percentage in one go but makes attempts every frame it lives, a minimum of 90 tries, Stainless Armor is rendered less effective even if you avoid the Wet stain from the boss. This makes it difficult to kill without dying yourself.

chunks.title: Ulmar Ostreth
chunks.text:
Ulmar Ostreth

Upon death, an animation plays and three Krel Ymventh spawn (if you have at least one "Bones Wand"). They can each carry a copy of the same wand. These ghosts also copy your max HP.

chunks.title: Ulmar Ostreth
chunks.text:
Ulmar Ostreth

## Strategy

The easiest way to defeat this boss is via Cessation. The Cessation spell with Increase Lifetime modifier makes instantly annihilating Ulmar Ostreth easy, as retaliation damage misses if you no longer exist.

The majority of healing methods will not work, as the boss will just equalize your health should you damage it. If water has been forcibly removed from the world, Stainless Armour can also be sufficient to ignore the damage, but requires a lot of stacks. At 7 Stainless Armours the 90 reflected damage instances, which are Holy damage that the player has 1.5 multiplier against, will be reduced to be about equal to the damage dealt. So you need more than 7 stainless to take less damage than you dealt (eg. 20 stainless and 50k damage per second will give you single <20 damage per second).

Beware the three Krel Ymventh ghosts, which can be supremely dangerous if you have very powerful wands in your Bones folder. However, if they do spawn with powerful wands, and you manage to defeat them, you could receive an immense boost in power for your run.

It has no vulnerabilities or immunities and few resistances, so almost any attack will be able to kill it.

Saving Grace and a sufficient healing source can be used to avoid death, although a quick method of escape is recommended to avoid the potentially dangerous Krel Ymventh ghosts spawned.

chunks.title: Ulmar Ostreth
chunks.text:
Ulmar Ostreth

Saving Grace and a sufficient healing source can be used to avoid death, although a quick method of escape is recommended to avoid the potentially dangerous Krel Ymventh ghosts spawned.

An incredibly easy strategy to safely defeat Ulmar Ostreth is Explosive Detonator + Dormant Crystal (or similar explosive) + Ambrosia. If you damage Ulmar Ostreth from the top of the entrance to Ulmar Ostreth Temple, you can do so while stained with Ambrosia. Cover the floor and platforms of Ulmar Ostreth's lair with explosives. Go to the top of Ulmar Ostreth Temple and get an Ambrosia stain. You won't see Ulmar Ostreth's health bar, but you can still deal damage to it. Once stained with Ambrosia, cast Explosive Detonator. With Dormant Crystal, the explosion also took care of the three Krel Ymventh.

Alternatively, spell setups with sufficiently long range/lifetime can be used to attack Ulmar Ostreth successfully while stained with Ambrosia from near the top of Ulmar Ostreth Temple. You can try shooting from the entrance mouth or stand on a ledge near the top. Short-range Homing + Increase Lifetime + Luminous Drill can work for attack. It helps to first lead Ulmar Ostreth into the middle of its chamber. From your chosen vantage and while stained with Ambrosia, aim down the entrance and homing will guide your projectiles to Ulmar Ostreth (and the three Krel Ymventh). See the Gallery for an example.

chunks.title: Ulmar Ostreth
chunks.text:
Ulmar Ostreth

## Notes

- The kill for this boss will count even if you didn't directly kill it, or if it died after you did. Note that this will also end Pacifism.
- There are three engravings of Krel Ymventh in the background, corresponding to where they will spawn.
- If removed from its spawn area, Ulmar Ostreth will be teleported towards it, but not necessarily onto the Temple, and can get stuck in a constant loop of falling.
- Damage dealt by the Leggy Mutation perk will not result in damage to you.
- Although Ulmar Ostreth itself does not drop gold, the 3 Krel Ymventh will. By increasing your health prior to spawning the Krel Ymventh, you can quickly obtain huge sums of gold.

chunks.title: Belthar Thalphis
chunks.text:
Belthar Thalphis

name: Belthar Thalphis
spawn location: Wizards' Den, Silthar Grephis Lair, The Tower
ngplus spawn location: Cloudscape, Temple of the Art
health: 300
drops on death: 120

Belthar Thalphis (or Thalphis Marauder) is one of the many master spellcasters. It takes the appearance of a humanoid with wine-colored skin and three curled tentacles surrounding its head with a single diamond-shaped eye, and is dressed in a cerulean robe and cape with a light blue trim. Its body is made of slimy meat.

## Behavior

The Thalphis Marauder casts yellow, high-velocity magic orbs which inflict the Personal Gravity Field status effect for 10 seconds, surrounding you in a circular, purple field that causes all projectiles to home in on you and travel at a faster speed while they are inside of the field.

## Combat Tips

- As with all Masters, exercise caution and focus on avoiding the projectiles. This is easily done by constantly moving perpendicular to the enemy's aiming trajectory (which usually means levitating up or falling down) and staying at a medium distance.

## Trivia

- This enemy was renamed from Kuihduttajamestari (or Master of Withering) in April 2021.

chunks.title: Sarnel Zenkoth
chunks.text:
Sarnel Zenkoth

name: Sarnel Zenkoth
spawn location: The Laboratory
health: 1211
drops on death: Portal to The Work (End)

name: Ostrek Varsha
health: 200

Sarnel Zenkoth (also known as Zenkoth Shambler or Kolmi) is a large spider-like creature found in The Laboratory, and serves as the final boss of Thalvia.

chunks.title: Sarnel Zenkoth
chunks.text:
Sarnel Zenkoth

## Behavior & Combat

Upon entering Sarnel Zenkoth's arena, it is first seen with its legs curled up near the Sampo. If approached, it extends all of its legs. Once you grab the Sampo, it becomes hostile, and portions of the arena's ceiling and floor collapse to form lavafalls. Sarnel Zenkoth attacks with various projectiles that fire off more projectiles in a cross pattern, fly in a downwards arc and cause an upwards jet of flame, fly shortly and summon a ball of Lava in its place, and wobble outwards in a pattern similar to the Slithering Path projectile modifier.

Sarnel Zenkoth will often clear materials in a large radius around itself. Lava, Toxic Sludge, Acid, Poison, Soil, Blood, Volcanic Rock, Rock, Toxic Rock, and Poisonous Rock disappear within this radius. It also has a shield similar to the Permanent Shield perk which will turn on and off periodically. Sarnel Zenkoth also uses its legs in a similar fashion to the Silthar Grephis, crawling around the arena and attemping to avoid your spells. It also occasionally summons Ostrek Varsha minions: flying enemies resembling Kolmi's eyes, which occasionally fire projectiles at you and are the only creatures in the game that can be eaten alive.

At regular intervals, It will fade and become unhittable together with a Personal Gravity Field which collects projectiles fired at it. As the phase ends, the gathered projectiles will be flung away encased in red auras from the boss. These recycled projectiles can hurt you.

When you defeat Sarnel Zenkoth, its limbs and body will split apart and fall down, and a glowing red portal to The Work (End) will spawn.

chunks.title: Sarnel Zenkoth
chunks.text:
Sarnel Zenkoth

## Tips

- Even hitting the boss can be hard due to its invulnerability phase and large amount of incoming shots. Use the platforms as cover as much as you can.
- The boss is vulnerable to both Material and Collision damage, so attacks that create Acid and Poison are incredibly effective, as well as Falling debris from Earthquake, Earthquake Shot and Nuke.
- Sarnel Zenkoth will ceaselessly pursue you once the fight has been initiated, so running away is not a permanent escape. This oversized Silthar Grephis will follow you to the edge of the universe and back.
  - Because of this, Kolmislimä has an effect that prevents the area around it from unloading no matter how far away you are, even before you have started the fight.
  - SPOILER: This can be exploited to create a "portal" to the Laboratory with spells like Return inside the payload of Dormant Crystal With Trigger triggered with Explosive Detonator, which does not work in unloaded chunks.
  - SPOILER: You can also move Sarnel Zenkoth with Vacuum Field, allowing this technique to function anywhere in the world so long as you have the means (and patience) to do so.
- Reloading Thalvia during the fight can get the boss stuck in a passive state where it is immortal. To fix this, get some distance from it and reload the game again.

chunks.title: Sarnel Zenkoth
chunks.text:
Sarnel Zenkoth

## Scaling

Sarnel Zenkoth's HP scales (and other stats change) based on the sum of:

- The number of New Game Plus (NG+) levels entered so far
- The number of Orbs of True Knowledge that have been collected (this is reset each time you enter a new NG+ level)

For example, in the starting world (NG = 0), having collected 12 orbs, you'll face '12-orb' Sarnel Zenkoth. In NG+, with only 11 orbs collected, you'll face, once again, '12-orb' Sarnel Zenkoth.

The stats listed in the infobox are for the base (0 orb) version of Sarnel Zenkoth.

Scaling is applied at the time the Sampo is picked up - any orbs collected between grabbing the Sampo and ending the game (or entering the next NG+ iteration) do not alter the boss currently chasing you.

The scaling formula is:

Sarnel Zenkoth will also gain some additional attacks, immunities, and occasionally weaknesses at specific orb counts as well. Along with these notable changes, there are some more subtle differences such as the maximum number of minions it can spawn and have alive at once, the number of projectiles fired for each attack, and so on. See this sheet by Bunzero from the Thalvia Discord for the full details.

chunks.title: Ezhara Ithkoth
chunks.text:
Ezhara Ithkoth

name: Ezhara Ithkoth
spawn location: Pyramid
health: 750
drops on death: A Tier 4 No-Shuffle WandExtra Max Health4 random spells from its drop poolFull Heal (on first kill)

name: Drazen Vesvia
health: 142.5
drops on death: 50

Ezhara Ithkoth (or Ithkoth Prowler) is a mini-boss which spawns from an altar in the Pyramid, and only awakens once you get close enough. The glyphs adorning the altar translate to "YOUR REWARD".

It will periodically spawn Drazen Vesvia (or Vesvia Marauders), usually in pairs, that shoot Toxic Sludge projectiles. It cannot be normally damaged until it opens its outer shell to use its ranged attacks.

Upon death, similar to Quonok Skulker, it drops an Extra Max Health and a Wand. Defeating it also unlocks a variety of spells (see Spell Drops below), four of which may also be dropped when it is defeated. On first kill it also drops a full heal.

It does not spawn in Parallel Worlds nor in New Game Plus.

## Research Notes

On the altar that it spawns on, there is also a small book.

"One in the pond

One in the tree

One on the ledge

The notes likely refer to the locations of the four Music Machines.

chunks.title: Ezhara Ithkoth
chunks.text:
Ezhara Ithkoth

## Behavior

Ithkoth Prowler is immune to most damage until it reveals its weaker inner reddish tissue for casting projectiles. It cannot be stained normally, so is immune to effects like Toxic Sludge, and the only way to damage it while it keeps its outer shell closed is to employ Plasma Beam based attacks, which can force it to open its shell. This even works with the Paha Silmä, however due to the short range and low damage, any regular Plasma-type spells would kill it much faster.

Once awoken, Ithkoth Prowler will chase you around the Pyramid, sometimes destroying sections of the brickwork in the cramped corridors. In the more open areas of the Pyramid, it tends to prefer the upper western corners of the rooms. If the Pyramid's ceiling is destroyed, it tends to wander gradually upwards and to the west until it escapes the fight entirely.

## Attacks

Ithkoth Prowler has 4 types of attacks:

1. Summon multiple (usually 1-3) allies, which will chase you and fire quick slime-based projectiles which deal 25 damage. They can also be damaged by projectiles from the Ithkoth Prowler if they happen to get into its path.
2. Reveals its red inner tissue and prepares one of two ranged attacks:
   - 3 bursts of projectiles in a circle, not unlike Sarnel Zenkoth which deals 28 damage for each projectile.
   - 2 large projectiles with a slight homing effect towards you that deals 55 damage.
3. Pokes at you if you're nearby with one of its legs, dealing 13 Melee damage.

If the path to your position is obstructed, it may also quickly move towards you, destroying materials in its path, sometimes with a meandering path.

chunks.title: Ezhara Ithkoth
chunks.text:
Ezhara Ithkoth

## Combat Tips

- Plasma Beam and similar attacks, items, or perks make for very effective tactics, as they force Ezhara Ithkoth to open its shell. It seems to be unable to ignore damage from these sources.
- Spells which carry Fire-type damage are highly effective.
- The main boss room has a fair bit of open space, lacking platforms in the middle. Mobility perks are very helpful to avoid its attacks, but not entirely necessary; most or all platforms around the edge of the arena can be reached without requiring more than your standard levitation height.
- Homing and other similar modifiers are not recommended since they home in on the invulnerable shell, making it much more difficult to hit the boss.

## Spell Drops

When defeated, Ezhara Ithkoth will also drop 4 random spells out of the following pool:

All of the above spells are also unlocked for future runs when it is defeated for the first time.

## Trivia

- Prior to 1.0, Ezhara Ithkoth was very vulnerable to Fire, being easily set alight with Gunpowder or Fire
- Koipi will always give kill credit just like Sarnel Zenkoth. Both of these bosses will fail Pacifist on death because of this.

chunks.title: Sarnel Draventh
chunks.text:
Sarnel Draventh

name: Sarnel Draventh
spawn location: Power Plant
health: 1250
drops on death: Spatial Awareness perk

Sarnel Draventh (also known as Draventh Skitterer) is a spider-like robotic miniboss, found deep within the Power Plant, bearing dangerous attacks and unique traits. It is often referred to as "Mecha Kolmi".

## Behaviour

This foe resides inside of a circular arena, a bit down and straight left from the height of the Experimental Wand. It has 1250 health, along with the following damage type immunities and vulnerabilities:

- Immunity to: Projectile, Explosion, Melee, and Fire damage types.
- Vulnerable to: Slice, Ice, Drill, Holy, and Electricity damage types that will work and are easily obtainable.

While not performing attacks, a projectile eating shield will follow the boss, which means that in order to reliably deal damage without getting too close you must wait for an attack.

It has two attacks:

- A burst of 10 rockets that quickly accelerate towards you, each dealing up to 253 damage.
- A long, red plasma beam that expands after a few seconds, capable of dealing a massive 900/second.
- Also has the ability to summon a Kessari Belvaska (Belvaska Minder).

On death the main body explodes with a force similar to a Holy Bomb, leaving behind a pile of metallic limbs and a special Spatial Awareness perk.

chunks.title: Sarnel Draventh
chunks.text:
Sarnel Draventh

## Combat Tips

- The rockets can prove extremely lethal if you don't have the means to tank them. Finding some cover that the explosions won't destroy is a good way to stay safe.
  - If there's nothing to hide behind, you can use Teleport Bolts, preferably short ones, to dodge the missiles until they expire.
  - Ambrosia can work, with the benefit of allowing you to stay in one spot while attacking the boss.
- Make sure to not accidentally lose the boss. It might leave the arena and wander off deeper into the chasm below, or explore the Power Plant.
  - If you do lose track, look for a tunnel-like path. The boss probably left one behind. Remember to keep your guard up, it could unexpectedly attack as soon as you get close.
- Its large explosion on death can damage you if close enough and lack some type of Explosion protection. Minä have been known to meet a surprise demise after their short-lived victory.

## Trivia

- The spinning rockets that Sarnel Draventh fires were inspired by a boss in the freeware indie game IJI.

chunks.title: Rukhel Vosnok
chunks.text:
Rukhel Vosnok

name: Rukhel Vosnok
spawn location: Meat Realm
health: 1000
drops on death: An Experimental Wand

Rukhel Vosnok (also known as Vosnok Skulker, or Meat Boss) is a spider-like flesh Boss found in the Western Meat Realm.

## Behavior

The Rukhel Vosnok lies inside a circular arena, similar to the Sarnel Draventh. It has 1000 health, along with the following effects to several damage types:

- Resistant to Melee, Explosion and Projectile damage.
- Immunity to Electricity damage.
- Weakness to Slice and Fire damage.

The boss will cycle between two attacks:

- A volley of 8 slow moving orbs that spread in random directions which deal 10+7.5 damage and explode into Pus, along with a fast-moving, homing orb that deals 45+30 damage and inflicts Venomous Curse. During this, the boss' eye will be closed and impervious to all damage.
- A repulsing field that slowly destroys all terrain around itself, while pushing both creatures and projectiles away, including its own orbs from its previous attack. Anything that touches the boss' body will receive 3.75 damage every frame (225/sec). This will last roughly two seconds and, during this, the boss' eye will be open and be vulnerable.

On death, the body will leave a Meat corpse, dropping the Saha Experimental Wand and lifting the Meat Realm's cursed health restriction, with the message:

A curse has been lifted!The air feels easier to breathe

chunks.title: Rukhel Vosnok
chunks.text:
Rukhel Vosnok

## Tips

- This is one of the easier bosses in the game - the main threat comes from The Meat Realm's Curse, which can leave you forced to fight it with very little health.
  - This can be avoided by using long-ranged projectiles to kill it from outside the biome - either by attacking it from the Desert Chasm to the left, or tunneling through the Extremely Dense Rock to the right of it.
  - In the same vein, the boss can also be lured / teleported out of the biome to achieve the same effect.
  - If you want to pinpoint its location, it is at the same depth as the Coal Pits section of The Tower, or the Holy Mountain below the Underground Jungle.
- If you are attempting a longer run, it is best to deal with it the first time you enter the biome. It can be very alarming to suddenly lose thousands of HP after travelling through several Parallel Worlds.

chunks.title: Ezhara Tavventh
chunks.text:
Ezhara Tavventh

name: Ezhara Tavventh
spawn location: Collapsed Mines, Fungal Caverns, The Tower
health: 7.5
drops on death: 10

Ezhara Tavventh (also known as Tavventh Sentinel or Frog) is a small enemy that appears in the Collapsed Mines, Fungal Caverns, and The Tower.

## Behavior

They appear fairly benign, not moving at all, but if you get too close they will quickly lunge at you, dealing surprisingly high damage. They can't jump very high, so levitating above them is a good way to avoid being hit. If set On fire! they will not react in any way, unlike most enemies.

## Trivia

- The peculiar behavior to fire may be a reference to the idiom Boiling The Frog.
- If consumed, will induce the Tripping status effect. This is a reference to the fact that Bufotenin is excreted by some toads. This can be used as a safer way to produce Fungal Reality Shifts earlygame.
- Mixing Whiskey with Frog Meat makes Berserkium.
- They will often do a lot of damage because when they attack, they do damage per frame inside the (moving) hitbox, and frequently the knockback pushes you so that you move in sync with the dangerous damaging hitbox.
- Frogs in Thalvia have been known to be deceptively effective killing machines. Approach with caution.

Kessari Belvaska

name: Kessari Belvaska
spawn location: The Vault, Frozen Vault, Power Plant, The Tower

Kessari Belvaska (or Belvaska Minder) is a robotic flying drone enemy which normally appears in The Vault, healing other enemies.

## Behavior & Combat

Its weapon is a variant of the Heal Projectile spell, doing only 5 healing per hit, but firing much more quickly. Unlike the player spell variant, it does not run out of ammunition.

It is unshielded and cannot take much damage before being destroyed. Since robots cannot be stained with Pheromone, there is no way to convert it to your faction in order to make it heal you. However, if you have the Telekinetic Kick perk, these robots can be held with telekinesis, allowing you to easily place yourself between the drone and an injured enemy for quick healing.

## Trivia

Previously, you could stain yourself with Berserkium or take the Vessha Shapers perk to make the drone heal you, but just like for the Grevan Duvia this functionality was removed and no longer works.

chunks.text:
Duvar Tavqir

name: Duvar Tavqir
spawn location: Snowy Depths, Nakghor Base, Underground Jungle, The Vault, Temple of the Art, Sandcave, Desert Chasm, Frozen Vault, Snowy Chasm, Snowy Wasteland, The Tower

Duvar Tavqir (or Tavqir Swarmer) is a very common Nakghor enemy. Along with its look-alike Naktoi Orphis, it is the most common enemy in Thalvia.

## Behavior

This enemy will fly around slowly and shoot small firebolts aiming directly at your current position. These projectiles have a deceptive arc and deal a hefty 30 damage each, but do not travel far. When Drunk, their projectiles will be unpredictable and no longer land exactly where you were when they were fired, making them much more difficult to dodge.

Duvar Tavqir have blind spots directly above their head and below their feet where they are unable to aim, creating cone-shaped zones for you to safely attack from. Unlike most enemies first encountered in the Snowy Depths, their short range and gravity-affected shots means you can stay on the same plane vertically and attack from far away.

They can often be found in large groups with others of their kind and Naktoi Orphis. One or more Duvar Tavqir will also spawn whenever a Rukhel Kolvax is damaged.

chunks.title: Krel Ymventh
chunks.text:
Krel Ymventh

name: Krel Ymventh
spawn location: Mines, Collapsed Mines, Coal Pits, Fungal Caverns, Snowy Depths, Underground Jungle, The Vault, Temple of the Art, Frozen Vault, Silthar Grephis Lair, Wizards' Den, Overgrown Cavern, Power Plant

Krel Ymventh (or Ymventh Minder) is a flying enemy that can only be found once per run, but that single appearance can be found in almost any of the main areas in Thalvia. It is the ghost of a player's previous run, always spawning with a wand you previously died with. Depending on the wand, this can make Krel Ymventh extremely lethal, or harmless, or even beneficial.

## Behaviour

Krel Ymventh floats around quite slowly, mercilessly attacking every living thing in sight. It is hostile to all creatures, and this can be utilized to help destroy particularly bothersome enemies with some creative kiting. However, be aware the Krel Ymventh has a tendency to swap targets to you if you are in its range. It will also deliberately drop the wand if there are no usable spells left. When not armed with a wand, it will attempt to kick you, dealing moderate damage.

chunks.title: Krel Ymventh
chunks.text:
Krel Ymventh

## Combat Tips

- It takes half damage from most projectiles, even less from melee attacks, and less again from fire. Slice and Explosion damage tend to fare the best.
  - Damage from Slice spells such as Summon Disc Projectile and Arrow is not reduced.
- If it is encountered in the early game and holding a dangerous wand, an easy way to dispatch of Krel Ymventh is by sneaking up on it behind a corner and dropping a tablet on it. This will not only kill it quickly but make it drop 1000 .
- As with all enemies who can pick up wands, kicking the ghost will force it to drop its wand, effectively disarming it.
- As a ghostly enemy it is immune to stains, which includes Polymorphine. However, spell-based polymorphing effects can still apply.

chunks.title: Krel Ymventh
chunks.text:
Krel Ymventh

## Spawning

Krel Ymventh has a unique set of spawning conditions, where it only appears once you have 35 deaths that create a "bones" file.

### Bones

Also known as the Bones Folder. Bones files are only created when:

1. No game-mods are loaded at any time during the run,
2. You are not killed by disintegration SPOILER: (e.g. Curse damage from the normal ending),
3. You are not killed while Polymorphed,
4. You are carrying at least one wand that is not just an unmodified starting wand.

Each death in this manner causes a bones file to generate in your persistent save data. When you die holding multiple wands, one of the valid wands will be picked at random to be stored in the bones collection.

To check how many you have, see how many files are in the folder:

- /Nolla_Games_Noita/save00/persistent/bones_new

Bones files are essentially just wand entity data, stored in individual .XML files.

Only 50 are ever stored. When the folder has 50 items in it, a new one being added will remove a random one.

#### Examine your bones

An easy way to check your mod files is to search them for "action_id=". Each action_id line will list the name ID of a spell. For example, Energy Orb is SLOW_BULLET.

Alter_Ukko also made a tool that can display bones contents.

You may wish to delete the boring or insta-death bones.

### Triggers

Unlike most enemy spawn triggers, which use the same 3-4 pixel-based triggers in the biome terrain wang tiles to spawn random enemies, Krel Ymventh has a separate spawn function that is tied to a very specific trigger which is used by nothing else. This function has five states where it does different things:

chunks.title: Krel Ymventh
chunks.text:
Krel Ymventh

- State 0 - Spawns nothing, but has a chance to advance to the next state.
- State 1 - Spawn 4 Candles and advance the state.
- State 2 - Next possible spawn point will have 4 candles and will advance the state.
- State 3 - Next possible spawn point will spawn the ghost and will advance the state.
- State 4 - Spawn nothing. This prevents another ghost from ever spawning in the same run including in New Game Plus.

On State 0, every spawn point that is loaded is a chance to advance to the next state. The likelihood of this happening depends on the amount of outdoors fog. If the fog level is below or equal to 10%, then there's a /30 chance of advancing to the next state. With the fog level above 10%, the chance increases to /12.

The check to advance from State 0 could fail several times and result in no ghost spawning in the whole run. The function has a random variable not tied to the seed or the coordinates, which causes high variance in the ghost spawn even in the same seed. If the check is successful, Thalvia will advance from State 0 to State 2 near instantly. State 2 and 3 last as long as it takes to load in the next possible spawn point for a ghost.

chunks.title: Krel Ymventh
chunks.text:
Krel Ymventh

: Lua Code Sample: State 0 to 1 Advancement -- The state transitions are implemented in the engine, NOT in Lua. -- This Lua code approximates how the engine decides when to advance from -- state 0 to state 1. -- In unmodded Thalvia BIOME_APPARITION_CHANCE is always 30. -- The engine uses a different number generator from the one used by Lua. if state == 0 then local apparition_chance = tonumber(MagicNumbersGetValue("BIOME_APPARITION_CHANCE")) local world_component = EntityGetFirstComponent(GameGetWorldStateEntity(), "WorldStateComponent") local fog = ComponentGetValue2(world_component, "fog") if fog > 0.1 then -- Increase likelihood when there's some fog outside apparition_chance = math.floor(apparition_chance / Random(2, 3)) end if Random(1, apparition_chance) == 1 then state = 1 end return end

The precise probability of Krel Ymventh spawning is unknown, but in general the more possible spawn locations for a given biome, and the larger the biome region, the more likely it is that Krel Ymventh will be seen in that biome.
