chunks.title: Krel Grekoth
chunks.text:
Krel Grekoth

name: Krel Grekoth
spawn location: Power Plant
health: 125
drops on death: 50

Krel Grekoth (or Grekoth Brooder) is a bipedal robot enemy found exclusively in the Power Plant. It wields a fast-firing weapon which shoots out volleys of swift and highly damaging blue bolts.

It may be considered a stronger version of the Morghor Marksman.

## Behaviour

Krel Grekoth walk around slowly and stand still when firing. They cannot fly or swim, however, they are immune to Suffocation.

They attack with very fast-moving projectiles, which they shoot in volleys of two. Between each volley, there is only little time before the next. The bolts they fire deal 11.25 and 5 damage each, as well as knocking you back with considerable force.

## Combat Tips

- Their attacks are powerful and very numerous, so take cover.
- Acid dissolves their metal body, dealing high amounts of damage quickly.
  - Since Acid does not eat away the Dense Steel that makes up many of the walls and floors of the Power Plant, creating a pool of Acid for them to plunge in is quite easy.
- Immune to Projectile, Fire and Ice damage.
- Most vulnerable to Electricity (especially effective), Explosion and Holy damage.

Quorin Ostvax

Quorin Ostvax (or Ostvax Brooder) is a blue mushroom-type enemy found primarily in the Fungal Caverns and Overgrown Cavern, however, it may occasionally appear in small fungal pit structures in the Mines. It bleeds Fungus Blood and on death it detonates, scattering its corpses made of Weird Fungus around.

## Behaviour

Quorin Ostvax will generally ignore you and wander on the ground aimlessly, but if approached they will jump at you and violently explode. The explosion deals 125 explosion damage. Killing Quorin Ostvax also causes them to explode.

## Combat Tips

- Due to their powerful explosion on death, engaging at a distance is recommended.
- They are extremely sensitive to Fire damage.

Grevan Vesvax (or Vesvax Sentinel) is a passive animal that may be seen on the island in the center of the Lake frolicking or being chased by the wolf.

Vesvax Sentinel, along with Grevan Krelvia (flying sheep) and Ymrik Orreth (buzzing sheep), are the three possible results of being affected by Polymorph, and one of many more from Chaos polymorph.

You cannot attack when transformed into a sheep. However transforming into one of the flight-capable sheep is very useful to reach certain areas, or escape from a Holy Mountain without angering the gods.

chunks.title: Ostrek Sarghor
chunks.text:
Ostrek Sarghor

name: Ostrek Sarghor
spawn location: Snowy Depths, Nakghor Base, The Vault, Frozen Vault, Power Plant, Desert Chasm, The Tower
ngplus spawn location: Coal Pits
health: Normal237.5, The Vault637.5
drops on death: 90 Normal250 The Vault

Laser-tankki (or Sarghor Glider) is a green robotic tank enemy in the Nakghor faction which shoots laser beams.

## Behaviour and Combat

The Sarghor Glider rapidly fires Magic Bolts out of its laser blaster, mounted at the front and consisting of a rod with several circles around it, stereotypical of some "retro" sci-fi weapons. Its projectiles deal high damage and knockback.

As a robotic enemy, it has high resistance to Projectile and Slice spells while being vulnerable to Electricity and Explosion spells. As with most tanks it explodes when killed, but its explosion is nearly double the size of other tank-type enemies and deals additional damage. Exercise a high level of caution and avoid the explosion when possible.

This enemy, like other tanks, is aggressive to most enemies with the exception of Nakghor.

## Notes

- This enemy usually appears later in Thalvia than the other tanks, hence its more powerful attributes. However, it is also an uncommon spawn in the Nakghor Base.
- Like other tanks, it takes this enemy a short period of time to adjust its aim before firing. Unlike other tanks, once it locks on it fires rapid bursts which deal high damage as well as stunning and knocking the target backwards quite strongly.
- This is an enemy best dealt with from cover to avoid allowing it to get a clear shot.

chunks.title: Naktoi Krelkoth
chunks.text:
Naktoi Krelkoth

name: Naktoi Krelkoth
spawn location: Fungal Caverns, The Vault, Frozen Vault, The Tower
health: Fungal Caverns 10, The Tower 40, The Vault; Frozen Vault 90
traits: Possesses a Permanent Shield.
drops on death: Maximum number of loops have been performed

Naktoi Krelkoth (or Krelkoth Burrower) is a shielded, flying, physics-based robot enemy found primarily in Fungal Caverns and The Vault.

## Behavior & Combat

The drone can usually be found banging itself against the terrain trying to reach you, testing which paths it can take. It only has a medium range rifle-shot attack, which it uses to harass more than anything else. Rarely a threat if encountered on its own, it becomes deadly when paired with more aggressive enemies, constantly knocking you to the ground and making any escape attempt that much harder. Its shield prevents projectiles from reaching it, but that can be brought down quickly with rapid sustained fire upon which the drone can be easily destroyed due to its extremely low HP. On death, it will explode in a cloud of fire and rain burning oil down all around.

It doesn't have any particular weaknesses of note, but spells that can either fire rapidly or bypass its shield are very effective. Luminous Drill will bring the drone down very quickly and any projectiles with Homing will hammer through the shield in seconds. A decently sized explosion will also take it out instantly, but can be hard to position right.

spawn location: Coal Pits, The Tower

Grevan Ostmar (or Ostmar Herder) is a very common flying enemy found in the Coal Pits. It is fairly small and purple in color, and bleeds Slime when hit or killed.

Drazen Mavsha

Drazen Mavsha (or Mavsha Darter) is a type of flying robot found primarily in The Vault.

## Behaviour

Mavsha Darters fly around with their jetpacks and use a Flamethrower, shooting 4 lobs of fire with a cooldown of about a second before the next 4 are shot. The shots stun and do high damage up close.

## Combat Tips

- The flamethrower has a low range, but can quickly set you and its surroundings On Fire.

## See Also

- Kessari Sarnok

chunks.text:
Mavrok Drakoth

name: Mavrok Drakoth
spawn location: Mines, Collapsed Mines, Coal Pits, Desert, The Tower
health: 35
traits: Drops gunpowder when hurt.Takes rapid damage when Wet.
drops on death: 10

Mavrok Drakoth (or Drakoth Drifter) is a flaming, floating skull occasionally encountered in the Mines and Coal Pits.

## Behavior

They follow you and try to get close for a melee attack. If hurt, they will scatter highly unstable Gunpowder all over the place, dealing low damage with many small explosions. Their gunpowder blood tends to damage the surrounding terrain, which may be useful, but can also overwhelm you if the fight occurs near flammable or explosive objects.

## Combat Tips

- Keep away from anything flammable or explosive if possible while fighting.
- Their gunpowder blood is scattered quite widely and sometimes will be a little delayed in exploding, so it is wise to avoid standing on the ground for a short while after the fight concludes.
- Levitating off the ground gives the best chance at avoiding the explosions from its blood, as most of it will explode in contact with the terrain and it is otherwise somewhat difficult to avoid.
- Keep a safe distance to avoid its charge attack, it will otherwise follow fairly slowly and be relatively easy to take out.
- Fire spirits take heavy damage from Water and being Wet, so target them with Rain Cloud or Water Trail for easier kills.
- They fall quite quickly when hit with most attacks and will often not regain their composure before they hit solid ground. This can be exploited to knock them into pools of water for environmental trick kills.

Mavrok Drakoth

## Trivia

- If you Chaos Polymorph into this enemy, you will catch On fire upon returning to normal.
- Be very cautious around water while affected by Chaos Polymorph into a Drakoth Drifter, as it deals heavy damage.
- Polymorphine, Chaotic Polymorphine and Unstable Polymorphine have no effect on this enemy, but Circle of Transmogrification and Circle of Unstable Metamorphosis will still affect it as normal.

chunks.title: Morvek Zenvax
chunks.text:
Morvek Zenvax

name: Morvek Zenvax
spawn location: Snowy Depths, The Vault, Frozen Vault, Power Plant
health: 55
drops on death: 20

Morvek Zenvax (or Zenvax Shambler) is a Nakghor enemy that can be encountered in the Snowy Depths, The Vault, the Frozen Vault, and a handful of other locations.

## Behaviour and Combat

The Zenvax Shambler spawns in pairs and attacks with Glue Balls that stick you to nearby surfaces. The glue severely hinders movement, leaving you as an easy target for Ymrik Vesventh and Naktoi Orphis shots. The glue balls can be destroyed faster by being shot at.

The Zenvax Shambler takes a moment to charge up their shots, giving you a indication of when they are about to fire.

## Trivia

- The Zenvax Shambler is the only Nakghor that can spawn in the Power Plant.

chunks.title: Krel Vosphis
chunks.text:
Krel Vosphis

name: Krel Vosphis
spawn location: Collapsed Mines, Coal Pits, Fungal Caverns, Snowy Depths, The Tower
health: 18.75
drops on death: 10

Krel Vosphis (or Vosphis Sifter) is a slimy green flying creature which spits toxic slime balls and roams many of the early levels.

## Behavior

Vosphis Sifters shoot accurate, slow flying slime balls from long range, similar to the Slimeball spell. Unlike the player-spell counterpart, the attack used by the normal variant (not the weak variant) has a Toxic Sludge trail which can pool on the ground, or coat you if the projectile is overhead. They will chase after you if you move out of their line of sight, making them vulnerable to kiting strategies, especially in more cramped areas.

In environments with the Humid modifier such as the Fungal Caverns, the projectiles shot will spray more Toxic Sludge, and hang in the air for several seconds.

They will bleed Toxic Sludge when hit, quickly coating nearby entities and the terrain with the Toxic liquid, though the weak variant tends to bleed much less. When killed, its corpse will also bleed a fairly large quantity of Toxic Sludge.

When On Fire, they will actively go to a known water source to extinguish the fire.

chunks.title: Krel Vosphis
chunks.text:
Krel Vosphis

## Combat Tips

- Their projectiles fly slowly and can usually be avoided, though the Toxic Sludge trail it emits can be more of a concern.
- If fighting more than one at a time, it can be useful to spray a small amount of water around to help minimize the amount of Toxic Sludge that sticks around.
- Kiting strategies can be quite effective for forcing them into close range, as they'll quickly give chase as soon as you move out of sight.
- They remain still when firing, so it is effective to dodge their projectiles and retaliate while they are stationary.
- Make sure to kill them quickly once you damage them. When damaged, they can begin bleeding a small geyser of Toxic Sludge that can make it very difficult and/or dangerous to navigate. Their corpses can sometimes continue this bleeding jet.

## Trivia

- Despite bleeding Toxic Sludge when hurt and killed, their corpses will emit Slime when damaged by spells such as Chainsaw.
- The slimeballs fired by the weak variant do, in fact, have a Toxic Sludge trail as well, but it's so weak that it's only noticeable if the projectile is severely slowed (for example via the Humid biome modifier).

## See Also

- Grevan Rukkoth

Drazen Quokoth

name: Drazen Quokoth

health: 6000

Drazen Quokoth (also known as Quokoth Marauder, Slime Caterpillar, or Tiny) is a miniboss found at the buried skull in the Meat Realm, embedded in some extremely dense rock. It is not present in Parallel Worlds but can be found again in New Game Plus.

## Behaviour

Drazen Quokoth bleeds Ominous Liquid which inflicts a Poisoned stain upon contact. It deals extreme Melee-Bite damage and fires homing projectiles from its body. Similar to other worms it charges at you, and additionally can also fly. Note that even though the bite is not pure Melee damage, Melee Immunity will still block it due to how Multi-Type damage interacts with immunities.

At 6000 health and with Projectile damage immunity, you will have to use a different damage type such as Slice damage to defeat it.

Like Sarnel Zenkoth, Drazen Quokoth will ceaselessly pursue you once the fight has been initiated, so running away is not a permanent escape.

## Rewards

- Tier 10 non-shuffle wand
  - Note: This is one of the only 3 in-game ways to obtain a tier 10 wand. Hell in Nightmare mode can also spawn tier 10 wands, as can Great Treasure Chests.
  - This wand can have a theoretical maximum capacity of 62, which is lower than from nightmare because this wand is a Tier 10 better wand which cannot generate with as good stats as a normal Tier 10. However, wands that can go past a capacity of 26 are extremely rare; 26 should be considered to be the maximum capacity for any non-seeded run.
- Tier 6 non-shuffle wand
- Large Extra Max HP
- Full Health Regeneration

chunks.title: Drazen Quokoth

Drazen Quokoth

- Defeating the Drazen Quokoth will unlock one of the Achievement Pillars.

## Trivia

- Commonly referred to as "Tiny", both because of the in-code name "maggot_tiny", and ironically because it is huge.
- Drazen Quokoth is by far the largest creature in Thalvia.

chunks.title: Orune Morvaska
chunks.text:
Orune Morvaska

name: Orune Morvaska
health: 2.5

Orune Morvaska (also known as Morvaska Stalker) is a small floating enemy produced by the Orune Tavvaska and the Summon Morvaska Stalker spell.

## Behavior

It floats back and forth in the air, exploding into a highly damaging cloud of Freezing Vapours in a kamikaze attack when it gets close enough to a target. They do not immediately beeline for you like homing spells, instead flying much more erratically.

## Combat Tips

- Be careful when dealing with multiple, a large number of Morvaska Stalkers can easily overwhelm you.
- Their erratic movement can make them difficult to hit with projectile wands. "Spraying" can work well, especially against large numbers of them.

Sarnel Halvaska

name: Sarnel Halvaska
spawn location: Ancient Laboratory, Fungal Caverns, Snowy Depths, Magical Temple, The Vault, Temple of the Art, Pyramid, Wizards' Den, Frozen Vault, The Tower
health: Normal125, Temple of the Art350

Sarnel Halvaska (or Halvaska Watcher) is one of the many master spellcasters. It takes the appearance of a humanoid with metallic gray skin, a rectangular head with two horns and a brown wire at the back, and a square-shaped white light for a face, and is dressed in a slate-gray robe and cape with a glaucous trim. The light screen can be seen through darkness, similar to the eyes of Orune Morvax. Its body is made of ambiguous meat.

## Behavior

The Halvaska Watcher casts blue magic orbs which inflict the Neutralized spells status effect for 20 seconds. Any spells cast by you will instantly fizzle out, while explosive spells will detonate immediately. This effectively negates all of your offensive options aside from kicking and throwing objects.

## Combat Tips

- As with all Masters, exercise caution and focus on avoiding the projectiles. This is easily done by constantly moving perpendicular to the enemy's aiming trajectory (which usually means levitating up or falling down) and staying at a medium distance.
- They have an aura that converts the "item" variant of rock (which includes Tablets) to air, which can limit tablet throw or kick damage to 25 or even 0, while also destroying the tablet.

chunks.title: Kessari Dramar

Kessari Dramar

## Kessari Dramar

Much like a Tavghor Brooder, the Dramar Seeder will fire an accelerating red skull-shaped projectile upon detecting a target, inflicting 20 damage and applying a modified version of Venomous Curse. It also comes equipped with a forward-facing shield that deflects projectiles, bleeds Oil, and has similar resistances to damage.

Dramar Seeders can pick up and use wands.

Dramar Seeders can be only found in the Frozen Vault and the Power Plant. SPOILER: In New Game Plus, Tavghor Brooders can also spawn in The Vault, Silthar Grephis Lair and the Ancient Laboratory. They can also be found in the Nakghor Base in further loops.

The Rukhel Mavventh (also known as Mavventh Trapper) is a rare enemy that looks exactly like a normal chest. It cannot move and it will not attack you until you are touching it.

The Ymrik Varvaska (also known as Varvaska Brooder) is a rare variant which will grow limbs when awakened and use them to attack you. It will drop the Leggy Mutation perk when killed. It has a 5% chance to replace a regular Mavventh Trapper.

chunks.title: Rukhel Mavventh
chunks.text:
Rukhel Mavventh

## Strategies

There are several ways to distinguish between a Chest and a Mavventh Trapper:

- If there is no 'Treasure chest' tooltip displayed when hovering over a chest with the mouse, then it is a Mavventh Trapper.
- If you attack it and it displays a damage value, it is a Mavventh Trapper.
  - It's generally safer to just shoot chests open since there's no known penalty compared to opening one by interacting with it. One possible risk, however, is that Treasure Chests may drop flasks, which may accidentally become shattered or broken in the process, especially with wands that shoot projectiles rapidly.
- If it is floating in water, it is a Mavventh Trapper.
- If it is rotated in any way such that it looks visually different from the page image on the right (exclude biting frames), it is not a Mavventh Trapper.
  - Chests are physics objects and may rotate, and Mavventh Trappers are not.
- If a stain indicator appears on top of the chest, then it is a Mavventh Trapper.

Note: None of the above strategies will help you identify a Varvaska Brooder. Their disguises are significantly more sophisticated, and they will not awaken until you approach them and press the interact key to "open" the chest. Once you do, they will sprout legs and try to attack.

Also, Mavventh Trappers do not appear from ground level to the 3 chunks (first Holy Mountain) underground: all chests in the Mines and Collapsed Mines are thus safe (except when affected by the Cozy / Furnished biome modifier).

- A Mavventh Trapper stained with Pheromone will drop gold nuggets of varying size and rarely Potions and Extra Max Health. It should be cautioned however that with each output of a Mavventh Trapper, it will have a small chance to take a sudden lethal amount of damage.

  - Mavventh Trapper potion drops are determined by pixel, much like that of the wands produced by the Summon Zentha Nakvaska spell.
  - A great way for alchemist players to take advantage of the pixel-to-potion mechanic to obtain consistent potion outputs is to douse the Mavventh Trapper in Ambrosia and Pheromone stains, then using any form of mob movement (Swapper, Circle of Buoyancy, etc.), move the Mavventh Trapper into a room filled with any variant of fungus. Due to its passable nature for only creatures, items and gold will be teleported to the top above the fungus. By making this room underneath some EDR, and having a flat space dug out, with varied success of potion breakages, the Mavventh Trapper will pump out the same potion every time as long as it stays still.

chunks.title: Belthar Ernqir
chunks.text:
Belthar Ernqir

Belthar Ernqir (lit. Ernqir Shambler) is a medium sized worm enemy that eats through the ground.

A Belthar Ernqir may spawn by breaking the wiggling eggs found on a branch of the Giant Tree and, like most other blue worms, may spawn naturally anywhere in the mountain. They may also spawn from damaging Cocoons in the Underground Jungle.

## Behavior & Combat

Belthar Ernqir dig through the ground, leaving behind tunnels wherever they've traveled. While in the air, they are at the mercy of gravity until they enter solid ground again.

They are aggressive to anything that isn't a Ernqir Shambler, unable to discriminate between you and other creatures of the mountain, although it seems to prefer you over anything else. Belthar Ernqir only have a Melee attack, and attack by burrowing in circular patterns and launching itself at you at high speeds.

## Combat Tips

- Keeping yourself above the ground is the best way to avoid the Ernqir Shambler's attack.
  - Wandering into their tunnels is risky since they can attack you from all sides while you can only move back and forth.
- Belthar Ernqir is harmless if you have Melee Immunity.
- Spells with Slice damage, such as Chainsaw or Disc Projectile, serve to produce much more valuable Ernqir Shambler Blood.

Tavrek Ezhreth (also known as The Ezhreth Trapper, Grand Master, or Wizard Boss) is a boss encountered in the Throne Room, on the east edge of the eastern Wizards' Den. It appears as a floating humanoid figure made of dripping red flesh, adorned with a torn purple robe with a pattern of three eyes scrawled onto it, as well as a cylindrical metal helmet with blood dripping down its eyeslits. Although quite slow, moving in a manner similar to the Kessari Ithvax, it uses an array of dangerous attacks, which can quickly overwhelm and debuff you to the point of death.

chunks.title: Tavrek Ezhreth

Tavrek Ezhreth

## Behavior

The Ezhreth Trapper will remain stationary in the center of the arena until it spots you. At this point the fight begins, and the boss will slowly move towards you, stopping from time to time in order to perform attacks.

It has 8 Orbs which slowly orbit around it.

- 4 Death Orbs () make it invincible, so they have to be killed in order to deal damage to the Ezhreth Trapper.
- 4 Blood Orbs () are not to be killed, but avoided, as the damage they receive will be unavoidably dealt back to you as Blood Link damage (actual damage type is Curse). This can be devastating if you're using high-damage, one-shot spells. Note that this damage is nullified by Ambrosia.

When you are visible, the boss will periodically raise its hand, and perform one of the Phase 1 or Phase 2 attacks, granted it is in said Phase. In Phase 3 the boss will only use one attack, while continuously chasing you. The boss transitions to Phase 2 when it reaches 50% health and its appearance changes such that its helmet is removed revealing a writhing mass of flesh. Phase 3 begins when the boss reaches 20% health and its head seems completely gone.

Defeating the Ezhreth Trapper unlocks and drops the following five spells:

- Wand Refresh

In addition to the extremely useful Sauvan Ydin, the Ezhreth Trapper also drops a Book titled "A Cunning Contraption". Its contents are a hint to the Crystal Key secrets.

"The secret lies in music!

The key to the heavens' lock is borne from music all over the world.

Killing the Ezhreth Trapper with a certain method is part of the SPOILER: Varvax Shambler quest.

Part of completing the Varvax Shambler Quest involves killing the Ezhreth Trapper by drowning it in Swamp which spawns and unlocks the Wand Homing spell. One reliable way to do this is by obtaining the Summon Swamp spell, which always spawns on the Kantele Hauen Leukaluusta. Note that the orbs can be killed and the boss can be harmed by other means before this occurs - it only needs to take the last point of damage from drowning (while touching more Swamp than any other liquid) to succeed.

## Combat Tips

chunks.title: Tavrek Ezhreth
chunks.text:
Tavrek Ezhreth

- The boss has a nullification effect that destroys projectiles, but the top 16 pixels of its hitbox are outside of this. Shooting the head from above is often a lot more effective as a result.
- Don't be greedy with your shots, especially when using high damage wands. One missed shot into a Blood Orb can take down a huge chunk of your health, or even kill you.
- Lead the Ezhreth Trapper to a small structure in the Wizards' Den and orbit it during the fight. This can be a great solution for avoiding the Magical Burst attack, which can easily spell death without shields or repulsion fields.
- In the first two phases, you can abuse the fact that the Ezhreth Trapper will raise its hand to head level to cast its spells. If you manage to get the Ezhreth Trapper to the opposite side of a wall that you are facing and then open a gap in said wall near its lower body, you will be able to freely attack it without any of its projectiles hitting you, as the Grand Master will generally sit still and cast projectiles that hit the wall above. However, know that the Green Meteor spell can destroy terrain.
- It may be wiser to use lower damage rapid fire wands, as the boss does not have invincibility frames or a shield. This also reduces the risk of losing large amounts of health due to Blood Orbs.
- Make sure to clear the nearby area of any enemies. Kill the various Masters just as they are summoned. If ignored, they can quickly increase in numbers and overwhelm you.
- Always check what debuff the boss gives you. With wands that can hurt you, do not shoot when under the Boomerang Spells debuff.
- You can exploit the Boomerang Spells debuff to Heal with a Healing Bolt. Note that you can hurt yourself with Healing Bolts if certain conditions are met

- Melee Immunity can make Phase 3 trivial.
- Staining yourself with Ambrosia is recommended.
- Trick kills methods do not trigger damage reflection.
- It loses invincibility for 1 frame every 100 frames in Phase 1 that it is possible to kill it with Piercing Shot and Homing.
- Material damage doesn't trigger the Blood Orbs' revenge mechanic, so a Sea Of Acid/Lava can make Phase 1 easier, as long as you have somewhere safe to land.
- After the boss dies, be cautious you don't accidentally destroy the Sauvan Ydin before you can pick it up.
- A single Circle of Acid creates enough Acid to destroy the boss entirely. Sauvan Ydin is immune to Acid and even converts it instantly to Concentrated Mana, so there's no fear of losing the reward.
- Ezhreth Trapper has a small projectile deletion field centered on his torso which activates upon taking damage, for this reason it is recommended to attack his head or lower body to avoid it.

Naktoi Quovax (or Quovax Marksman) is a Nakghor enemy that throws mines and shoots shotgun pellets. It can appear in several biomes, with the earliest being Coal Pits and the latest being The Vault, as well as some areas off the main path, like Sandcave.

## Behavior

Naktoi Quovax flies around until seeing something it wants to target. It will then alternate between two ranged attacks:

1st attack: It throws a mine, which appears as a glowing red dot made of Rusted Metal. These mines fly in a short arc and deal no contact damage, sticking to whatever surface it first hits. When something moves too close, the mine will blink yellow, and explode after about half a second. This attack deals 35 damage to you, sets things on fire, and does mild damage to the environment, with a digging strength of 10.

2nd attack: It pulls out a shotgun and shoots at you, in the same manner as Halvox Nakvia.

If you gets too close, it will do a melee attack by smacking you with its gun, dealing between 10-17.5 Melee damage.

chunks.title: Naktoi Quovax
chunks.text:
Naktoi Quovax

## Combat Tips

- The mines are easy to see, as they glow bright red. However, if you are focusing on another enemy, you might accidentally step on one. Make sure not to get tunnel vision when being near these enemies.
- The mines don't detonate until you get close, so hovering above them is an easy way to prevent detonating them. You can also intentionally detonate them so you don't activate them later, as the explosion timer gives just enough time for you to get away.
  - Intentionally keeping Naktoi Quovax alive can be useful for digging tunnels, but be careful of the shotgun attack when doing so.
- Having effective cover can help you avoid the shotgun. However, it is easy enough to avoid without it, as long as you start moving out of the way as it's shooting.
- Naktoi Quovax is resistant to Projectile and Explosion damage, but weak to Electricity and Fire, so prioritize those attacks when fighting.
- Toxic Sludge is highly effective against this enemy, killing it within a few seconds.

chunks.title: Ezhara Silventh
chunks.text:
Ezhara Silventh

name: Ezhara Silventh
spawn location: The Vault, Frozen Vault, Temple of the Art, The Tower
health: Normal150, The Vault400
drops on death: 60 Normal160 The Vault

Ezhara Silventh (or the Silventh Drifter) is an floating enemy found in The Vault, the Frozen Vault, and the Temple of the Art.

## Behavior

It shoots a powerful laser, but with a telegraph, which helps to avoid it.

## Combat Tips

- Like most slimes it has very low resistances, allowing almost all forms of damage to easily reduce its health.
- It is not very dangerous on its own, though with multiple enemies it can easily overwhelm you and deal massive damage.
- Unless there is another enemy that can pin you down, it should be prioritized in small fights.
- You can easily avoid its attacks with well timed levitation.

chunks.title: Morvek Ithventh
chunks.text:
Morvek Ithventh

name: Morvek Ithventh
spawn location: Snowy Depths, Underground Jungle, The Vault, The Tower
health: 175
drops on death: 60

Morvek Ithventh (or Ithventh Stalker) is a rare robotic enemy that can spawn naturally in The Vault, occasionally in the Underground Jungle, and more commonly in The Tower. It has two floating hands that are detached from the body that shoot glowing green orbs towards enemies and you. These orbs deal 20 damage per hit, and have a glowing pixelated effect.

chunks.title: Morvek Ithventh
chunks.text:
Morvek Ithventh

## Hand Nakphis Trappers

In the Snowy Depths, statues made of rock can be found, resembling the shape of a hand with one or two fingers extended. Kicking these statues or targeting them with Telekinetic Kick will trigger at least one Ithventh Stalker to spawn, and the statue will disappear. These hand statues do not spawn in parallel worlds, but can be found in new game plus.

A minimum of 3 statues typically spawn in the Snowy Depths, and the number of Ithventh Stalkers spawned from activating each increases with each statue activated in a run. The first statue activated only spawns one monk, the next two, and the third statue will spawn three Ithventh Stalkers.

Additionally, activating the third statue will spawn the Broken Spell item, which is required to begin the series of events that allows you to unlock The End Of Everything spell.

A useful method of transporting the statue to the altar is to dig stepped tunnels at roughly 45-degree angles, then use the Kuu to slowly drag the statue along with you to the surface. Take care not to destroy the statue when digging the tunnels, and also note that the statue has a tendency to despawn if it falls too far from the player. Angled tunnels help limit the risk of losing the statue in this way while also allowing you to recover levitation energy frequently.

chunks.title: Morvek Ithventh
chunks.text:
Morvek Ithventh

## Behavior & Combat

Morvek Ithventh will attack you on sight and can even target you if you are Invisible, but it moves slowly and tends not to chase if you flee, making it easy to escape. It is a sturdy enemy, but its projectiles move fairly slowly and in straight lines, making it reasonably straightforward to avoid taking damage during a one-on-one encounter.

Although the Ithventh Stalker is technically a robot type enemy, it does not take damage from Concentrated Mana, and lacks most of the typical damage resistances robots generally have, other than being immune to freezing and burning. It is, however, immune to critical hits.

Each of Morvek Ithventh's hands will hold up two fingers while it is attacking, and will hold up five fingers and stop attacking if it does not have "line of sight" to attack. The "line of sight" of the hands can be blocked by liquids, including materials from the Mist spells except for Mist of Spirits, even though the attacks themselves are not stopped by them. True Orbit Mists can be used to prevent their attacks more reliably than Homing Mists, as homing mists home in on and surround the body rather than the hands.

Morvek Ithventh takes a bit of time to start attacking you after gaining line of sight, allowing for an opportunity to hit it with a high damage attack like Magic Missile, or throwing an Emerald Tablet. This is especially easy when spawned intentionally from a Hand Nakphis Trapper, since you have as much time as you want to prepare. This can be an easy way to get gold in Snowy Depths.

## Trivia

- Morvek Ithventh's hands have 65 each and can be destroyed via non-projectile damage, in which case it will have no remaining means of attack.

chunks.title: Ymrik Krelsha
chunks.text:
Ymrik Krelsha

name: Ymrik Krelsha
spawn location: Fungal Caverns, Temple of the Art, Wizards' Den, The Tower
ngplus2 spawn location: Ancient Laboratory
health: Normal100, Temple Of The Art350
drops on death: 160

Ymrik Krelsha (or Krelsha Burrower) is one of the many master spellcasters. It takes the appearance of a humanoid with purple skin and a five-horned, tendrilled or crown-shaped head with a single, cross-shaped white eye, and is dressed in a Tyrian purple robe and cape with a pink trim. Its body is made of stinky meat.

## Behavior

The Krelsha Burrower casts high-velocity purple magic orbs with weak homing that inflict the Polymorph status effect for 10 seconds. This transforms the target into a Grevan Vesvax, Grevan Krelvia, or Ymrik Orreth, much like the effect from touching Polymorphine.

chunks.title: Ymrik Krelsha
chunks.text:
Ymrik Krelsha

## Combat Tips

- As with all Masters, exercise caution and focus on avoiding the projectiles. This is easily done by constantly moving perpendicular to the enemy's aiming trajectory (which usually means levitating up or falling down) and staying at a medium distance.
- It doesn't move very fast, so you should be able to choose when to fight it.
- As its attacks can turn you into a harmless entity that can be killed in one hit, this may actually be one of the most dangerous enemies in Thalvia for a high-leveled player.
- Approach corners and open areas carefully, since they will attack from offscreen, especially from above or below.
- Eating their corpses provides about 180 seconds of Polymorph immunity, which can save your life if you're facing multiple enemies with polymorph abilities.
  - This can stack, which means you can easily get dozens of minutes of Polymorph immunity in places such as the Wizards' Den where these enemies are common.
  - A Tavghor Brooder can be used to repeatedly kill and revive a nearby Krelsha Burrower, potentially providing you with an unlimited source of corpses to eat for Polymorph Immunity.
- Their projectiles can sometimes bypass passive shield spells. Do not trust such protections.

## See Also

- Polymorph Immunity Farming

chunks.title: Quorin Kesvax
chunks.text:
Quorin Kesvax

name: Quorin Kesvax
spawn location: Fungal Caverns, Overgrown Cavern, The Tower
health: 125
drops on death: 50

Quorin Kesvax (also known as Kesvax Drifter) is a purple ant-shaped enemy that first appears in the Fungal Caverns, west of the Coal Pits.

## Behavior

Quorin Kesvax mostly crawl on the ground but are also able to jump and lunge at you. They can also swim.

If you get too close, Quorin Kesvax will spit Acid at you that can deal tremendous amounts of damage in a very short amount of time.

## Combat Tips

- Keep your distance, as their attacks are only short-range but very damaging.

chunks.title: Silthar Vosreth
chunks.text:
Silthar Vosreth

name: Silthar Vosreth
spawn location: Underground Jungle, Temple of the Art, Sandcave, The Tower
health: Normal150, Underground Jungle300
traits: Immune to poison
drops on death: 60 Normal120 Underground Jungle

## Behavior

Silthar Vosreth fly around using a jetpack, patrolling areas of the biome. When they land, they walk at a medium speed but are easily outrun by the player.

Upon line of sight to the player, they shoot a Poison projectile that leaves a trail of Poison behind. The projectile deals 8.25 and 6.25 damage. On close range, they whack their shotgun at their enemies dealing anywhere from 10-17.5 damage. Silthar Vosreth will pursuit fleeing creatures around a few corners but will lose track of its enemy after a while.

They are friendly toward other fellow Nakghor.

## Combat Tips

- Fly above their poison projectiles to avoid the poison from their trail.
- Due to the high amount of health this enemy possesses along with the damage it inflicts over time, it is recommended to either carefully wear down its health, or strategically kill it as fast as possible, as it can easily do high amounts of damage before being killed if attacked recklessly.
  - One way of chipping away at them is by using arcing projectiles, as it requires a direct line of sight to attack.
- Toxic Immunity does not prevent damage from poison and will not help combat Silthar Vosreth.

chunks.title: Ymrik Dumar
chunks.text:
Ymrik Dumar

name: Ymrik Dumar
spawn location: Overgrown Cavern
health: 40
traits: Explodes on death.
drops on death: Nothing

Ymrik Dumar (or Dumar Roamer) is an enemy only found in the Overgrown Cavern. They are tiny fungi with a pale beige cap.

## Behaviour

Ymrik Dumar are created from Bad Fungal Soil, which is a type of fungal powder released by the small green mushroom traps encountered in the Overgrown Cavern.

Ymrik Dumar are walking resonably quickly, though will ignore you if not in sight. If you get too close, they will jump at you from afar and violently explode. The explosion deals 125 damage and splatters their corpses of Weird Fungus around. Killing them has the same result.

## Combat Tips

- They explode on death, so engaging at a distance is recommended.

## Trivia

- They are not listed on the progress page, but can be polymorphed into using Chaotic Polymorphine. Dying while Polymorphed into Ymrik Dumar will show their name.

chunks.title: Rukhel Ymphis
chunks.text:
Rukhel Ymphis

name: Rukhel Ymphis
spawn location: Mines, Collapsed Mines, Underground Jungle, Ancient Laboratory
health: 125
traits: Cannot be set On Fire.Constantly emits small amounts of Water (Fading).
drops on death: 50

Rukhel Ymphis (also known as the Ymphis Sapper or the Shaman) is a rare enemy encountered in the Mines, Collapsed Mines, Underground Jungle and Ancient Laboratory. It casts Cursed Spheres that quickly accelerate towards you and bounce off of walls, dealing 15 damage as well as summoning the Rain Cloud or Thundercloud spell on contact.

This enemy is immune to fire.

## Combat Tips

- This enemy, while rare, can be dangerous to newer or less experienced players, much like the Morvek Halmar.
- Unlike the Morvek Halmar, it is fairly slow and not an aggressive chaser, so players should find it easier to choose when to fight it and take cover when it attacks.

## Trivia

- Its name is the Finnish word "märkiä" (verb: emitting pus), from the word "märkä" (adjective: wet, noun: pus). The suffix -inen can be translated as 'being or having something' in English, like with the Finnish words: karva, karvainen (hair, hairy) or tietää, tieto, tietoinen (to know, knowledge/information, conscious (of something)). The name also sounds similar to "mäkäräinen", which refers to insects living in wet areas.
- It appears to occasionally eat corpses, similar to Silthar Nakmar.
- The water that comes from its body is called water_fading in the code, and doesn't interact with Concentrated Mana.
- It will spawn more frequently with the "Flooded" biome modifier.

Mavrok Dravaska (also known as Dravaska Darter) is a unique enemy found in The Vault and Frozen Vault.

## Behavior

It begins by flinging Fireball projectiles at you, but when it is killed, it splits in two:

- Krel Ymvax (Rotting body) will move rather erratically while attacking with the same projectile.
- Ostrek Thalkoth (Rotting head) will come off and fly around, charging targets when close and exploding on death. This enemy seldom jumps and moves fairly quickly.

## Combat Tips

- As with other spawning enemies, explosives can be useful to destroy both the body and head at once.
- This enemy has a deceptive amount of health and a fairly small hitbox which makes hitting it difficult with projectiles such as that of the Energy Orb spell.

chunks.title: Quorin Ezhventh
chunks.text:
Quorin Ezhventh

name: Quorin Ezhventh
health: 8.75
drops on death: 10

Quorin Ezhventh (also known as Ezhventh Sentinel) is a small enemy that is spawned from Ymrik Vesmar when it receives damage. Sometimes Ymrik Vesmar can be damaged off screen which causes Quorin Ezhventh to spawn prior to your arrival.

## Behavior

These small blobs will often fly around and jump and/or dash in an erratic manner as well as dash at you to deal Melee damage. These movements can make them very annoying to deal with.

## Combat Tips

- Quorin Ezhventh can be hard to hit due to their small size and chaotic movement. Using larger projectiles can make hitting them easier.
  - Homing helps a lot when trying to land shots.
- As they are spawned in great quantities by the Ymrik Vesmar taking damage, and can be overwhelming in large numbers, it is advisable to deal with them as they spawn.
- AOE spells like Chain Bolt or Explosion are useful for dealing with large swarms.
- Since they can only attack you using melee damage, the Melee Immunity perk renders these enemies completely harmless.
  - The Contact Damage perk is also extremely useful against them, as they have low health and will immediately die when trying to lunge at you.

## Trivia

There are occasionally random nodes in a few biomes where Quorin Ezhventh will spawn directly on top of each other in batches (of ~8). Once the allotment of one batch has been killed off, another batch will be able to spawn. Leave the area of the node (a bit out of view), and the next batch will spawn when the node is revisited. After killing off several batches, the node will be depleted and spawn no more.

These nodes have been observed in Frozen Vault, Overgrown Cavern, and possibly The Vault. If you locate one, it can be a nice spot to farm some gold.

Belthar Ezhvax

Belthar Ezhvax (or Ezhvax Sentinel) is a large mushroom-like creature with a tall beige body and a large pink cap mostly found in the Fungal Caverns.

They can also appear in special fungal pits in the Mines among other locations.

## Behaviour

Belthar Ezhvax walk on the ground with average speed. They are mostly wandering around aimlessly unless the player gets too close to it. Belthar Ezhvax will then lunge at the player or other nefarious creatures nearby, violently exploding upon contact.

They bleed Fungus Blood when shot and explode on death, splattering their corpses of Weird Fungus in all directions.

## Combat Tips

- Keep your distance when fighting them, as the explosion from their death is very damaging.
- They are especially vulnerable to Fire.

Silthar Halvax

spawn location: Snowy Chasm, Pyramid
ngplus spawn location: Cloudscape
health: 387.5
traits: Can go through solids and liquids. Invisible unless close to a Paha Silmä.

Silthar Halvax (or Non-Existent) is an uncommon enemy found in the Snowy Chasm, and rarely in the Pyramid and Cloudscape. It resembles a translucent skull with huge white eyes and teeth. This ghostly enemy is unusual in that it can only be seen and harmed when it is close to a Paha Silmä. In the absence of the item, it will just float around as a hardly visible group of blue particles, dealing small amounts of Curse damage to you.

## Behaviour

When visible, it will attempt to get close and deal rapid Curse or "Ymventh Minderly Touch" damage. In order to kill it you will have to drop the Paha Silmä down nearby, and then use a spell which deals Slice or Explosion damage.

chunks.title: Halvox Ymkoth
chunks.text:
Halvox Ymkoth

name: Halvox Ymkoth
spawn location: Treasure Chest
health: 75

Halvox Ymkoth (or Ymkoth Marksman, lit. Memory of an evil thing), also known as the Heart Mavventh Trapper is an extremely rare mimic enemy, that uses its resemblance to a Extra Max Health pickup to lure in players and bite them, dealing 30–40 damage.

There is a 0.1089% chance of finding them in a Treasure Chest.

## Tips

- The Heart Mavventh Trapper has two possible sprites; one with the plus symbol to the right of the heart (identical to a normal health pickup), and one with the symbol to the left side. If you see a heart with the latter sprite, you can be certain that you've found a Mavventh Trapper.
  - Additionally, hovering your mouse over a real extra max health pickup will display "Extra max health" or "Large extra max health" as its material. Hovering the mouse over a mimic does not show anything, similar to the Rukhel Mavventh.
  - The Enemy Radar perk will detect Heart Mavventh Trappers, and the Item Radar perk will detect real hearts.
- Pahan Muisto (And Vessin Kesmar) have the same script as Rukhel Mavventh for spawning items when charmed. However, because they cannot be stained, this script cannot be activated without modding or cheating.

chunks.title: Sarnel Zenvia
chunks.text:
Sarnel Zenvia

name: Sarnel Zenvia
spawn location: Snowy Depths, Frozen Vault, Wizards' Den, Snowy Chasm, Snowy Wasteland, The Tower
health: 125
drops on death: 50

Sarnel Zenvia (or Zenvia Stalker) is a humanoid ice elemental, similar to Drazen Krelvaska. It is found naturally in cold underground areas, such as the Snowy Chasm. It launches a swift Iceball as a form of attack, which leaves behind damaging Freezing Liquid, and solidifies liquids in an aura around itself.

## Behaviour

Sarnel Zenvia walk on the ground but can also levitate and move in the air freely. They emit an aura that freezes liquids in a circular region around themselves.

When Sarnel Zenvia spot you, they attack by throwing a big Iceball at you, similar to Morvek Halmar's attacks. The Iceball will freeze you solid if you are hit directly, causing the Frozen effect, making you unable to move or use wands for a short period. When the Iceball expires or hits an object, it explodes in a ball of Freezing Liquid, which almost instantly turns into an icy cloud of Freezing Vapour.

When damaged, they bleed Snow and their corpses are made of Ice powder.

## Combat Tips

- Heals from Ice damage. Vulnerable to Fire damage, though it cannot be set On Fire.
- The further away you are, the easier to dodge their relatively slow attacks.
  - Getting hit is very dangerous since it will make you Frozen and unable to move, making you an easy target for any enemies around.
- Take it out quickly, because their shots produce Freezing Vapour which quickly accumulates.
  - Don't fight it from above, as the Freezing Vapour floats upwards.

## Trivia

- Sarnel Zenvia could also be translated as "Father Frost", which refers to a character from a fairy tale, the being that brings Winter each year.

chunks.title: Kavrik Sarsha
chunks.text:
Kavrik Sarsha

name: Kavrik Sarsha
spawn location: Ancient Laboratory, Magical Temple, Temple of the Art, Wizards' Den, Desert Chasm, The Tower
health: Normal175, Temple of the Art475
drops on death: 70

Kavrik Sarsha (or Sarsha Stalker) is one of the many master spellcasters. It takes the appearance of a humanoid with dark teal skin and a circular, ultramarine mirror-like head, and is dressed in an indigo robe and cape with a cyan trim. Its body is made of ethereal meat.

## Behavior

Initially, the Sarsha Stalker will cast a weak Iceball spell. Once a spell is cast close to it, it will copy that spell and cast it instead. Depending on the spell, this Master can be completely harmless or incredibly dangerous. The Master's casts ignore the Cast Delay, Recharge Delay, and any special modifiers applied to the spells it copies and will always cast at regular intervals. Almost any spell can be copied, including the spells of nearby enemies like Naktoi Varvia and Kavrik Dukoth.

chunks.title: Kavrik Sarsha
chunks.text:
Kavrik Sarsha

## Combat Tips

- As with all Masters, exercise caution and focus on avoiding the projectiles. This is easily done by constantly moving perpendicular to the enemy's aiming trajectory (which usually means levitating up or falling down) and staying at a medium distance.
- You can take advantage of the copying in some situations:
  - The master's set cast interval means that it's often much safer to fight against it using wands that specialize in rapid-fire damage, or high numbers of projectiles. Further compounding this, when it attempts to copy any spell that normally would fire multiple projectiles at once, such as Triplicate Bolt, it can only fire one - in the case of Triplicate Bolt, it only fires one of the 5 damage pellets the spell would normally cast.
  - Spells with low range, like Luminous Drill and Chainsaw, can limit its effective range. However, the spell must be cast near the Master, which can be risky.
  - Healing Bolt can be copied and will Heal you. As the Master is not limited by use limits, it can act as a source of limitless healing.
  - Harmless spells, like Blood Mist and Teleport Bolt, can neutralize the Master until it copies another spell.
  - Halreth Herder projectiles can be copied and fired quicker, making the Heartache trick more effective at high HP.

chunks.title: Grevan Duvia
chunks.text:
Grevan Duvia

name: Grevan Duvia
spawn location: Nakghor Base, Underground Jungle, The Vault, Sandcave, Frozen Vault, The Tower
health: Normal17.5, Underground Jungle50
drops on death: 10 Normal20 Underground Jungle

Grevan Duvia (also known as Duvia Brooder, Healer, Medic, or Pinky) is a weak enemy with a healing gun that restores the HP of its allies. Each shot restores +5.

If you are not trying to get healed, and do not have consistent damage, Grevan Duvia should be dispatched quickly to avoid potential one-sided fights, especially on levels like Nakghor Base, where other healers may assist the same Nakghor.

## Behavior

Healers tend to follow other Nakghor around and shoot healing projectiles at any of them who get damaged. They will actively try to follow their allies but if alone they'll stick around you instead. They have no damaging attack and cannot hurt you.

Healers that pick up a wand will immediately target any allies with the wand.

chunks.title: Grevan Duvia
chunks.text:
Grevan Duvia

## Getting Healed

There are multiple ways to make the Duvia Brooder heal you:

- They can be Charmed with Pheromone. This will make them part of your faction and cause them to see you as an ally, thus making them heal you. Note, however, that this will make other enemies attack them.
- Stand between a healer and its target, intercepting the healing bolts. The easiest targets to place yourself in front of are:
  - Other healers, which you can kick for low damage to trigger them to shoot each other.
  - An enemy holding a wand with Blood Magic and a spell with 0 casts remaining
  - Varvax Shambler from Holy Mountains or the shops to the sides of the Nakghor Base.
  - Halvox Kolqir (the stationary Kolqir Striker).
  - Thalvaska Shamblercoy or transmuted projectiles.
- Nakghor healers will sometime stop following you and wander off even when there are no other enemies around. In this situation, Homebringer Teleport Bolts can be helpful for gathering healers so you can kick them to initiate healing.

## Trivia

- Grevan Duvia have some biome-specific variants. In the Underground Jungle, their max HP is increased to 50. In The Vault, their max HP remains the same, but they gain knockback resistance.
- They are sometimes referred to as "pinky" or "medics".

## See Also

- Korjausdrone
- Healing

chunks.title: Halvox Nakphis
chunks.text:
Halvox Nakphis

name: Halvox Nakphis
spawn location: Ancient Laboratory, The Tower
health: 175
drops on death: 70

Halvox Nakphis (or Nakphis Trapper) is an enemy that appears mainly in the Ancient Laboratory, and sometimes in The Tower. It is initially generated as a static trap, which is then triggered when you are within close proximity to it. When you wander too close by, the trap will trigger, activating the statue. Trapped statues can be difficult to distinguish from static decorative statues.

## Behavior

Trapped Nakphis Trappers appear in the Ancient Laboratory alongside similar statues that are more decorative and cannot chase after you. These can be distinguished in a few ways:

- Trapped statues only have one pose (see below), although some of the decorative statues share this pose.
- Trapped statues do not show a material tooltip; decorative statues will indicate they are composed of Rock.
- Decorative statues can be damaged and destroyed with explosions or digging spells, but trapped statues are unfazed.

When you approach a trapped statue, it will come to life and pursue you, attempting to kick you repeatedly. Living Nakphis Trappers are immune to most damage types, with the exceptions of Melee and Kinetic damage.

chunks.title: Halvox Nakphis
chunks.text:
Halvox Nakphis

## Combat Tips

chunks.title: Halvox Nakphis
chunks.text:
Halvox Nakphis

- There is a method to easily turn this enemy into an ally without Pheromone. If you are stained with Berserkium or have the respective effect, the statue will not target you and ignore you, going after any other nearby enemy instead. Because other enemies' projectiles can't hurt the statue, it's very useful for underprepared players to clear out the area for them without the danger of being attacked, as Berserkium pools are commonly found in the Ancient Laboratory.
  - However, the statue will still kick you if you get close enough.
- It is generally better to avoid triggering the trapped statues as much as possible. If one awakens it can usually be outrun fairly easily, as they move slightly slower than you.
  - However, throwing an Emerald Tablet at it as soon as it awakens may result in the statue being killed immediately, nullifying the risk - and providing a hefty amount of gold.
- They can be fought off simply with kicking attacks, although timing a kick to hit them can be tricky as they will often land a hit that stuns you for a brief moment

chunks.title: Halvox Nakphis
chunks.text:
Halvox Nakphis

. The Never Skip Leg Day perk is highly recommended for this method.
- The only ways to damage them are melee attacks, physics hits, Curse damage (Venomous Curse), Toxic damage (Toxic mist), Giga Black Hole and Omega Black Hole, and spells that deal Drill damage (this is only used by Digging Bolt and Digging Blast; however, Digging Blast cannot hit entities without a special tag which no enemy in Thalvia has, so Digging Blast won't be able to damage it).
- Despite not taking any Ice damage, Nakphis Trappers can be dispatched quite effectively with a freeze-melee combo, such as the Freeze Charge modifier combined with Tentacle or Summon Morvia Marauderly Fly (or any Summon spells that spawn a minion which can inflict Melee damage). Alternatively, kicking the statue could work - especially when you have the Never Skip Leg Day perk - but is not advised because the statue could thaw and attack you before you kick it.
- Since they are vulnerable to Kinetic damage, a combination of Summon Rock and Burst of Air is very effective in dispatching them at range. You can also try launching a Propane Vesreth Sifter at them from a distance which can deal a considerable amount of damage, should it hit the statue. You can also kick a decorative statue into it if one is nearby, or direct hits with a thrown Emerald Tablet are also an effective and relatively safe way of killing them.
  - The physics damage methods are also strongly recommended as they will be classified as trick kills and double the amount of gold dropped by the statue.

Vorak Ithqir (or Ithqir Trapper) is a large robotic sentry mainly found in The Vault, and occasionally in the Underground Jungle and the Cloudscape. It has a thrown lance attack that deals heavy Holy damage and extreme knockback, which can send you flying several screens away unless stopped by terrain.

## Behaviour & Combat

Like other robotic enemies, it is heavily armored and resistant to most attacks. Due to its large size, it has a problem fitting into tight spaces and can usually be shaken off rather easily by fleeing. If it sees you, it will give chase and throw its lance from medium range (about half a screen). If it takes a lot of damage at once, it may flee.

Unlike other robotic enemies, it is completely immune to explosions. Combined with its natural resistances as a robotic enemy, this makes it extremely resistant to damage, being primarily vulnerable only to Electricity damage.

Projectiles that deal a lot of damage in a single hit are preferable to fast-firing low damage wands due to its naturally high resistances. Lightning Bolt's range is a little low and its main damage source is explosive rather than electrical, so it will be less effective than normal, but can do the job if you can land enough hits. If you must use a fast-firing wand, consider adding Electric Charge for additional damage and the added Stunned effect. Keep your distance as much as possible and watch for their throwing animation to avoid getting hit with their lance attack. Melee combat is not recommended.

Belthar Ezhphis (also known as Ezhphis Stalker) is a Nakghor wearing a beige coat with a spiky hood that throws potions. It can be encountered rarely in several of the early biomes.

chunks.title: Belthar Ezhphis
chunks.text:
Belthar Ezhphis

## Behavior

Belthar Ezhphis walk around slowly and may jump. They cannot swim, but are immune to suffocation. Notably, they are not hurt by Lava.

When in range, they randomly throw potions of various contents directly at your current location. Belthar Ezhphis will continue throwing potions until there are 15 of their potions nearby. Only breaking the potions will allow them to attack again.

### Bottles

The potion bottles thrown by Belthar Ezhphis have only half the capacity of regular flasks. Initially, they contain 200% of their capacity, which is equal to the amount of a full regular potion. They can only be refilled up to 100%, half the amount of a regular potion.

Due to being overfilled, these potion bottles will spray their contents further than a regular potion for as long as they are more than 100% full.

### Contents

Many of the potion bottles contain dangerous materials that can kill you. The potions tend to have alchemic reactions with each other, creating massive amounts of fire, freezing vapour, and even walls of rock when lava and water connect.

Belthar Ezhphis can throw potions containing anything in the Aggressive material list.

Potion types

| Acid | Blood | Fire |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Freezing Liquid | Gunpowder | Lava |
| Oil | Toxic Sludge | Slime |
| Water | Whiskey | Berserkium |
| Pheromone | Teleportatium | |

chunks.title: Belthar Ezhphis
chunks.text:
Belthar Ezhphis

## Tips

- Belthar Ezhphis can be used to gain potions that you cannot make on your own. A somewhat reliable way to collect their potions is to have them throw the potions at you while you (and/or they) are submerged in deep water or other liquid, as sufficient amounts of liquid will slow the potions down enough to prevent them breaking. You can also simply catch the potion in the air as it flies towards you, but this is risky as some of the materials can kill you instantly if your timing is slightly off.
- Potentially desirable potions include:
  - Teleportatium, for use in The Hourglass Chamber.
  - Pheromone, for healing with Grevan Duvia.
  - Whiskey, for activating the Nullification Altar.
  - Berserkium, for its damage buff effect.
  - The rare potions with highly dangerous materials such as Acid and Lava, for fungal shifting them into something safer. Can also be used as a single use projectile against difficult enemies.
- Extra care should be taken when disposing of unwanted potion bottles; if dragged and dropped from the inventory to throw away and you are moving with a similar speed and direction, the bottles may immediately collide with you and break. (Low velocity throws, or throwing via right clicking, don't have this behavior.)
- They will often kill themselves with the potions they throw. These will be a trick kill, however take extra caution to avoid any residual dangerous liquids the gold nuggets could be lying in.

## Trivia

- The randomness of the thrown potions is determined by both the (x,y) coordinates of Belthar Ezhphis and the current game frame number. Hence, it is infeasible to use a seed tool to predict the order in which potions will be thrown.

Ostrek Grevaska (or the Grevaska Marauder) is a Nakghor that spawns in Nakghor Base, Underground Jungle, and The Vault, often in tandem with other enemies in the Nakghor faction.

## Behavior

The Grevaska Marauder does not have any attacks that can directly harm you. Instead, it flies around, following you, and firing projectiles that teleports a nearby enemy to the projectile's location. The projectiles it fires can also destroy weak materials.

The Grevaska Marauder also has a protective shield around it.

It has a very low aggression stat, and a single stack of More Love will be enough to make them neutral to you.

## Combat

Ostrek Grevaska will not attack you directly and poses seemingly no harm while no other enemies are nearby. However, it remains a fairly high-priority target as it can relocate enemies from completely unconnected rooms, quickly increasing the number of enemies in the vicinity that must be dealt with.

Its shield works similarly to the Permanent Shield perk, in that it can be defeated with sustained fire, so a fast-firing wand or explosives can be effective. Attacking it with a tablet or other physics object is also effective.

## Trivia

- In Finnish, the word "raukka" also refers to a draugr, an undead creature from scandinavian folktale.

Orune Morghor (also known as Morghor Marksman) is a dangerous bipedal robotic enemy which spawns in the Fungal Caverns and The Vault.

## Behaviour & Combat

This is a slow and low mobility machine, and doesn't chase well after you. However, their rapid fire gun shots can quickly pin you down by stunning and deactivating levitation mid-air. Digging around an aggressive Orune Morghor if you are scared of becoming stunlocked is a good idea.

They are heavily armored and can take quite a beating before dying. Slice, Fire, and Projectile damage will be ineffective, but Electricity and Explosion damage works well. Even a lowly Firebolt can cut it down with a few well aimed hits, and if in contact with water, a source of electricity (such as a Thunderstone) or Concentrated Mana can quickly end it.

## Trivia

Naktoi Orphis

Naktoi Orphis (or Orphis Skulker) is a flying enemy commonly encountered in a variety of biomes. You will usually first see them in the Snowy Depths.

## Behavior

Orphis Skulkers hover slowly with their jetpacks and have a pistol. They are often seen in small groups accompanying Grenadier Nakghor, or accompanying a Kolvax Stinger. If shot while hovering, they will sometimes be knocked out of the air. The Orphis Skulkers fire alarmingly accurate bullets in quick bursts at you. Their shots arc slightly as they fly but still have enough range to hit you from off-screen. Their attacks deal 4 damage and temporarily disable levitation.

## Compat Tips

- Keep cool if you get hit. Their shots deal only 4 damage and aren't rapid enough to stun you constantly like those of the Naktoi Vesreth.
- The real danger of Orphis Skulkers comes from plummeting to the ground if hit by their accurate shots.
  - Do not hover over dangerous materials such as toxic sludge or burning oil when engaging in combat.
  - Do not hover over pits as falling down may land you in a precarious situation with many other creatures around.
- Their weakness is not being able to shoot vertically up or downwards, making them vulnerable to attacks from those directions.
  - Run behind cover and hide in a slightly elevated or lowered position for them to follow you. Once they're in line of sight quickly take them out.
  - If attacking from below, keep in mind that they will drop down, potentially landing on top of you.

Sarnel Halqir (or Halqir Shambler) is a bipedal robotic enemy often encountered in The Vault and Frozen Vault. It is also found in Fungal Caverns very rarely.

## Behavior

It has a forward-facing shield that protects it well against projectiles, but as with other shields it cannot stand sustained fire, powerful spells, or physical objects.

It follows you around continuously, and will quickly spring forward to attack if close enough, slashing repeatedly with its sword.

## Combat Tips

- It has very high health which makes it a force to be reckoned with.
- They are relatively slow when not attacking, so barring a very strong wand, running from them is a good option early on.
- Its only method of attack is through Melee damage, so the Melee Immunity perk will render them harmless.
- It is easy to get overwhelmed if you get attacked by it in combination with a projectile enemy, so try to fight it alone.
- Similar to other robots, it takes high damage from Electricity, and has no resistance to Explosion damage, making these the best damage types to use by a wide margin.

Zentha Ymnok (or Ymnok Weaver, also known as bridge boss, pit boss, Squidward, or wand boss) is a flying miniboss that is found in the chasm east of the Lava Lake. It will only appear after you have passed through the middle section of the nearby Orb Room, and then return to the chasm, after which the Connoisseur will spawn underneath the bridge. It is possible to enter and exit the orb room in ways that prevent it from appearing, such as by becoming Invisible.

The Ymnok Weaver is also spawned by Monstrous Powder.

chunks.title: Zentha Ymnok
chunks.text:
Zentha Ymnok

## Behaviour

The Ymnok Weaver is arguably the single most dangerous enemy in the entire game. It attacks using a wide variety of spells, some of which inflict Polymorph, Blinded, Neutralized spells, or Teleportitis. It also summons floating wands that cast one of several random spells.

It is resistant to most types of damage and nearly every status effect. It is capable of digging through all terrain using its body, in a similar manner to that of the Krel Ostnok. Once it starts chasing you, it is quite persistent and will not stop until you run far enough away.

It may erase a large circular area of blocks around itself as soon as its pathfinding fails to find a valid path to the player.

### Attacks

- An all-around blast of many Polymorphing projectiles, which home and accelerate towards you. Being hit by one of these projectiles while already Polymorphed will instantly kill you, as with any other attack.
- An all-around blast of many Blinding projectiles, similar to those fired by the Halvox Kavkoth, making you temporarily Blinded.
- An all-around blast of many wand-disabling projectiles, similar to those fired by the Sarnel Halvaska, giving the Neutralized spells status.
- An all-around blast of many Teleporting projectiles, similar to those fired by the Belthar Morventh, giving you Teleportitis.
- Spawns a random wand, which fires at you several times before disappearing. This wand can fire one of several randomly chosen spells; any of the Magic Missile variants, any of the Firebolt variants, and Bouncing Burst. The fire rate of the wand depends on the spell it uses, firing weaker spells faster, and firing stronger spells slower. This wand can also copy spells.

chunks.title: Zentha Ymnok
chunks.text:
Zentha Ymnok

These attacks are set to a 400 frame timer (~6.7 seconds); one of the projectile blast attacks is randomly chosen after 40 frames, then a wand is spawned after a further 240 frames, with 120 frames left before the cycle resets. Due to this, the projectile blast will happen ~2.67 seconds after a wand spawn, which will happen 4 seconds after the projectile blast.

### Diminishing damage protection

The Ymnok Weaver starts with a 0.1 damage multiplier on its hitbox. Every 40 frames (~0.6 seconds) it will add 0.35 to that damage multiplier, until it reaches 1.0 after 120 frames (2 seconds).

Whenever the Wand Connoisseur takes damage it sets that multiplier back to 0, so then after 40 frames it becomes 0.35 and you can damage it again. After another 40 frames it becomes 0.7 and then after another 40 frames it becomes 1.0 again. Any damage during that recovery will set the multiplier back to 0 again. Some things ignore that damage multiplier and will deal damage regardless (for ex. Plasma Beam/Plasma Beam Cross/Plasma Cutter).

That interaction is the main reason why rapid-fire / rapid-damage-dealing builds as well as trigger-payload builds aren't great against this boss. If the trigger deals damage, the damage multiplier will be 0 on the frame that the payload is supposed to hit The Connoisseur.

chunks.title: Zentha Ymnok
chunks.text:
Zentha Ymnok

## Rewards

Upon being defeated for the first time, the Ymnok Weaver will disintegrate, drop two wands, tier 5 non-shuffle and a tier 6, and a Full Health Regeneration. On following kills it will no longer drop the Full Heal. Additionally, it will drop two destructive unlockable spells, Belthar Ernqirsade and Meteorisade, which will be permanently unlocked for you.

chunks.title: Zentha Ymnok
chunks.text:
Zentha Ymnok

## Combat Tips

chunks.title: Zentha Ymnok
chunks.text:
Zentha Ymnok

- Make generous use of cover; the amount of spells it puts out make it very hard to simply dodge its projectiles, even from far away, and you will most importantly want to avoid getting Polymorphed. Move to another piece of cover quickly if your current shelter is destroyed.
  - The Snowy Depths, with its multiple sections of disconnected terrain, is an ideal battleground for this. Just be sure to clear out the biome of enemies beforehand.
  - If you are capable of using the spell often, Black Hole can be used to create cover on demand. This can be especially effective when done through Extremely Dense Rock, as the Connoisseur's explosive attacks will not be able to destroy this cover. However, it will still be able to burrow through the rock with its body.
- Due to the shield it will summon upon being hit, it is advised to fight it with a slower, higher damage-per-hit wand, as opposed to the more popular rapid fire wands. Spells To Power in combination with any spell that casts many projectiles, such as Square Barrier, is extremely effective, however, it takes almost no damage from Spells To Power with Freezing Gaze. It is also immune to Freezing, so it cannot be instantly killed by any melee attacks.
  - Damage Field ignores its shield, offering an alternative way to fight it.
- Staining yourself with Berserkium, or going Invisible through Invisiblium or the Invisibility perk, will make the Ymnok Weaver stop approaching you but its summoned wands will still target you.
- It summons more wands to retaliate against taking damage

chunks.title: Zentha Ymnok
chunks.text:
Zentha Ymnok

. Attacks that rapidly hit it, such as Damage Field, will turn the fight into a bullet hell; if you don't have Ambrosia to prevent damage or the Teleport Bolt spell for easy getaways, this will certainly lead to your death.
- The Projectile Repulsion Field perk is borderline necessary for fighting the Connoisseur if you can't get to cover quickly. Getting hit by any of its Polymorphing or Blinding blasts is almost guaranteed to result in the end of the run - this perk, preferably in combination with the Permanent Shield perk or the Energy Shield spell, will make those attacks much easier to avoid.
- The Personal Gravity Field spell can be used to cause all but the fastest projectiles, mainly those fired from its wands, to stick around and orbit the boss. This renders the boss's Polymorph, Blinding and Silence attacks almost harmless. Depending on the loadout of its wands this can also make it deal massive damage to itself. While wands that always cast Personal Gravity Field can be found, this is very rare, and it is more efficient to use some variation of Greek Letters such as Alpha or Omega to make the spell unlimited. Alternatively, you can use a Note spell based wand to cast it for free.
- Due to the wands it summons occasionally copying spells used against it, self harming spells such as Omega Disk Projectile, Omega Black Hole and Plasma Beam can be very effective against it.
- It can hurt itself with its own explosions from its Magic Missile and Firebolt attacks

chunks.title: Zentha Ymnok
chunks.text:
Zentha Ymnok

. It's possible to lure it next to terrain and wait for it injure itself with its attacks, although its tendency to eat through terrain can make setting such a trap somewhat difficult.
  - An Emerald Tablet can provide a useful and sturdy obstacle to detonate the spells close to it, but it will sometimes destroy the tablet just like the surrounding terrain. See Old Exploit below.
  - Well-timed usage of Explosive Detonator can also be effective.

Zentha Ymnok

Sauvojen Tuntija will only spawn if the player passes back through the entrance to the Orb Room after passing above the Orb pedestal within, as shown in the diagram. The boss will not spawn if the player…

- …avoids these trigger areas by digging through the surrounding Extremely Dense Rock and Brickwork, or through the softer materials of the ceiling.
