Belthar Morventh (or Morventh Stinger) is one of the many master spellcasters. It takes the appearance of a humanoid with brown skin and an animal head (potentially that of a dog), and is dressed in a green robe and cape with a tan trim. Its body is made of Ethereal Meat.

## Behaviour

The Morventh Stinger casts small blue orbs which inflict the Teleportitis status effect for 20 seconds that functions identically to Teleportatium. The projectile is rather fast, with slight homing ability, so it can be hard to dodge if you aren't immediately aware of its presence. If you are struck with it, you will teleport to the direction of cursor (or randomly, if impossible) 2-3 times before stopping, which can be incredibly dangerous due to the possibility of relocating into other enemies like Rukhel Greventh and Orune Morghor, or into dangerous liquids like Lava or Acid. The Master itself is permanently stained with the Teleportatium effect, which may result in it disappearing mid-battle, only to encounter the same one again in a different location. It also may relocate into neighboring biomes, such as into the Coal Pits or Underground Jungle.

chunks.title: Belthar Morventh
chunks.text:
Belthar Morventh

## Combat Tips

- As with all Masters, exercise caution and focus on avoiding the projectiles. This is easily done by constantly moving perpendicular to the enemy's aiming trajectory (which usually means levitating up or falling down) and staying at a medium distance.
- If get hit by projectile in coal pits, point to the right for more safety, to not encounter Fungal Caverns enemies like Rukhel Greventh and Orune Morghor.
- As it bleeds Teleportatium, attacking with a short range/melee spell (such as Chainsaw) is generally unadvised.
- This Mage becomes especially dangerous once it finds a wand. Due to the mage's teleporting nature, it may show up from seemingly nowhere to surprise you.

chunks.title: Thalven Mavphis
chunks.text:
Thalven Mavphis

name: Thalven Mavphis
spawn location: Pyramid, Temple of the Art, Watchtower, Wizards' Den, Desert
health: 2.5
drops on death: Nothing

Thalven Mavphis (or Mavphis Howler) is a small, harmless animal which has little health, no attacks, and will be targeted by enemies.

chunks.title: Ymrik Varnok
chunks.text:
Ymrik Varnok

name: Ymrik Varnok
spawn location: Holy Mountain, The Tower
health: 900
traits: Will spawn if 3 Rukhel Ymqirs are killed.Has two large protective shields that deflect moving projectiles.Dissolves nearby terrain.
drops on death: 360

Ymrik Varnok (lit. Varnok Trapper, sometimes referred to as Scott or Big Steve) is a significantly stronger variant of Rukhel Ymqir, which will spawn in its place in Holy Mountains after angering the gods if at least 3 Rukhel Ymqir have been killed already.

After killing 3 separate instances of Rukhel Ymqir (no matter where they spawned), you receive the message:

The gods are enraged

After this, all further Holy Mountains will instead spawn Ymrik Varnok. Additionally, further damaging Holy Mountain brickwork after this event will give the message:

The gods are very angry with you

chunks.title: Ymrik Varnok
chunks.text:
Ymrik Varnok

## Behaviour & Combat

Ymrik Varnok is significantly stronger than Rukhel Ymqir, with 900 HP and two layers of shielding. In addition, it is completely immune to all Frozen and electrical Stunned effects. Upon seeing you within a certain distance or when you move too close, Ymrik Varnok will become more aggressive and start dissolving all terrain around itself, including Holy Mountain brickwork and physics objects. As a result, landing a hit with an Emerald Tablet is generally quite difficult, but can be done by teleporting to the portal Ymrik Varnok emerges from before it spawns, and throwing the tablet.

Similarly to Rukhel Ymqir, Ymrik Varnok has a long range and a short range attack. At long range, Ymrik Varnok casts a pair of quickly accelerating explosive projectiles with slight homing, which explode into a spread of 12 bubbles on impact. At short range, it shoots out similar little sparks to Rukhel Ymqir, though they are more damaging than those used by Rukhel Ymqir.

### Tips

chunks.title: Ymrik Varnok
chunks.text:
Ymrik Varnok

- Protection from all from Ambrosia will keep you safe, but be cautious of Ymrik Varnok's terrain destruction capabilities.
- Any kind of Plasma Beam spell, especially with a Homing modifier, will be quite effective.
- A Homing modifier on a Rock can be effective, but Ymrik Varnok's terrain destruction can extend to physics bodies too if it's already chasing you. To avoid this, cast the rock before being seen, then stay out of sight.
- A Luminous Drill paired with either Ping-Pong Path or Increase Lifetime is a good choice because of its ability to pierce through Ymrik Varnok's shields.
- Ymrik Varnok will activate its matter-eating field and follow you even when you are Invisible, but will not attack.
- Since Ymrik Varnok bleeds solid Bone Dust, some wands built to hit multiple times with the same projectile will not work as well without a Drilling Shot modifier, as the projectiles hitting the dust is treated like hitting terrain.
- If you damage Ymrik Varnok before it has seen you, it will try to seek you out, but will not immediately trigger its aggressive matter-eating and path-finding behavior until its conditions are satisfied. If you block off paths for it to navigate to you beforehand, e.g., with Chunk of Soil or Sea of spells, you can often attack with impunity through walls without risk that it will find you due to this pre-matter-eating behavior. Completely flooding the area around Ymrik Varnok (with liquid and/or its own Bone Dust) will immobilize it in this early state, though it is easy to accidentally venture too close and trigger the matter-eating state if not attacking through walls

chunks.title: Ymrik Varnok
chunks.text:
Ymrik Varnok

. If using Sea of Mavventh Trapperium for this type of purpose, make sure it is converted to water first, as lamps breaking may turn the Mavventh Trapperium into Magical Liquid, which rapidly evaporates.
- Taking the Peace with Gods perk will stop Ymrik Varnok from spawning, just like Rukhel Ymqir, but any existing Ymrik Varnok will become Charmed making a powerful ally.
- Ymrik Varnok can be avoided entirely by either not killing a third Rukhel Ymqir instead leaving any future Rukhel Ymqir alive.
- Rukhel Ymqir killed while Polymorphed will not increase the Rukhel Ymqir kill counter, allowing Ymrik Varnok to be avoided.

chunks.title: Ymrik Varnok
chunks.text:
Ymrik Varnok

## Trivia

- "Ymrik Varnok" is Helsinki slang for "cop".

chunks.title: Ymrik Vesventh
chunks.text:
Ymrik Vesventh

name: Ymrik Vesventh
spawn location: Snowy Depths, Nakghor Base, The Vault, The Tower
health: Snowy Depths45, The Vault155
drops on death: 10 Snowy Depths60 The Vault

Ymrik Vesventh (also known as Vesventh Drifter, or just Sniper) is a Nakghor equipped with a sniper rifle featuring a red laser sight. Their extremely high-velocity bullets can deal 25 damage to you, as well as massive knockback.

## Behavior

These Nakghor typically attack all other enemies, but will not attack other Nakghor. They use their signature sniper rifle, as well as have a Melee attack (10–17.5 damage).

Vesventh Drifters have an incredibly long target acquisition range, which they use in conjunction with their equally long-range weapons. Before firing, they always telegraph with a red laser sight first, though it is not always visible - any material will block the laser sight, even if it is something that their bullet could easily go through, such as powdery Snow or a thin layer of Ice. Furthermore, once they spot something, they will always have nigh-perfect aim, meaning that the laser sight is merely an optional courtesy for whatever they've targeted.

chunks.title: Ymrik Vesventh
chunks.text:
Ymrik Vesventh

## Combat Tips

- If you know that you're being targeted by a Sniper Nakghor, move perpendicularly to the laser sight the moment before the bullet reaches you.
  - Levitating normally or even falling like a rock will help you avoid the bullet. However, if you are too close, it may be completely impossible to avoid the bullet.
- Attacking a Sniper Nakghor will interrupt their own attack, forcing them to restart from the beginning.
- Although their bullet can go through snow easily, it cannot go through Frozen Rock - nor can the bullet get past other Nakghor. Earn accidental kills by moving the Sniper's laser sight into their friends.
- The sound of a Sniper's bullet notably changes as it slows down travelling through softer materials like snow.

## Notes

- The Sniper Nakghor can be seen aiming down its sight before firing.
- A pixel of brass is ejected when the Sniper Nakghor takes a shot, reminiscent of spent bullet casings.
- They are actually less dangerous in the Nakghor Base's narrow corridors than the wide chasms of the Snowy Depths.
- On August 24 they have a very small chance of spawning in an alternate form, replacing their regular attack with throwing urine jars instead, which is a reference of Jarate in Team Fortress 2.

chunks.title: Halvox Kavkoth
chunks.text:
Halvox Kavkoth

name: Halvox Kavkoth
spawn location: Fungal Caverns, Snowy Depths, The Vault, Temple of the Art, Wizards' Den, Desert Chasm, The Tower, Silthar Grephis Lair
ngplus spawn location: Collapsed Mines, Ancient Laboratory
health: Normal100, Temple of the Art350
drops on death: 40 Normal140 Temple of the Art

Halvox Kavkoth (or Kavkoth Herder) is one of the many master spellcasters. It takes the appearance of a humanoid with dark lavender skin, horns, and a hole instead of a face, and is dressed in a brown robe and cape with a mulberry trim. Its body is made of ambiguous meat.

## Behavior

The Kavkoth Herder casts homing, slow-moving purple magic orbs, which inflict the Blinded status effect for 20 seconds. While blinded, the screen will become completely dark, and you will only be able to see a small distance around yourself. However, glowing enemy parts, such as eyes, will still be visible. The blindness will leave you highly vulnerable, so extreme caution should be taken when fighting this Master.

## Combat Tips

- As with all Masters, exercise caution and focus on avoiding the projectiles. This is easily done by constantly moving perpendicular to the enemy's aiming trajectory (which usually means levitating up or falling down) and staying at a medium distance.

chunks.title: Naktoi Varvia
chunks.text:
Naktoi Varvia

name: Naktoi Varvia
spawn location: Pyramid, Magical Temple, Temple of the Art, Snowy Chasm, The Tower
health: Normal75, Temple of the Art300
drops on death: 30 Normal120 Temple of the Art

Naktoi Varvia (also known as Varvia Herder or Spiral of Death) is an enemy found in the Magical Temple and the Temple of the Art. It closely resembles the Kavrik Dukoth, with the only difference being its 'hair' and number of eyes.

## Behaviour

The Naktoi Varvia is a floating creature, passively patrolling the Magical Temple and Temple of the Art until it learns your location. Once it knows your whereabouts, it approaches until it has a clear line of sight, then shoots blue orbs which arc toward you.

The orb travels through the air at a somewhat slow speed and stops upon reaching a wall or object. Once it has stopped, it remains stuck to what it has hit for a few seconds. Along its flight, the orb sends out smaller blue orbs in a counter-clockwise fashion. This continues until the original orb disappears, then, the Naktoi Varvia sends another orb to continue its attack.

## Combat Tips

- Both this and the Kavrik Dukoths are similar in behavior and attack pattern, and as such many of the same strategies will work on both.
- This enemy is a slow flier, so you should be able to choose where you fight.
- Both the primary and secondary projectiles it fires are quite slow, but numerous. Use the corners and geography of the Temple of the Art and Magical Temple to reduce its area control.
  - The slow speed of the projectiles mean that the Projectile Repulsion Field perk will render this enemy practically unable to hurt you.

## See Also

- Kavrik Dukoth

chunks.title: Morvek Halmar
chunks.text:
Morvek Halmar

name: Morvek Halmar
spawn location: Mines, Collapsed Mines, Desert Chasm, Desert
health: 80
traits: Takes rapid damage when Wet.Becomes passive if holding a Kiuaskivi.
drops on death: 30

Morvek Halmar (also known as Halmar Prowler) is an enemy found in the Mines which shoots fireballs, bleeds lava, and is immune to Fire.

chunks.title: Morvek Halmar
chunks.text:
Morvek Halmar

## Behaviour

Morvek Halmar patrols around on foot, and while it cannot fly, it jumps quite high. Once in range, it fires a weaker version of the Fireball spell, exploding either on impact or when the fireball reaches its target location, being your position at the time of the attack. The fireball has a weak explosion that will damage solid material.

They are not harmed by fire and will cause nearby flammable materials, powders, and liquids to combust. Additionally, they bleed Lava, which can prove a highly threatening hazard, particularly in the early game where they are normally encountered. Solidifying the lava with water first can help in collecting their dropped gold, but be aware that the gold may be stuck beneath the rock that forms.

Water, and a few other materials, do considerable damage to the Morvek Halmar, and immersion quickly proves fatal. They will avoid deep water to the best of their ability, but may overlook small puddles, which still damage them. Also, if the water is below a liquid harmless to Morvek Halmar, they will not avoid it. Morvek Halmar interestingly does not avoid Toxic Sludge, which you can convert into water easily. Harmful materials include: Water, Mud, Brine, Swamp, Snow, and Ice, as well as all the regular harmful materials, with the exception of Lava. These include: Acid, Poison, Freezing Liquid, and Freezing Vapor. They will not bleed if damaged by materials.

If you are holding a Kiuaskivi, Morvek Halmar will become peaceful.

chunks.title: Morvek Halmar
chunks.text:
Morvek Halmar

## Combat Tips

- Morvek Halmar is one of the most dangerous enemies that spawns normally in the Mines, especially to new players.
- It will often jump towards you and shoot at the same time, which can throw you off when trying to dodge its attacks.
- Make sure you are doused in a fire-proof liquid. Even if you manage to not get hit, the frequent fire particles generated by fighting it will likely dry you off and set you On Fire.
- Wands with the Rain Cloud spell are often found in the Mines, which are convenient for killing it with water.
- You can douse a Morvek Halmar with a Water (or Swamp, Brine, etc.) Potion by dropping the liquid from above, but also by pouring it into the ground the Morvek Halmar is standing on, from below, which will cause Thalvia to spawn the sprayed liquid above at the nearest open space, in this case, right underneath the Morvek Halmar.
  - Killing them with water also counts as an accidental kill, dropping double gold. This can be a useful way to get gold early game if you're willing to take the risk.

## Trivia

- Morvek Halmar is a Finnish slang word for a lighter.
- Etymology from Swedish word Tändare.

## See Also

- Drazen Krelvaska
- Halvox Ymmar

chunks.title: Rukhel Ymqir
chunks.text:
Rukhel Ymqir

name: Rukhel Ymqir
spawn location: Holy Mountain, The Tower
ngplus2 spawn location: Temple of the Art
health: 600
traits: Will spawn if the gods are angered.Has a large protective shield that deflects moving projectiles.
drops on death: 240

Rukhel Ymqir (translation: "Ymqir Lurker") is a dangerous flying skeletal enemy which spawns in response to the Holy Mountain being damaged.

Rukhel Ymqir has 600 and high knockback, and is among the highest damage dealers that can be encountered on the Main Path of progression. He is often referred to as "Steve" by the community, or "Mall Varnok Trapper" as he can be cheesed with relatively simple methods.

The destruction of any "protected" Brickwork, located on a set of lines encapsulating the inner Holy Mountain, will trigger the following message:

You have angered the gods

The source of this damage is not tracked and is thus irrelevant as to how it came about. Whether it be directly caused by Minä, environmental hazards, or a stray worm; the outcome is the same. You will receive the same message, and a Rukhel Ymqir will be spawned in the perk chamber to hunt you down.

The message is triggered only when specific pixels are broken/replaced in a Holy Mountain. There is a buffer between the play area and the trigger to prevent the Holy Mountain from being too fragile.

After the message, Rukhel Ymqir will summon and, even if defeated, will appear in other uncollapsed Holy Mountains upon your arrival.

## Spawning

There are 4 main ways a Rukhel Ymqir can be encountered:

- Damaging the Holy Mountain
- Chaotic Polymorph into Rukhel Ymqir
- Spawning in SPOILER: The Tower
- Casting SPOILER: The End of Everything

chunks.title: Rukhel Ymqir
chunks.text:
Rukhel Ymqir

## Behaviour

The Rukhel Ymqir has a powerful, accelerating long-range explosive attack, as well as a short-range bubble attack. While the individual attacks are damaging, it is not that much (many enemies exist that do much more). Instead the danger comes from the incredible knockback of the former that can easily throw you around the temple making combat against it much more difficult, and the rapid fire ability of the latter. Since it also comes with a powerful version of the Energy Shield, it is also difficult to even hit in the first place. Additionally, both of the projectiles experience homing. This homing is weak enough that it doesn't pose a huge threat, but it should be noted regardless.

Upon taking direct damage, it bleeds Bone Dust powder. Upon death, it drops an impressive number of gold nuggets.

Killing 3 Rukhel Ymqir will cause the Holy Mountains to start spawning Ymrik Varnok instead of Rukhel Ymqir, and you receive the message:

The gods are enraged

chunks.title: Rukhel Ymqir
chunks.text:
Rukhel Ymqir

## Combat Tips

chunks.title: Rukhel Ymqir
chunks.text:
Rukhel Ymqir

- Both of its ranged attacks can be surprisingly easy to dodge so long as you continue moving vertically.
- This enemy has hit points in the hundreds. It is highly recommended to either run away with a Teleport Spell or similar, or to use your nastiest tricks to defeat it. Chain Bolt and Plasma Beam are very effective since they can pierce its projectile shield.
- Using Protection from all from Ambrosia makes you block damage so you can attack while standing in place (since the effect wears off extremely fast when moving or falling).
- Silthar Grephis Minion perk is useful.
- When exiting a Holy Mountain, the exit will collapse from a small-scale Earthquake. The falling debris may actually trap this enemy and deal massive damage. Should this finish it off, don't be tempted by the gold: you must still watch out for the highly damaging red 'desecrated' particles that linger for some time after the collapse occurs. See the Holy Mountain page for more details.
- Projectile Repulsion Field is very useful against Rukhel Ymqir's projectiles. Standing right next to him will make all of his projectiles fly away from you, even the accelerating bolt, since it starts off pretty slow. You can then take your time to kill him.
- Can be easily killed using Freeze Charge, Freezing Gaze, or Circle of Stillness and then kicking it while frozen.
- Vulnerable to the Chainsaw and Luminous Drill spells due to their rapid fire and shield piercing ability. After getting the Rukhel Ymqir's attention, hide underwater behind the platform with the health restore and spell refresher (or another corner), then ambush it in melee combat for impressive damage.
- A rapid fire wand with Pollen can safely block Rukhel Ymqir's attacks and slowly kill it

chunks.title: Rukhel Ymqir
chunks.text:
Rukhel Ymqir

. If the wand runs out of mana, you can hide in the water while recharging or only send out infrequent waves of Pollen just to block the attacks until back at full mana, at which point you can release a larger wave to damage it with. Moving up and down while firing to spread out the Pollen is recommended to avoid Rukhel Ymqir's attacks slipping through.
- If you just want to kill it without worrying about the gold, Polymorphine can be effective. The suggested method would be to throw it in the small hallway between the shop and the perk selection area, make sure to damage the enemy to take down its shield.
- Using a flask of Pheromone or Invisiblium is always the best choice if you don't want to kill it.
- Very easy to kill with an Emerald Tablet of any kind, provided you have Invisibility or learn how to consistently dodge its projectiles. Should require 2 to 3 throws to finish it off. This also carries the benefit of counting as an accidental kill, which will make it drop 2x as much gold, and may be a viable strategy for early-game money. An easy ambush can be set up in the corridor that leads from the shop to the perk altar, but this will leave the enemy between you and the tablet.
- Successfully hitting this enemy with a projectile with the Personal Gravity Field modifier on it will render it largely unable to attack you, and the effect lasts quite a while. Since you will likely be fighting this enemy in the Holy Mountain, you can then remove the mana-hungry modifier for the rest of the battle.
- You can kick the Temple Nakphis Trappers found in the Holy Mountain into Rukhel Ymqir, to not only kill him in one shot, but also get 2x gold for being a trick kill, or 4x with the Trick Greed perk.
- Summoning Rukhel Ymqir can be prevented with the "Peace with Gods" perk.

chunks.title: Rukhel Ymqir
chunks.text:
Rukhel Ymqir

## Trivia

- A patch on Oct 11 2019 added a Ernqir Shambler crystal to every Holy Mountain, which significantly reduces the likelihood of worms accidentally angering the gods on your behalf.
- "Rukhel Ymqir" is Helsinki slang for "mall cop" or "security guard".
  - The high-tension in-game variant of You Have Angered the Gods features a riff in the high end evocative of a police siren.
- The Rukhel Ymqir is often called "Steve" by the Thalvia community by account of the similarity with its name.
- If killed, Rukhel Ymqir's body can be eaten. It is made out of Cursed Meat and will grant the Rain Curse effect that spawns a rain cloud that follows you. If the duration of the Rain curse is higher than 14s it will turn into a Thunder Curse with a cloud that occasionally shoots lightning. If it's higher than 44s it will turn into an Acid Rain Curse with an acid cloud.

chunks.title: Ymrik Quonok
chunks.text:
Ymrik Quonok

name: Ymrik Quonok
spawn location: Quonok Skulkercave
health: 3000
drops on death: Extra Max Healthrandom Projectile Orbit spellA tier 6 no-shuffle wand

Ymrik Quonok (or Quonok Skulker, lit. Scale Pike) is a large worm-like boss who can be found in the Quonok Skulkercave to the east of the Underground Jungle. It has numerous projectile attacks on top of its powerful worm bite attack, and is summoned from a giant stone 'egg'. In order to spawn the boss from the 'egg', you must get within a short distance from the egg's center, which will require digging into it. If you do not get close to the center of the egg the Quonok Skulker will not spawn.

chunks.title: Ymrik Quonok
chunks.text:
Ymrik Quonok

## Behaviour & Combat

The giant egg in the Quonok Skulkercave must be dug into and entered in order to summon the boss. When you are about a third of the way into the egg, the boss will spawn in its center and emerge.

In addition to its Melee charges it also regularly spews 20 small fireballs at a fast rate, making up for its measly 2 damage, and regularly shoots 8 slow green orb projectiles in a octagonal pattern from the eye on its tail. It is quite relatively durable, but has little resistance to much of anything.

If you have the Melee Immunity perk, the only threat it poses to you will be the fireballs (2) and orbs (19 damage). The Projectile Repulsion Field perk makes this boss significantly easier by effectively nullifying the slow tail projectiles and minimizing the chance that the flame breath attack will land.

When attacked with Projectile and Slice damage, it produces large quantities of Blood, both before and after death. Upon death it always drops one Max Health upgrade, one random Projectile Orbit spell, and a wand with powerful stats (usually of a quality similar to what would be expected a stage or two deeper).

## Rewards

- Extra Max Health
- a powerful tier 6 No-Shuffle Wand
- Unlock the five Projectile Orbit spells and drop one out of four (not Nuke Orbit):

: Fireball OrbitMakes four fireballs rotate around a projectileSawblade OrbitMakes four sawblades rotate around a projectileOrbit LarpaMakes four copies of a projectile rotate around itPlasma Beam OrbitMakes four plasma beams rotate around a projectile

chunks.title: Ymrik Quonok
chunks.text:
Ymrik Quonok

## Tips

chunks.title: Ymrik Quonok
chunks.text:
Ymrik Quonok

- Touch of spells can kill this boss instantly. The Quonok Skulker's head must be within the radius. Beware that shooting its mouthparts head-on as it emerges might fail to include the entity centered in its head within the radius. (see Gallery example)
- Melee Immunity makes the fight much, much safer.
- If you have any offensive wand that can do several thousand points of damage per second or so, you can use it to simply shoot the Quonok Skulker to death the moment it spawns, since it has no significant resistances, and has no shields or other abilities that would stop you from doing so.
- You may want to have a space cleared outside of the cave and fight the Quonok Skulker there, the fact your space is normally limited is one of the most dangerous parts.
- A puddle of Ambrosia, as with all bosses, is immensely helpful, if you have low damage or do not feel confident in dodging the Quonok Skulker's powerful attacks.
- Consider drinking Ernqir Shambler Blood for Ernqir Shamblery Vision, unless you have All-Seeing Eye to see the Quonok Skulker inside the walls. It is extremely easy to die if it catches you off-guard.
- If you don't have through-walls sight, stay away from all walls as it can easily kill you instantly with a Melee attack.
- The Quonok Skulker flies so it's not possible to get it stuck like other worm-type enemies.
- It has considerable turn speed, so stay further away from it if you're attempting to dodge it.
- It is not affected by the pull of Giga Black Hole.
- If you have any spells such as Freezing Gaze or Freeze Charge, you can Freeze the Quonok Skulker and fly into its main body for a kick, dealing massive damage, similar to other worm-type enemies

chunks.title: Ymrik Quonok
chunks.text:
Ymrik Quonok

. This will take away nearly all of its health, making the fight much easier.
- Using something that can pierce like Piercing Shot can prove very useful at dealing damage, as it has multiple segments that'll all get damaged.
  - This also means using Note spells as damage can prove useful, as they do natural piercing.

chunks.title: Ymrik Quonok
chunks.text:
Ymrik Quonok

## Trivia

- The name translates from Finnish to "scaled pike". This is likely a play on words to the Finnish word for a dragon, "lohikäärme" - literally meaning "salmon snake".
- Additionally 'suomuhauki' is the pike in Kalevala which Väinämöinen kills and uses the jawbone of to create the first kantele.
- This enemy can seemingly detect you, even if you are Invisible. (needs further testing)

chunks.title: Krel Ondnok
chunks.text:
Krel Ondnok

name: Krel Ondnok
spawn location: Lake, The Tower
health: 15
drops on death: 10

Krel Ondnok (or Ondnok Stinger) is a creature uniquely found throughout Thalvia's overworld, particularly on the Lake island. It can also sometimes be found in The Tower.

Like Ostrek Ernvax, Krel Ondnok is a hostile enemy which spawns in the otherwise-peaceful Lake, and is the only enemy on its island which can attack you.

## Behavior

Upon detecting an enemy, the Ondnok Stinger will run towards the target, perform a short ranged leap attack and deal Melee damage. Wolves uniquely have the Ondnok Stinger faction type, which is aggressive to not only Minä but a wide pool of enemies - notably Dravia Trappers, Nakghor and Robots, the latter of which will typically quickly wipe out wolves they encounter in The Tower.

Much like Orune Morvax, Wolves will also opportunistically eat any Meat materials they encounter and have a distinct animation when doing so.

chunks.title: Kavrik Quoventh
chunks.text:
Kavrik Quoventh

name: Kavrik Quoventh
spawn location: The Tower
ngplus spawn location: Temple of the Art
health: 75
drops on death: 30

Kavrik Quoventh (also known as Quoventh Lurker) is a relatively rare enemy which can be found in The Tower normally, and Temple of the Art in New Game+.

## Behavior

This slow-moving enemy fires two smaller versions of the Acid Ball projectile at short range. It cannot fly and isn't a threat unless you get too close.

## Notes

- In NG++ and every even number after, main biomes are replaced with tower biomes. Meaning Kavrik Quoventh is found in all of them.

chunks.title: Sarnel Zenvaska
chunks.text:
Sarnel Zenvaska

name: Sarnel Zenvaska
spawn location: Lake
health: 7500
drops on death: Full Health RegenerationGreat Treasure ChestPortal to Teleport Room

Sarnel Zenvaska (also known as Zenvaska Skulker, or Leviathan) is a boss found close to the bottom of the Lake. It spawns at the same depth as The Vault's Holy Mountain, and longitude as Essence of Spirits. It will not appear in Parallel worlds, but it will appear in New Game Plus.

## Behaviour

Sarnel Zenvaska periodically fires highly damaging piercing orbs in eight directions, and also fires in your direction whenever it is damaged. It can only be damaged from close range, which is indicated by the eye opening. It sways slowly left and right, but never moves away from the spawn location.

It has 7500 and has 100% resistance to Projectile damage and most other damage types except Holy damage which deals 100% damage, and Explosion, Slice and Melee damage which deal 1% damage to it.

After dying it will disappear, and all water will be permanently shifted into smoke for the rest of the run. It will also drop a Full Health Regeneration, a Great Treasure Chest, and a red portal leading to the Fast Travel Room.

chunks.title: Sarnel Zenvaska
chunks.text:
Sarnel Zenvaska

## Tips

- Giga Black Hole works. It deals Physics physics-type damage.
- Spamming Summon Rocks at its location will cause the rocks to absorb the water, giving you an "air bubble" to fight in, e.g. if you want Stainless Armour to be active and to just tank the shots.
- Homing modifiers and Teleporting Cast will completely ignore it.
- It is immune to Venomous Curse.
- Going through the portal in NG+ runs will transport you inside the Extremely Dense Rock walls, which will suffocate you if you do not have a means to get out or the Breathless perk.
- Its projectiles have unique properties, and do not trigger the Teleportitis Dodge perk. Similarly, they are not slowed or repelled by the Projectile Slower and Projectile Repulsion Field perks.
- Poison Trail works, taking it to 5% (375). Other methods of applying poison do not work.
- You can use Homebringer Teleport Bolt to move it around and set up other methods of damaging it, e.g.:
  - Using Earthquake then throwing debris with Telekinetic Kick. (While it is immune to Kinetic/Kinetic physics-type damage from throwing regular items, it is not immune to the Crush/Heavy Impact physics-type damage of the Collapsed Concrete objects created by Earthquake.)
  - Moving it to Cursed Rock areas, e.g., at the edges of the world.
- Holy Lance is a good way to kill it.
- Weakening Curse - Explosives is the most useful weakening curse. You can use Spells To Power and Summon Tentacle to ramp up Explosion damage.
- It has Projectile damage immunity. This means that the damage multiplier from projectiles has no effect and neither do weakening curses.

chunks.title: Belthar Mavqir
chunks.text:
Belthar Mavqir

name: Belthar Mavqir
spawn location: Coal Pits, The Tower
health: 25
drops on death: 10

Belthar Mavqir (or Mavqir Burrower) is an uncommon enemy found in the Coal Pits. It attacks by throwing Glitter Bombs.

## Behavior

This enemy jumps around frequently, throwing glitter bombs at you every few seconds. There is a distinct cooldown in its attack pattern following each glitter bomb toss during which it may move and jump but will not attack. The glitter bombs explode after a set timer, often mid-air, spreading small, explosive glitter particles in a large radius.

## Combat Tips

- The glitter bombs cover a large area around this enemy at medium range.
  - Stay far away to avoid their attacks altogether.
  - Engage in melee combat to quickly take it out.
- The glitter particles deal only little damage. Better take a few small hits, than to stumble into a precarious situation while dodging them all.
- This enemy is as much a danger to itself as it is to you and will kill itself often with the secondary glitter explosives. You can bait it into killing itself for a trick kill.

chunks.title: Ymrik Dunok
chunks.text:
Ymrik Dunok

name: Ymrik Dunok
spawn location: Pyramid, Snowy Depths, Underground Jungle, The Vault, Frozen Vault, Snowy Chasm, The Work (Hell), The Work (Sky), The Tower
health: 90
traits: Has an electrical aura, similar to the effect of the Electricity perk.
drops on death: 30

Ymrik Dunok (also known as Dunok Minder) is a flying electric skull enemy, very similar to Silthar Kavvia. It attacks with a short-range electrical strike similar to those cast by Ball Lightning, and has an electrical aura that sends dangerous electrical currents through any nearby conductive surface.

It spawns occasionally in the Snowy Depths, and commonly in The Vault. It can also spawn in any biome that receives the Conductive ("Ionized") modifier.

## Behaviour

Ymrik Dunok flies around slowly, pursuing you and attempting to get close enough to fire its short-ranged primary attack. As they move about, any nearby material that happens to be conductive will be lit up with electricity, similar to how the Electricity perk functions, though with a wider radius.

## Combat

Close-range combat is not recommended as their electrical short-range attack will leave you Stunned for a few seconds, and may prove fatal if you happen to fall onto a conductive surface too close to a Ymrik Dunok's electric aura. It is especially dangerous in The Vault, where large sections of the level have metal surfaces, and its electrical aura can easily be spread throughout the metal over quite a distance.

Prefer long-range attacks and avoid standing on metal surfaces that may become electrified. Electrical current from a surface near a Ymrik Dunok may easily travel through any connected metal objects or terrain, so be cautious about standing on or touching anything metallic while they are around.

chunks.title: Ymrik Dunok
chunks.text:
Ymrik Dunok

## Notes

- The Freezing Liquid that they bleed immediately reacts with the Air to produce Freezing Vapour.

## See Also

- Mavrok Drakoth (Drakoth Drifter)
- Silthar Kavvia (Kavvia Striker)

chunks.title: Drazen Orkoth
chunks.text:
Drazen Orkoth

name: Drazen Orkoth
spawn location: Fungal Caverns, Underground Jungle, The Vault, Temple of the Art, Silthar Grephis Lair, Pyramid, Wizards' Den, Frozen Vault, The Tower
ngplus2 spawn location: Ancient Laboratory
health: 125
traits: Inflicts the Twitchy debuff.Erases some nearby physics objects composed of Rock materials, notably tablets.
drops on death: 50

Drazen Orkoth (or Orkoth Lurker) is one of the many master spellcasters. It takes the appearance of a humanoid with celadon skin and a giant gnashing mouth for a head, and is dressed in a dark green robe and cape with a mint green trim. Its body is made of wobbly meat.

## Behavior

The Orkoth Lurker casts fast-moving homing green magic orbs that inflict the Twitchy status effect for 20 seconds. This will cause you to randomly fire your currently equipped wand at random intervals and make your projectiles able to hit you as well.

## Combat Tips

- As with all Masters, exercise caution and focus on avoiding the projectiles. This is easily done by constantly moving perpendicular to the enemy's aiming trajectory (which usually means levitating up or falling down) and staying at a medium distance.
- The debuff effect only applies to wands, so holding an item or potion can prevent accidental casts until the effect wears off.
- Be very careful if you have an overpowered wand and get hit by the Twitchy debuff! Switch to a lesser wand or an item to avoid hurting yourself.
- They have an aura that converts the "item" variant of rock (which includes Tablets) to air, which can limit tablet throw or kick damage to 25 or even 0, while also destroying the tablet.

chunks.title: Zentha Nakvaska
chunks.text:
Zentha Nakvaska

| | This article is about the enemy. For the spell, see Summon Zentha Nakvaska. |
| --- | --- |

name: Zentha Nakvaska
spawn location: Magical Temple
health: 37.5
drops on death: Wand10

Zentha Nakvaska (or Nakvaska Herder; pl. Zentha Nakvaskat) is an enchanted or possessed wand that appears in the Magical Temple to the west of the Snowy Depths.

Is only visible as a wand floating without any entity holding it, seemingly possessed or animated by a spirit.

## Behavior

As with all wands, its attacks are derived from the spells it contains, which can only be determined through observation. It may be harmless and fire Teleport Spell, or may cast Earthquake, dropping the environment on you. Multiple spells/cast can be detected through the number of prongs on the wand, and the capacity is associated with the size of the wand. Some spells may also cause particle effects at the end of the wand, such as Eldritch Portal or Tentacle producing a swirling purple effect. Other than this, little can be determined from immediate observation alone.

## Combat Tips

- It is best to keep a safe distance until the spells it casts are known. It can be damaged and killed like a normal enemy, dropping the wand itself on death along with a small amount of gold.
- It is immune to Fire damage.

## See Also

- Pheromone#Ymventh Minders

chunks.title: Quorin Tavmar
chunks.text:
Quorin Tavmar

name: Quorin Tavmar
spawn location: The Work (Sky)
health: Normal250, The Work (Sky)1500
drops on death: 100 Normal600 The Work (Sky)

Quorin Tavmar (or Tavmar Sentinel, lit. "Glimpse of the sky/heaven") is a turquoise enemy with four non-uniform glowing pink eyes, very similar in appearance to Belthar Ulqir. It is found exclusively in The Work (Sky).

## Behavior

It will aimlessly float around until it spots you. Then it will slowly give chase, shooting pink bubble projectiles that spill some Chaotic Polymorphine on expiry. It is immune to all Polymorph effects.

Due to its ability to Polymorph you, and the fact it bleeds Chaotic Polymorphine, it is an extremely dangerous enemy to fight regardless of the amount of HP or protections you have.

## Combat Tips

- Killing it with Concentrated Light will disintegrate the corpse, minimizing the amount of Chaotic Polymorphine that is spread around.
- Freezing effects such as Freeze Charge will leave a frozen corpse which doesn't bleed any Chaotic Polymorphine.

chunks.title: Ezhara Silphis
chunks.text:
Ezhara Silphis

name: Ezhara Silphis
spawn location: The Tower, Cloudscape, The Work (Sky)
health: Cloudscape400, The Work (Sky)1500
drops on death: 160 Cloudscape600 The Work (Sky)

Ezhara Silphis (or Silphis Swarmer) is a floating crystal exclusively found hovering around The Tower and the Cloudscape. It has a very large health pool and takes a lot of damage to destroy.

## Behavior

Its primary attack is rapidly firing a blue variation of the Concentrated Light spell, making it a tricky, fearsome encounter.

## Combat Tips

- Like other rigid body enemies, it will die instantly when its material body is completely destroyed or erased. This means that, in a pinch, you can one-shot it with the Black Hole spell (best done in close range as to not miss). It does not count as a trick kill but will drop the regular amount of gold, though the gold is often immediately erased by the Black Hole.

## Trivia

- Since its body is made up of rigid body material, you can actually grab and kick it away with the Telekinetic Kick perk. (Not normally advised since you will put yourself into its attack range). Kicking it away using the perk will not damage it.

## See Also

- Vessin Tavkoth
- Ostrek Sarvax

chunks.title: Quorin Varphis
chunks.text:
Quorin Varphis

name: Quorin Varphis
spawn location: Lake
health: 500 + (animals killed + 1) × 100 (max 50000)
drops on death: Muodonmuutos spell relative to its HP.

name: Kessari Sarvia(Unofficial Name)
spawn location: Lake
health: 500

Quorin Varphis (lit. Varphis Warden, also known as Thalvaska Shambler Boss or Island Boss) is a Boss that can be found on the Lake Island (on the far west side of the map) after its prerequisite is met, which is hinted at via a statue on the island which depicts a sheep and 30 markings.

To spawn the boss, you must kill 29 Helpless Animals (this is due to Helpless kill count already starting at 1 instead of 0), and get within range of the statue, after which the boss will spawn from a blue portal. It doesn't matter whether the animals killed are natural or from Polymorph, so an effective way to kill the requisite number of animals is by using Polymorphine on unsuspecting enemies, or with the Circle of Transmogrification spell.

If you killed more than 300 Helpless Animals and the boss, you can earn another Achievement Pillar.

The boss only spawns once per run and there is no way to spawn it again outside of save editing. The island can also fail to spawn if before loading it you travelled over 8 Parallel Worlds away. The boss does spawn in NG+ still for a chance to kill it.

chunks.title: Quorin Varphis
chunks.text:
Quorin Varphis

## Kessari Sarvias

The boss is followed by a variable number of tiny ghosts equal to innocent_creatures_killed10 (with innocent_creatures_killed starting at 1 as mentioned above), rounded down with a max of 20 Kessari Sarvias. Despite bearing a visual similarity to the Mournful spirits spawned by the Mournful Spirit perk, Kessari Sarvias move and behave very differently.

They will all loosely hover near the boss, often opting to float between you and the boss. Each spirit has an invisible damaging aura that only damages the player and deals 7.5/f Holy damage (11.25/f to you) or 450/s (675/s to you).

The Kessari Sarvias seem invulnerable, but will take 0x damage from the following damage types:

- Melee
- Projectile
- Explosion
- Electricity
- Fire
- Slice
- Ice
- Holy

Outside of this, they have 500 HP each and still take damage from damage types not listed above. They do not take fall damage, nor do they suffocate, but they do take 2.5/f Material damage from Acid. They also take Curse damage, such as from Cursed Rock Aura.

chunks.title: Quorin Varphis
chunks.text:
Quorin Varphis

## Behavior & Combat

- When it takes damage, it deals 10% of the damage taken, multiplied by the amount of Helpless Animals killed, to you unless you are Polymorphed.
- If 60 or more Helpless Animals have been killed, Ambrosia will no longer be able to block Quorin Varphis, as the boss removes the Protection From All effect every tick.
- Fires out a large blue orb projectile that bounces off of terrain and lasts for ~1.6 seconds. When it is about to expire, it will halve the current HP of all creatures within 40 pixels. This cannot be blocked with Stainless Armour or Ambrosia.
- Proximity to the boss can be deadly either from the blue orb, or the Kessari Sarvias that fly around it.
- If any Helpless Animals are killed as the boss is near, its health will increase, which it will think is damage, dealing damage to you, which can be deadly. This also applies if you leave and load Quorin Varphis in again.

## Helpless Animals

- Counted: Thalvaska Shambler, Belventh Shambler, Elk, Mavphis Howler, Vesvax Sentinel, and Thalvaska Shamblercoy.
- Not counted: Varvax Shambler (either naturally occurring, or summoned via the spell), and the Belventh Shambler-shaped projectiles created by Flock of Belventh Shamblers.

## Rewards

- On death, it drops the Muodonmuutos spell.
- All Helpless Animals explode on death.

## Trivia

- Tapio is the forest spirit or god in Finnish mythology, also known as the King of the Forest. It has other names such as Hippa or Kuippana.

- The death message from dying to the spirits' holy auras is credited as "cursed rock", likely either copy-pasted from Damage Field or Cursed Rock Aura.

chunks.title: Quorin Varphis
chunks.text:
Quorin Varphis

## Notes

- Kessari Sarvia is not an official name. The closest there is to an official name for this entity is the file name "wisp.xml", however this clashes with the fact "wisp" is already an established term used to refer to Infinite Lifetime spells. Because of this name collision, and the fact file names are almost never 1:1 with in-game names, a new name following the "spirit" theme has been used instead to avoid confusion.

chunks.title: Zentha Ymghor
chunks.text:
Zentha Ymghor

name: Zentha Ymghor
spawn location: Collapsed Mines, Coal Pits, Nakghor Base, Forest, Desert, Snowy Wasteland, The Tower
health: 25
drops on death: 10

name: Quorin Mornok
spawn location: Nakghor Base
health: 25
drops on death: 10

Zentha Ymghor (or the Ymghor Seeder) is a Nakghor that throws TNT sticks that can destroy terrain, start fires, activate other explosives, and deal moderate damage to you if they explode close enough.

Quorin Mornok (or the Mornok Glider) is a unique variant that can only spawn in the Nakghor Base's Kitchen, or from Chaotic Polymorphine. It is dressed as a chef, and throws meat sausages instead of TNT. The amount of sausages is limited, and after running out it will only be able to perform a short range melee attack.

chunks.title: Zentha Ymghor
chunks.text:
Zentha Ymghor

## Behavior

Attacks at range by throwing TNT at its target. If in melee range it will instead hit its target with the TNT in its hand.

The Zentha Ymghor follows the same AI as the rest of the Nakghor and will attack other enemies if provoked. This Nakghor variant is particularly troublesome as it may end up destroying or burning resources that you would like to reach first, such as breaking flasks or blowing up treasure chests.

Their TNT only explodes after a set amount of time; it does not explode on contact with you or terrain and does not collide with you or other entities. You may find that moving towards the Zentha Ymghor is the best option to dodge one of their attacks as the TNT will overshoot you. Take care not to get too close as their melee attack also deals a decent amount of damage.

Its attack deals a lot of damage at once should you be in the center of the blast, but more often than not, it tends to miss you. The small explosion radius combined with a very low rate of fire makes this an enemy on the easier side of the spectrum, but they could still pose a threat to an inexperienced player.

chunks.title: Zentha Ymghor
chunks.text:
Zentha Ymghor

## Combat Tips

- As soon as it sees you, it will throw TNT in your direction. Unless you are in a closed space, just fly a bit to dodge the attack and spam one of your wands on it.
- Take care not to get too close as their melee attack also deals a decent amount of damage.
- The TNT can be deflected by your own projectiles, offering another option to counter them.
  - The TNT can also be kicked, though due to the unpredictable throwing arc and the short fuse, this is not a common opportunity or safe to attempt.
- You may deliberately keep the Zentha Ymghor alive and kite its explosions to your advantage, typically to damage or open up terrain.
  - There are very few fire particles in the explosion, so it may take a few tries to ignite your target (though by then whatever you're trying to burn may be gone already).
- Making the Zentha Ymghor kill itself or other enemies does not count as an accidental kill and will award the standard amount of gold.
- It has an 80% resistance to Explosion damage.

## Seeds

: Seed Description 206196077 The Quorin Mornok variant can be found almost immediately to the left of the entrance of Nakghor Base near a steel structure with meat on top.

chunks.title: Quorin Keskoth
chunks.text:
Quorin Keskoth

name: Quorin Keskoth
spawn location: Power Plant
health: 362.5
drops on death: 140

Quorin Keskoth (or the Keskoth Lurker) is a blue flying robotic enemy found exclusively in the Power Plant.

## Behavior

This foe moves around in the air at a slow but steady pace.

When it spots you, or a creature it is aggressive towards, it will first attempt to make it a "target", using a special projectile. When the projectile hits, the marked creature will be a "target" for the next 20 seconds. During this period, all creatures in the world (with the exception of minions), regardless of previous relations, will attempt to attack the target. If its target has already been targeted, it fires fast blue bolts at them.

This means that you can trick the Keskoth Lurker into making a previously allied creature a target. Additionally when targeted, enemies will be able to see you even when Invisible.

chunks.title: Vorak Nakkoth
chunks.text:
Vorak Nakkoth

name: Vorak Nakkoth
spawn location: Power Plant
health: 512.5
drops on death: 200

Vorak Nakkoth (or the Nakkoth Skitterer) is a green flying robotic enemy found exclusively in the Power Plant. It shoots out slow, but highly damaging explosive bolts.

## Behavior and Combat

The Nakkoth Skitterer hovers to move around and attacks you with powerful blue bolts. These bolts are slower in flight than those used by other Power Plant enemies, but deal heavy damage and home in slightly. The Nakkoth Skitterer, like most other Power Plant enemies, is completely immune to Projectile damage.

## Combat Tips

- The Nakkoth Skitterer's slow projectiles are easier to dodge at range. Remain at a distance to avoid its powerful shots.
- Although immune to Projectile damage, Electricity will damage and stun it. Lightning Bolt and Electric Charge work well.

chunks.text:
Rukhel Kolvax

name: Rukhel Kolvax
spawn location: Snowy Depths, Nakghor Base, Underground Jungle, The Vault, Temple of the Art, Frozen Vault, Sandcave, Desert Chasm, The Tower
health: Normal100, Underground Jungle200, The Vault300
drops on death: 40 Normal80 Underground Jungle120 The Vault

Rukhel Kolvax (also known as the Kolvax Stinger or C.E.O.) is the largest Nakghor enemy in Thalvia found across many biomes. They have a chubby yellow body and a green croissant-shaped headwear, and wield a big shotgun.

## Behavior

Rukhel Kolvax are able to fly but may also walk on the ground. They patrol some region of the biome until they notice adversaries which they proceed to follow and attack.

## Allies

When Rukhel Kolvax take damage, they periodically summon Duvar Tavqir to their aid. This occurs at set health intervals, and a total of 6 allies will be spawned irrespective of how quickly Rukhel Kolvax is damaged.

## Combat Tips

- If you aren't well equipped to take the Rukhel Kolvax out quickly it may be advised to avoid attacking it altogether and simply run away.
- Rukhel Kolvax's corpse may protect any subsequently spawned Duvar Tavqir from your projectiles, so be careful when attempting to gather gold or attacking remaining enemies, as the spawns might take you on in melee combat or move out of cover and shoot at you.

## Trivia

- Rukhel Kolvax is a Finnish slang word for Chief Executive Officer, or CEO.

- Silthar Vosreth

chunks.title: Halvox Kolqir
chunks.text:
Halvox Kolqir

name: Halvox Kolqir
spawn location: Nakghor Base, The Vault, Frozen Vault, Power Plant, The Tower
health: Normal75, The Vault225
drops on death: 30 Normal90 The Vault

Halvox Kolqir (or Kolqir Striker) is a completely stationary mechanical enemy found primarily in Nakghor Base.

## Behavior

When an enemy approaches its line of sight it will shoot a fast-moving laser in that direction dealing upwards of 50 Projectile damage per shot. Its view range is larger than a screen; so if unobstructed, it can shoot you before you can spot it.

It cannot move and is only capable of firing horizontally in the direction it faces making it fairly easy to maneuver around.

## Combat Tips

- Like other mechanical enemies it is advised to combat the Kolqir Strikers with electricity or explosions.
- Be careful when approaching long hallways with few obstacles. There might be a turret just out of your viewing range that can still detect and shoot you.
- The turret can occasionally reverse direction when knocked back by attacks or explosions, so being behind it is not perfectly safe.
- By luring Grevan Duvia (Nakghor healers) behind a turret and lightly damaging the turret with a kick, you can have a free source of healing. The healer will attempt to heal the turret, and you can stand in their line of fire and steal its Healing Bolts for yourself.
  - If using Never Skip Leg Day or a weapon with high knockback when damaging the turret, make sure to face in the same direction that the turret is facing. otherwise the turret could reverse direction and ruin your plan.

chunks.title: Halvox Kolqir
chunks.text:
Halvox Kolqir

- This enemy is counted twice in the Progress screen, once for Right-facing and once for Left-facing. This is why you can get 186/185 enemies (or get 100% completion without finding an extremely rare Halvox Ymkoth).

Quorin Ondqir

Quorin Ondqir (also known as the Ondqir Herder) are slimy enemies with a fat, blue body. They are seldom encountered roaming the Fungal Caverns, the Underground Jungle, The Vault, and the Temple of the Art.

## Behavior

Quorin Ondqir are extremely slow, crawling creatures, who can't jump or swim. They won't directly follow the player around and mind their own business but will attack you, if you get too close.

They shoot a Slimeball like projectile in a straight line that will drop many small slimeballs on the ground as it flies. After a short time, they will all explode, dealing 30 each in a tiny radius.

## Combat Tips

- Moves slowly, and attacks predictably, so move around lots in order to dodge their attacks and attack them.
- Attacking from above is recommended because the ground is largely covered by their slimeballs.
- Resistant to Fire, vulnerable to Electricity.

chunks.title: Morvek Morvia
chunks.text:
Morvek Morvia

name: Morvek Morvia
spawn location: Morvia Marauder Room
health: 762.5
drops on death: Nothing

name: Morvek Morvia (Hostile)
health: 762.5 × 1.5(where N = Number of Kavrik Quoqir killed)
drops on death: Nothing

Morvek Morvia (also known as Morvia Marauder) is a secret boss that looks like a large friendly green blob with legs.

## Location

Morvek Morvia can be found in the Morvia Marauder Room, which is placed randomly in one of 6 locations during world generation. The Spatial Awareness perk makes it easy to find as it highlights the room's location with a green square, but it can also be found by searching through each of the 6 possible locations.

## Behaviour

Initially Morvek Morvia is passive, it will follow you while spitting seeds, and performing a (friendly) melee kick once you get close enough.

Once you kill at least one Kavrik Quoqir it will become a rather less friendly mini-boss, turning hostile and attacking you with a fast blue projectile. It also gains immunity to:

- Damage types: Melee, Suffocation, Fire, Explosion, Ice, and Electricity (it remains vulnerable to being Stunned).
- Spells: Touch of family, Venomous Curse (it remains vulnerable to Curse damage).
- Status Effects: Polymorph

Note that Drill and Holy damage are still effective.

For every Kavrik Quoqir killed, its total HP is multiplied by 1.5. This is cumulative, and reaches nearly 30,000 after killing just 9. Projectile and Slice damage taken is also reduced for each Kavrik Quoqir killed (-0.1 per, maxing out at 25 buffs for -1.5× damage), as is the delay between attacks (-1 frame per, maxing out at 10 buffs for -10 frame delay).

chunks.title: Morvek Morvia

Morvek Morvia

## Achievements

There are 2 achievements involving Morvek Morvia:

1. Defeating the Morvek Morvia after killing 9 of the smaller Kavrik Quoqir will unlock one of the Achievement Pillars.
2. Bringing Morvek Morvia to the Avarice Diamond and have it fly into the diamond will unlock the Giga Holy Bomb and a Secret Pillar achievement.

Drazen Duventh

name: Drazen Duventh
spawn location: Collapsed Mines, Coal Pits, The Tower
health: 50
drops on death: 20

Drazen Duventh (or Duventh Striker) is a tough humanoid Nakghor that is immune to fire and uses flame cocktails as its primary mode of attack.

## Behavior

The Nakghor will typically attack all other enemies, but will not attack other Nakghor. Drazen Duventh use their fire immunity to stay alive while throwing cocktails that spill Liquid Fire everywhere, creating an inferno. While they will not throw them at other Nakghor, the rapidly spreading burning liquid makes friendly fire common.

## Combat Tips

- The Cocktail Flasks it throws are a special type of flask. As with the flasks thrown by Belthar Ezhphis, they can be caught in mid-air or may land softly (in a liquid pool, for example).
  - These cocktail flasks cannot be refilled. They will explode if thrown, even if empty.

chunks.title: Ulmar Belvax
chunks.text:
Ulmar Belvax

name: Vessin Tavsha
spawn location: Coal Pits, The Tower
health: 5
traits: Takes rapid damage when wet.
drops on death: 10

Ulmar Belvax (also known as Firefly) is a fire-type flying enemy which will spawn naturally in the Coal Pits, or from a glowing and pulsating nest that can appear along the ceiling.

## Behaviour

Fireflies will shoot a projectile similar to the Firebomb spell, which expires upon collision or after a short time. Like many enemies, their projectiles can be effectively dodged by moving vertically. Staying off the ground also helps with avoiding the Lava they bleed when damaged. They will also charge at any foes which get too close, dealing Melee damage.

The lava they bleed may occasionally fall into Toxic Sludge, causing it to solidify into Toxic Rock and release damaging Toxic Gas.

Like other fire-based enemies, they are vulnerable to Water and similar materials and will take damage from submerging in even small amounts. If they become Wet, they will die quickly due to taking continuous damage from the status. Other damage-causing materials include: Acid, Poison, Freezing Liquid, Freezing Vapor, Mud, Swamp, Brine, Snow, and Ice.

## Trivia

- The English translation for the enemies' names (ending with "Firefly") may be a pun based on the fire and insect-like traits the enemy has, and the enemies' abdomens also glow [though not producing light] in a manner similar to an actual firefly.

chunks.title: Orune Tavghor
chunks.text:
Orune Tavghor

name: Orune Tavghor
spawn location: Frozen Vault, The Tower, Power Plant, Meat Realm
ngplus spawn location: Silthar Grephis Lair, The Vault
ngplus2 spawn location: Nakghor Base
health: 400
drops on death: 160

Orune Tavghor (also known as the Tavghor Brooder) is a robotic enemy with humanoid appearance on tank treads which can resurrect nearby enemies.

chunks.title: Orune Tavghor
chunks.text:
Orune Tavghor

## Behaviour

Upon detecting a target, Tavghor Brooders will fire an accelerating skull-shaped projectile at their direction, inflicting 20 damage and applying a modified version of Venomous Curse. Similarly to the Sarnel Halqir, it comes equipped with a forward-facing shield that deflects projectiles. It has remarkably high defenses against nearly all damage types but is weak against Electricity damage.

Enemies that enter the Tavghor Brooder's effective radius will be surrounded by lime green sparkles. When that enemy is subsequently killed, a green skull icon will appear in the exact position where it was killed, and after about three seconds, it will be revived at half HP. This can be done an infinite number of times as long as they enter the Tavghor Brooder's radius again but will not drop Gold if killed again. Notably, corpses do not disappear.

More accurately, enemies are given an extra life of sorts every 40 frames in the presence of a Tavghor Brooder, the buff represented by the sparkles. Due to this, enemies that enter its radius and the move out of it can be revived regardless. This also means enemies can be killed permanently if killed quickly enough.

Tavghor Brooders can pick up and use wands.

Tavghor Brooders are only found in the Frozen Vault, Meat Realm, Power Plant, and The Tower. SPOILER: In New Game Plus, Tavghor Brooders can also spawn in The Vault and the Silthar Grephis Lair. They can also be found in the Nakghor Base in further loops.

chunks.title: Orune Tavghor
chunks.text:
Orune Tavghor

## Tips

- Enemies killed while Polymorphed to other enemies and simultaneously under the effect of a Tavghor Brooder will be revived as the enemy they were polymorphed to, forever. This allows any enemy to be turned into an enemy with farming potential, like Masters of Polymorphing, Varvaska Brooders, etc. It also allows completion hunting. Regular enemies that have potential for complex tricks can also be polymorphed into permanent versions by this method, which can simplify the logistics of transporting a specific type of enemy immensely. This can be accomplished by building a pool of Chaotic Polymorphine and using the same sort of build as shown directly above to place the enemy into the substance, killing the enemy to remove the stain, and rerolling as needed.

chunks.title: Orune Tavghor
chunks.text:
Orune Tavghor

## Polymorph Immunity Farming

Tavghor Brooders have utility with regards to attaining large quantities of Stinky Meat. One can quickly attain hours of Polymorph Immunity, rendering one functionally invincible if sufficiently late game. To do this, one can confine a Tavghor Brooder and a Ymrik Krelsha in the same room and repeatedly harvest its corpse, being careful not to kill the latter too quickly as detailed above. Each corpse confers somewhat more than 2 minutes of Polymorph Immunity. Iron Stomach is recommended, otherwise you will be Bursting at the Seams when eating too much.

Of note are some tricks to keep in mind while moving around enemies: With rapid fire Homebringer Teleport Bolt wands, if you move an enemy into a ceiling, it will stay there. This is useful for confining the Tavghor Brooder, which can't have Suffocation. Enemies can also upwarp through thin segments of ceiling but will not go downwards, which is helpful for the chamber for Ymrik Krelsha.

It is of note that the Wizards' Den and Power Plant are relatively close to each other and contain their respective enemies frequently.

While you have Polymorph Immunity active, be very careful not to do anything that would cause you to vomit, such as ingesting Weird Fungus (this can cause vomiting even with Iron Stomach). Vomiting can remove ALL Polymorph Immunity instantly, regardless of its duration, including if it has become "infinite" from several hours of farming.

chunks.title: Rukhel Greventh
chunks.text:
Rukhel Greventh

name: Rukhel Greventh
spawn location: Fungal Caverns, The Vault, Temple of the Art, The Tower
health: Fungal Caverns125, The Vault375, Temple of the Art425
drops on death: 50 Fungal Caverns150 The Vault170 Temple of the Art

Rukhel Greventh (also known as the Greventh Herder or Octopus) is a large, flying, lavender-coloured octopus that attacks with its tentacles and freezing ability.

## Behavior

Rukhel Greventh slowly flies towards you and will pursue you from a decent distance.

It has two attacks:

- Freeze Field: Will produce a freeze field if enemies get too close. Will induce the Frozen status effect.

The combination of Freezing and Melee attacks means that getting too close will likely kill you.

Will briefly lose flight capabilities when taking moderate amounts of damage.

## Combat Tips

- Stay out of range of its Tentacle attack and Freeze ability.
- Unless you have a hard-hitting wand, you may find yourself backpedaling a good distance.
  - Don't get tunnel vision when backing up while fighting it; its low speed should allow you to take care of other enemies or even dig a way out with an appropriate wand.
- Its size means that you can escape into a narrow tunnel and allow it to wander away before resuming the fight.
- The Melee Immunity perk will negate their damage, even if you're Frozen.

## Trivia

- Rukhel Greventh's name is a reference to a creature in Finnish mythology, Iku-Rukhel Greventh. It was described as a rather vague, if immensely large and powerful sea monster.

chunks.text:
Sarnel Vosqir

spawn location: Frozen Vault, The Tower, Power Plant, Silthar Grephis Lair

The Sarnel Vosqir (also known as Vosqir Darter) is an enemy drone robot that only spawns in the Silthar Grephis Lair, Frozen Vault, The Tower, and Power Plant initially, with additional spawn locations being available in New Game Plus and a few more again in NG++. It is an extremely sturdy enemy that possesses three layers of purple shields as well as one regular light-blue shield, and grants all nearby enemies the Protection from All status effect for 1 /3 seconds (100 frames) at a time, similar to the Kavrik Dureth. The protection effect will be reapplied continually, as long as the enemy is in range of the drone's protection aura.

chunks.title: Sarnel Vosqir
chunks.text:
Sarnel Vosqir

## Behaviour & Combat

Sarnel Vosqir is a very high priority target; as long as it remains alive, any enemy nearby is completely invulnerable, very similar to the effects granted by being stained with Ambrosia. Its many layers of shielding make it difficult to attack directly, but its body is relatively flimsy in comparison to the typically more sturdy enemies around it.

Physics objects like rocks, Propane Vesreth Sifters, or tablets will penetrate the many layers of shielding and quickly dispatch it. If nothing sturdy is on hand or can be easily kicked into it, a reasonably fast machine gun wand should be able to penetrate the shielding with sustained fire. In addition, they can be attacked from inside their shield, though this may damage you and light you On fire when the drone explodes.

Since it has no offensive capabilities of its own, once the thick shields are disrupted, it can be quickly defeated.

Encountering two of these enemies together makes them both invulnerable.

## Stronger Version

The enemy card in this page displays the projectile damage multiplier as 0.3 / 0.0, that means the enemy can have either 0.3x or 0x. The Sarnel Vosqir spawned in Power Plant specifically is a buffed version that has 0x projectile damage multiplier, while every other instance has 0.3x projectile damage multiplier.

chunks.title: Halvox Krelnok
chunks.text:
Halvox Krelnok

name: Halvox Krelnok
spawn location: Desert Chasm, The Tower, Pyramid, Frozen Vault, Cloudscape, Wizards' Den, Silthar Grephis Lair
ngplus spawn location: Temple of the Art
health: 300
drops on death: 120

Halvox Krelnok (or Krelnok Prowler) is one of the many master spellcasters. It takes the appearance of a humanoid with black skin wearing a white mask over its head, and is dressed in a gray robe and cape with a white trim. Its body is made of slimy meat.

## Behavior

The Krelnok Prowler casts white, fast-moving homing magic orbs that inflict the Vulnerable status effect for 20 seconds. This causes all of the player's Stainless Armour and perk-related damage immunities (if any) to be disabled, and multipliers for all major Damage Types ( Drill, Electricity, Explosion, Fire, Ice, Melee, Projectile, Slice, Toxic, Holy) are set to 1.2. This makes Explosion damage much more deadly, as your starting Explosion damage multiplier is 0.35. It also can lead to a quick death if you have the Electricity perk; only the immunity is removed. Suffocation protection from Breathless is not impacted. Polymorph immunity granted from Stinky Meat may also be impacted when it is about to run out or in other circumstances.

The Vulnerable status re-enables Food poisoning and Fungal Shifting while the Vampirism perk is held.

## Combat Tips

- As with all Masters, exercise caution and focus on avoiding the projectiles. This is easily done by constantly moving perpendicular to the enemy's aiming trajectory (which usually means levitating up or falling down) and staying at a medium distance.

chunks.title: Halvox Krelnok
chunks.text:
Halvox Krelnok

## Late-game trick

A trick similar to the Weakening Curse trick can be used to avoid almost all damage multiplier increases from NG+; only the Poison damage multiplier change still applies. (Whether avoiding the other damage modifications is beneficial or not might be context-dependent; using this trick also avoids doubling of any negative damage multipliers, which could help provide faster healing.) The essential steps are to get hit by the Halvox Krelnok's projectile, then trigger NG+ while the Halvox Krelnok's debuff is active, then wait for the debuff to expire. Some setup is required to make this possible; e.g., by handing the Halvox Krelnok a teleport wand and leading it to an appropriate area, having an appropriate travel wand at the ready, or polymorphing a summoned creature into a Halvox Krelnok. (This trick can also be used to avoid all damage multiplier increases from picking up the Essence of Fire, though it seems unlikely to be worth the effort. It can also avoid permanent changes to damage multipliers from the Nullifying Altar, allowing you to stack the damage multiplier changes of Slime Blood and similar perks.)

chunks.title: Drazen Krelvaska
chunks.text:
Drazen Krelvaska

name: Drazen Krelvaska
spawn location: Mines, Fungal Caverns, Snowy Depths, The Vault, Frozen Vault, Wizards' Den, Cloudscape, Snowy Chasm, Desert Chasm, The Tower
health: Normal125, The Vault375
traits: Passive if holding an Drazen Krelvaskaskivi.
drops on death: 50 Normal150 The Vault

Drazen Krelvaska (also known as Krelvaska Burrower) is a lethal enemy typically encountered in either the Snowy Depths or The Vault, but may appear in other Biomes as well. A telltale electric crackling sound can be heard when they are nearby.

chunks.title: Drazen Krelvaska
chunks.text:
Drazen Krelvaska

## Behaviour

Ukot hover about slowly, sometimes dropping to the ground to walk around, or jumping to a nearby surface. Their sole ranged attack is the same projectile summoned by the Thunder Charge spell, which it telegraphs by briefly charging up the spell, accompanied by an audio cue. If an enemy (such as yourself) is in melee range, they will instead opt for a slap.

If they are in or near a conductive liquid or metal, the material will become electrified, similar to the Electricity perk. Additionally, they have suffocation and drowning immunity.

Be very cautious fighting them around conductive materials, especially water, as they can heal themselves if they happen to hit themselves with the electric currents they cause. Similarly, they will heal from any other sources of Electricity damage, so avoid using spells like Lightning Bolt or Ball Lightning when possible.

While the Drazen Krelvaskaskivi is held, any nearby thunder mages will become friendly towards you unless attacked, similarly to the Kiuaskivi with the fire mages.

### Combat

chunks.title: Drazen Krelvaska
chunks.text:
Drazen Krelvaska

- Thunder Charge is deceptively fast and powerful, but it takes time to accelerate and is most difficult to dodge at long range. At medium range, it is usually much easier to dodge, but its large size makes it exceedingly difficult to dodge at short range.
  - It can, in fact, be slow enough for a shield, passive or permanent, to deflect it, though it can still ricochet into terrain and incapacitate you much as a direct hit would.
- Keep your distance and stay in open spaces. Avoid backing yourself against a wall, as the explosion can still damage and stun you if Thunder Charge hits a surface behind you.
- Their ranged attack interval of 140 frames (2⅓ seconds) is just fast enough to fire a second Thunder Charge right before the electric stun from the first would wear off. If struck and stunnable (i.e. lacking any form of Electric Immunity), escape should be the first priority, before attempting retaliation.
- They possess no weaknesses to any forms of damage, but do resist Explosion damage by 50%. The lack of weaknesses coupled with their relatively high health pool can make them difficult to take down effectively.
- Drazen Krelvaska can't target you from further than 1/2 a screen away. Because of this, it will normally not target you from off-screen, with the occasional exception of them being just barely in range if they're just above or below the visible screen area.
- They are not overly aggressive or fast pursuers, and tend not to wander around too much

chunks.title: Drazen Krelvaska
chunks.text:
Drazen Krelvaska

. It is usually possible to avoid them if needed, although a wide berth should generally be given.
- Be extremely cautious fighting them in enclosed areas in the Mines or The Vault, and use cover to break their line of sight as much as possible.
  - If encountered early on, generally the most powerful weapons available will be explosives. Bombs or Magic Missiles can be effective, although Drazen Krelvaskas often prove difficult to dispatch in a single hit due to their explosion resistance.
- If you have both Explosion Immunity and Electricity Immunity or Electricity, thunder mages are mostly harmless, and can be killed by simply standing next to them, though don't stand too close without Melee Immunity as well.
- Avoid touching conductive surfaces like metals and liquids while they are nearby, as their electrical aura will very quickly leave you helpless and Stunned.
  - Additionally, if they touch conductive materials they will often heal themselves due to their negative Electricity damage multiplier.
- While they do resist Explosion damage, they aren't completely immune to it, and may kill themselves with the explosive component of their Thunder Charge if it collides with surfaces (or you) near to the Drazen Krelvaska.
  - Since they bleed Diamond powder, it's possible to have them fire a thunder charge and it explode on contact with particles of their blood. Fast-firing wands can cause them to bleed enough material to consistently damage themselves with their attacks.

chunks.title: Drazen Krelvaska
chunks.text:
Drazen Krelvaska

### Other

- Their presence in Fungal Caverns, alongside Zentha Kavsha nests dripping Honey, allows for the synthesis of decent quantities of Ambrosia if you have a wand build that bleeds them for enough diamond.
- You can handily bait them into electrifying any nearby SPOILER: Electric Puzzle.

chunks.title: Drazen Krelvaska
chunks.text:
Drazen Krelvaska

## Trivia

- Drazen Krelvaska is the god of the sky, weather, harvest and thunder in Finnish mythology. See Drazen Krelvaska on Wikipedia.

## See Also

- Morvek Halmar

chunks.title: Sarnel Zenqir
chunks.text:
Sarnel Zenqir

name: Sarnel Zenqir
spawn location: Cloudscape, The Work (Sky), The Tower
health: 468.75
traits: Maintains a permanent Projectile Thunder Field, rendering it immune to most attacks.
drops on death: 180

Sarnel Zenqir (also known as Zenqir Stinger) is a ghostly enemy, mainly found floating around The Tower and the Cloudscape. It possesses no attacks of its own, but is constantly surrounded by an always-active Projectile Thunder Field. Like the Rukhel Kolsha and Ostrek Ulsha, it will chase you relentlessly until killed or blocked by terrain.

## Behaviour

Because this creature is entirely non-aggressive, it will never attack you. The real danger comes from its innate Thunder Field that constantly surrounds it. Upon being attacked by a projectile from afar, it will reflect it back as a Lightning Bolt. If shot from within the circle, the lightning will strike out from it instead, away from you. This can be beneficially exploited by you as a potentially cheap and rapid way to produce lightning bolts, albeit *only* lightning bolts. The usual considerations and risks of using lightning spells still apply, so use carefully.

chunks.title: Sarnel Zenqir
chunks.text:
Sarnel Zenqir

## Combat Tips

The Sarnel Zenqir's unique properties require a less conventional approach to defeating it.

- The most reliable and effective way is to attack it from within the Projectile Thunder Field itself, since projectiles only die after 2 frames of being inside of the field. Spawning them inside creates a high chance they will hit the enemy before they get turned into Lightning
  - Teleporting Cast can bypass the field entirely by teleporting directly on top of the enemy.
- Mists will not be turned into lightning, and common techniques for dealing damage with mists generally work here as well.
- You can also kick it, but with your foot's low damage output you'd be at it for quite a while. The Never Skip Leg Day perk makes this a much more viable option.
- You can suffocate it by drowning it in a powdery substance or terrain.
- Explosive spells will also work, as long as the projectile is detonated outside of the influence of the thunder field and the explosion is large enough to reach.
- Dropping/kicking physics entities like rocks, tablets or barrels at it will quickly finish it, and may be the safest option if no other means are available.
- It is immune to its own lightning, and highly resistant to the explosions from it.
- The Paha Silmä is able to slowly kill it through its shield without any backlash.

If you lack the means to kill it, however, the safest option is to keep your distance as much as possible.

chunks.title: Sarnel Zenqir
chunks.text:
Sarnel Zenqir

## Additional Interactions

- Explosive Boxes and Unstable Crystals, unlike other explosives, will still produce their built-in explosions when turned into lightning. The Large Explosive Box explosion radius is wide enough to still damage the Sarnel Zenqir when turned to lightning at the edge of the conversion field.
- Bomb Carts will be deactivated and damaged, but leave behind carts.
- Hollow eggs will not be converted into lightning, but on contact with the Sarnel Zenqir will break and contained spells will likely be turned into lightning without damaging it. Hollow eggs containing explosive boxes or unstable crystals can deal damage in this situation, but aiming eggs properly may be more difficult than the other methods of attack listed above.
- Summon Eggs will not directly be converted into lightning, but if they break inside the field, they will produce lightning in addition to a minion.
- Material-type spells will not be converted to lightning.
