Belthar Sarmar (also known as The Sarmar Striker or Ymventh Minder Boss) is a boss found in the Sarmar Striker Cave, west of the Snowy Chasm. It moves in unpredictable ways, which, when combined with the nearby enemies, makes for a chaotic fight.

chunks.title: Belthar Sarmar
chunks.text:
Belthar Sarmar

## Behavior

Belthar Sarmar will stay in the middle of the arena until you approach, at which point the fight begins. The boss will move towards you, continuously launching Morvek Rukphis from its mouth, which explode for quite high damage when close to you. Every 3 seconds, the boss will attempt to spawn an Silthar Halvax until two have been summoned.

If in contact with the boss's main body, you will also take very high Curse damage over time.

Belthar Sarmar and its Morvek Rukphis minions cannot be damaged unless a Paha Silmä is close. This means that in order to kill the boss, the item must be strategically placed in a spot close to the boss and safe from matter-destroying spells.

Despite all of this, the real danger comes from the surrounding enemies in the arena. The Vossha Marauder in the center summons dangerous illusions that cannot be damaged, and the two Silghor Minders will heal and grant invulnerability to the boss.

Upon taking damage, Belthar Sarmar will emit 4 orbiting Plasma Beam-like projectiles. These beams become longer, wider, and deal more damage each time Belthar Sarmar takes damage. The beams will gradually weaken over time, and are eventually disabled if enough time has passed without the boss taking damage.

When killed, it will fade into a white cloud of particles, dropping a Full Health Regeneration and Sun Seed.

chunks.title: Belthar Sarmar
chunks.text:
Belthar Sarmar

## Combat Tips

- Due to its resistances, spells that deal both high Explosion and Electricity damage (such as Lightning Bolt, Ball Lightning or Thunder Charge) are best fit for this fight.
- Make sure to rid of the crystals and nearby enemies as quickly as you can. If left alone, they make the fight much harder.
- Rapid fire or rapidly damaging wands can be very dangerous, as the revenge plasma can very quickly expand and cover most of the arena, very quickly killing you.
- Remember to keep a safe distance away, to avoid taking high Curse damage, and have time to destroy the Rukphis Drifters.
- Take caution when using matter destroying spells as they may destroy the Paha Silmä while it is on the ground. This includes the Sun Seed reward.
- The boss can be killed by Acid.
- 3 or more copies of More Love will prevent Belthar Sarmar from continually spawning Morvek Rukphis. However, Morvek Rukphis will still spawn if you damage Belthar Sarmar or are stained with Berserkium.
- The boss is vulnerable for a few frames upon loading in, making it possible to kill the boss even without a Paha Silmä.

## Builds

Acid can kill this boss instantly

chunks.title: Thalven Ulmar
chunks.text:
Thalven Ulmar

name: Thalven Ulmar
spawn location: Fungal Caverns, Snowy Depths, Temple of the Art, Wizards' Den, Cloudscape, The Tower
ngplus spawn location: Ancient Laboratory

drops on death: 40

Thalven Ulmar (also known as Ulmar Sentinel or Swapper) is one of the many master spellcasters. It takes the appearance of a humanoid with blue skin, a single white, cross-shaped eye, and a tiny, gray stem on its head, and is dressed in a kobicha brown robe and cape with a white trim. Its body is made of Ambiguous Meat.

## Behaviour

The Ulmar Sentinel specializes in homing blue magic orbs that do not deal damage, but cause the target and itself to immediately switch positions, identical to the Swapper spell. More importantly, this effect also triggers when it is damaged by another entity. This can cause you to be hurt by your own projectiles that can deal self-damage, such as Summon Disc Projectile or any spell with the Piercing Shot spell modifier.

chunks.title: Thalven Ulmar
chunks.text:
Thalven Ulmar

## Combat Tips

chunks.title: Thalven Ulmar
chunks.text:
Thalven Ulmar

- As with all Masters, exercise caution and focus on avoiding the projectiles. This is easily done by constantly moving perpendicular to the enemy's aiming trajectory (which usually means levitating up or falling down) and staying at a medium distance.
- The on-damage swap occurs once per damage type on a projectile. Hitting them with a projectile that deals an even number of damage types avoids leaving you at the mage's location unless the killing blow was dealt by an odd-numbered damage type.
  - One way to craft around this is to use a projectile that deals x damage of one type and x damage of another type, where an even multiple of x is required to completely deplete the mage's health pool. This is not completely reliable when other enemies are damaging and/or healing the mage.
  - Another way is to use a projectile with x damage of one type and y damage of another, where x and y are both individually less than the mage's max health, but x+y is greater. This is also unreliable when other enemies have hit the mage.
- Accidental kills are another option, as they won't trigger the swapping effect.
- If you do not have such a setup, be sure to fight this enemy in isolation

chunks.title: Thalven Ulmar
chunks.text:
Thalven Ulmar

. Its slow speed and unaggressive behavior should make it easy to pick where you fight.
- Be careful when using spells that linger or home in on enemies, such as the common late-game Homing+Drilling Shot+projectile combination, as this may cause you to swap unexpectedly some distance away; possibly into the middle of a crowd of enemies.
- Avoid using Plasma Beam spells against this enemy, as hitting them with one will swap you directly into the plasma beam.
- If you have the Contact Damage perk, jumping right on top of them (with care taken to avoid their projectiles as one gets close) immediately draws the player an their position to the same place, and completely shuts down their movement and actions generally resulting in a quick kill. Some movement is still possible as a player in this state, only they are truly frozen.

chunks.title: Thalven Ulmar
chunks.text:
Thalven Ulmar

## Trivia

- Being the sole creature in the mage-swapper class, it is the only enemy that will attack itself.

Tavrek Ymreth

Tavrek Ymreth (also know as the Ymreth Marauder) is a red flying robotic enemy found exclusively in the Power Plant.

## Behaviour and Combat

The Ymreth Marauder is invisible by default. It shoots very fast blue bullets to deal moderate, unexpected damage. It is healed by Electricity damage. Although difficult to see, it is not truly invisible when concealed, and can be seen before its attack. Its bolts have a short attack range, so they try to get close to you before firing.

## Combat Tips

- Move away from it. Its short attack range causes it difficulty in constantly attacking.

chunks.title: Naktoi Ernreth
chunks.text:
Naktoi Ernreth

name: Naktoi Ernreth

Naktoi Ernreth (also known as Ernreth Marksman) is a large floating alchemist that can cast destructive spells, depending on the glyph that floats above it.

## Behavior

Ernreth Marksmans can conjure large spectral wands, similar to Intense Concentrated Light, that will cast a powerful spell after a short delay.

The type of spell it casts corresponds to the glowing sigil floating above the alchemist:

- Orange - A single Meteor.
- Purple - A purple Intense Concentrated Light.
- White - Three Pinpoint of Lights that detonate on contact rather than after a short pause.
- Blue - Three Lightning Bolts.

## Trivia

- Its alternate name implies this enemy has succeeded where Kavrik Dureth and Drazen Orghor (whose entity names are failed_alchemist and failed_alchemist_b) could not.
  - Whatever process it has succeeded at may be related to Kessari Ithvax, as the 4 types of attacks Ernreth Marksmans can use are identical to the attacks casted by the Ithvax Trapper's projectile.

chunks.title: Vessin Kesmar
chunks.text:
Vessin Kesmar

name: Vessin Kesmar

Krel Quovaska (or the Quovaska Drifter) is a strange magical enemy in Thalvia. It is only seen in the Silthar Grephis Lair or via the use of Chaotic Polymorphine.

## Behaviour

The Quovaska Drifter shoots projectiles that look very similar to itself which act both as an attack and its main method of moving around, appearing to launch itself at foes. It does not appear to be vulnerable to damage while moving in this fashion, and its moving / attack projectile has an effect similar to Phasing Arc where it appears to teleport short hops along its path rather than moving more conventionally.

chunks.title: Krel Quovaska
chunks.text:
Krel Quovaska

## Combat Tips

- Dispatch it quickly, from a distance, taking care to avoid its attacks and firing only as it is finishing a movement / attack action to ensure attacks make contact.
- Avoid attacking it at close range when possible, as the Ominous Liquid it bleeds stains you with a fairly strong Poison effect.
- While Ominous Liquid can spawn naturally in the Silthar Grephis Lair in small to large pools, it can also often be a sign that Quovaska Drifters are around.
- The darkness in their home biome can make them a very tough enemy to spot before they engage. Teleportation spells are highly recommended for quickly moving to medium or long range to make dodging its attacks easier. Falling down a screen or two can also be an effective way of gaining a lead for kiting, but as always, be very cautious of any potential enemies below.
- If forced into close range without means of escape, focus purely on attacking and dodging. In close quarters, you're very likely to receive a poison stain from their blood, but in most cases this is a less immediate concern than surviving the direct attacks.
- Keep a Water Potion (or other harmless liquid, like Slime or Invisiblium) handy to rinse off any poison stains accumulated from their blood at the first opportunity.

## Trivia

- The Quovaska Drifter is the only enemy which can efficiently fly while Polymorphed, making it a desirable target for Chaotic Polymorphine use.

Vessin Tavkoth (also known as Tavkoth Trapper) is an enemy that is normally only encountered in The Work (Hell). It is made of an unique material known as Purple Crystal, and is able to survive having parts of it destroyed.

## Behavior

It hovers passively until it detects Minä or another enemy nearby. When it does, it will hover near them. If they get too close to the Vessin Tavkoth, it will fire eight purple energy spheres in all directions that do heavy damage. It should be noted that being Invisible does not prevent the Vessin Tavkoth from firing if you move too close, it only prevents the crystal from detecting your presence. More Love perks will similarly not stop them from attacking. This attack happens automatically via a collision trigger, which is a 60x60 box around the enemy looking for anything tagged as prey. It can trigger every 30 frames.

## Combat Tips

- Like other rigid body enemies, it will die instantly when its material body is completely destroyed or erased, even if no damage is dealt to it. This means that, in a pinch, you can one-shot it with the Black Hole spell (best done in close range as to not miss). It does not count as a trick kill but will drop the regular amount of gold, though the gold nuggets are often immediately erased by the black hole.

## Trivia

- Since its body is made up of rigid body material, you can actually grab and kick it away with the Telekinetic Kick perk. (Not normally advised since you will put yourself into its attack range). Kicking it away using the perk will not damage it.

Kessari Ithvax (also known as Ithvax Trapper or Alchemist Boss) is a boss found waiting in the Abandoned Alchemy Lab.

The Ithvax Trapper moves very slowly, but it has several deadly projectile attacks and a field that reflects projectiles back toward their sender. It's important to note that the field is not in any way related mechanically to shields used by some other enemies. Killing the Ithvax Trapper unlocks and drops the extremely valuable Greek Spells, which can be used to copy other spells. It is a powerful enemy for any who braves its domain.

chunks.title: Kessari Ithvax
chunks.text:
Kessari Ithvax

## Behavior

The Ithvax Trapper will remain idle in the center of its arena until you approach, at which point it will become aggressive and the fight will begin. Be wary, as the Ithvax Trapper can see you about a full screen away and may begin attacking before you see it.

The Ithvax Trapper moves by floating around very slowly, pursuing you in a manner similar to Krel Vosphis and the many other floating enemies of the world.

While you are in its sight, the Ithvax Trapper will periodically fire a bouncy, homing orb projectile, which dissipates after a short time. As the orb travels through the air, it will summon three large, ethereal wands that aim at you before firing, telegraphing their attacks similarly to Intense Concentrated Light. There are four different types of ethereal wands the Ithvax Trapper's orbs can summon, and each orb that is shot will only summon one type of wand.

### Dark Wand

A ghastly purple wand that fires a tight cluster of fast, potentially bouncy beams; nearly identical to Intense Concentrated Light. Very deadly in enclosed spaces, especially if all three instances of the wand are angled properly.

Due to its dark, transparent appearance, this attack may be hard to spot when there are many projectiles and/or effects present on the screen.

### Glowing Wand

A shimmering white wand that fires a burst of explosive lasers, similar to Pinpoint of Light. The lasers can cleave through most terrain, and are likely to hit you if you are hiding behind fragile cover.

### Volatile Wand

A fiery orange wand that shoots a Meteor at you. Can set you On Fire, and can instantly kill you on a direct hit unless you have accrued a large amount of HP. The Alchemist is capable of damaging itself with this attack.

### Thunder Wand

chunks.title: Kessari Ithvax
chunks.text:
Kessari Ithvax

### Thunder Wand

A cyan electrical wand that fires a Lightning Bolt at you. Although short-ranged, it can be lethal in closed spaces, leaving you Stunned and vulnerable to deadly follow-ups.

### Projectile Reflecting Field

Alchemist passively generates a special field around itself every 10 seconds or whenever it takes 50 single instance or 75 cumulative damage.

The field lasts for 4 seconds and is actually a projectile, which makes it possible to kill with Explosive Detonator or similar projectile-deleting scripts.

Any projectiles within that field will be deleted with very few exceptions (notably Mist projectiles). An identical but unmodified projectile will be spawned redirected at you, changing ownership, gaining +15 extra Projectile damage and doubling its Explosion damage and becoming damaging to you. Some projectiles don't self-reference and are instead turned into Magic Missile. A few of them simply reference a different projectile, in that case that different projectile is what will be created. For example, Ball Lightning references Lightning Bolt so that's what the field will spawn instead.

The field entity also has a CellEaterComponent which makes it destroy solid matter in a 38px radius. This also displaces liquids making it almost impossible to get hurt by Acid (which is why it's a terrible way of killing it, even if it does take damage from it).

## Fields and self-damage

The Ithvax Trapper raises its field after receiving 50 damage in a single hit or 75 damage across multiple hits. It will also raise its field once every 10 seconds. These checks are done independently and can result in overlapping fields.

On occasion, the Ithvax Trapper may damage itself with its attacks. There are various factors that may contribute to this.

Notably, its own Lightning Bolt can hit it. Additionally, as mentioned above, the Ithvax Trapper periodically creates a projectile-reflecting field. It can reflect its own projectiles, which can hurt it. However, this may not happen in most circumstances. When it creates a field naturally, it also sets its damage multiplier to 0, which causes many attacks to simply bounce off. However, there are caveats to this. This is not caused by fields created by either high damage (50) or accumulated damage (75). Additionally, when any of its fields expire, its damage multiplier is set back, which can cause brief moments of vulnerability with a field active, should their timings appear to overlap.

Lightning Bolts can deal self-damage quite easily during times when its damage multiplier is not 0, which can lead to a field which can then be used to have its other attacks deal self-damage. Kicking the Ithvax Trapper can be useful to reposition it for such cases, as this will cause it to fall down. Moreover, its accumulated damage is only checked when it takes damage, and either damage-based field decreases it by 75. If it has already taken heavy acute damage (for instance, from Lightning), one may be able to predictably trigger this field with a simple kick or weak projectile.

chunks.title: Kessari Ithvax
chunks.text:
Kessari Ithvax

- Be very careful about your position throughout the fight - each time a wand spell is spawned, it will be aimed directly at where you currently are, and then fire after a short delay. Prediction of when, where, and how the wands will fire is key to survival.
- Each summoned orb will summon multiple spectral wand spells, aimed at where you are when that spell is cast. Take care that avoiding the first attack does not leave you in the path of the second attack.
- Unlike a typical Projectile Field, everything that hits the Ithvax Trapper's field will be reflected at you. The Tentacle spell can be very deadly towards you if reflected, but can still be very effective against the Ithvax Trapper when the field is down

chunks.title: Kessari Ithvax
chunks.text:
Kessari Ithvax

. However there is no animation when the field activates so it is advised to only go in for damage shortly after the field is gone, then stop and wait for it to go up again.
- Due to the nature of its field and vulnerabilities, a reliable method of killing the Ithvax Trapper for longer runs is to acquire a wand with Lightning Bolt, Thunder Charge, Explosion of Thunder or Ball Lightning (behind a trigger for safety) midway through a standard run along the Main Path and return to the surface via the shaft from the Snowy Depths up to the Lava Lake; with a teleport wand or the right perks and potions, it should be a simple matter to reach the arena, and from there a few shots will be enough to take down the Alchemist quickly.
- If you have ways to increase your movement and flight speed and/or time such as Hastium or the right combination of Perks, you can fly around the Alchemist in circles and consistently avoid the wands, shooting when its field is down.
- Using Teleport Bolt to move behind the Ithvax Trapper after it throws an orb also guarantees you'll have enough distance from the spawned wands to dodge their spells (or even fully stay out of range for the Lightning wand).
- The Ithvax Trapper will easily erase large amounts of terrain to get to you, if necessary.
- Halvox Nakphis can be lured in from the Ancient Laboratory and can fight the Ithvax Trapper on its own, as Halvox Nakphis are immune to all of its attacks.
- The Ithvax Trapper can hit itself with its own spells, they deal very decent damage in case you don't have a good damage wand but have a travel/teleport wand.
  - The Ithvax Trapper's field blocks all attacks but not you

chunks.title: Kessari Ithvax
chunks.text:
Kessari Ithvax

. So a reliable way to win the fight quickly is to fly inside the field and attack from close range.
- If utilizing Chain Bolt to bypass the Ithvax Trapper's field, be aware that the field still functions as intended -- it will change the ownership of the projectile, but due to Chain Bolt's behavior, it will not reflect and will instead continue on to damage the Alchemist (remember that spells owned by the Alchemist still hurt it, such as Prickly Spore Pod). If this happens, credit for the kill does not go to you, which means it won't unlock in the Progress Menu. To guarantee your kill is recorded, finish off the boss with a high-damage projectile when its field is completely down.
- A small pool of Ambrosia can make the fight much easier, but be wary of the Alchemist's attacks destroying terrain and the Slime bled by it washing off the stain.
- If you managed to kill Rukhel Vosnok earlier in the run, the Saha wand can kill the Alchemist in literal seconds even if it has no spells attached, thanks to its extremely low Cast Delay, Recharge Time and Always Cast Chainsaw and Bloodlust. Just wait for the Ithvax Trapper to throw its first orb, dodge it and its wands, and then jump on it and rip it to shreds. They won't even have time to throw a second orb.
- Piercing Shot on Prickly Spore Pod is an infamous combination that can routinely instantly kill the Alchemist, and with both not being too rare to find, proves to be a pretty foolproof method.
- The mechanics of the damage field also allow one avenue of attack with repeatedly-hitting wands which are normally not suitable

Grevan Rukkoth (also known as Rukkoth Skitterer) is a sphere-shaped creature with multiple eyes found in various biomes.

## Behaviour

Grevan Rukkoth will tend to lazily fly towards you, attempting to bite you once they get close enough. This giant Slime bleeds acid that can quickly dissolve the surrounding terrain. When close to death, it will spawn three Krel Vosphis. On being killed, it will create a small acid explosion that has a fairly high chance of killing its children if they are still too close.

## Combat Tips

- Killing the Mother quickly after it spawns slimes will often cause the explosion to take them out as well.
- Throwing Emerald Tablet at Grevan Rukkoth typically kills in one hit and results in a beautiful pop that kills the slimes along with it.
- Stay above or away from it when fighting it, to avoid having acid rain down on you.
- The Mother is slow-moving and only has a melee attack, so it's of little threat until you attack it. If you don't have the damage output to take care of it and its children quickly, avoiding it altogether is often the best option.
- Because it explodes into acid on death, collecting its gold can be dangerous. Collect it without touching the ground, or don't collect it at all, to avoid the risk of stepping in an acid puddle - gold is much less valuable than health in the early areas, and in the later areas the 50 it drops is worth very little anyway.
